events.text: The siege of your mountain enters its second month. {sw_foe} always seem to know which gate is weakest, and which night the patrols change. Then the kitchen reports that old Cook Bai has started steaming exactly the right number of buns for the night watch, before anyone has told the kitchen how many will stand it.

choices.text: Pretend to know nothing and lead the dawn sortie as planned

effects.log: You ride out on schedule. Behind you, someone in the kitchen counts the riders.

choices.text: Change every patrol at the last moment and strike their camp instead

effects.log: The patrols change at midnight, unannounced. For once the enemy is the one surprised.

choices.text: Go out alone to challenge {sw_leader} before the leak can matter

ok.log: You win in front of both camps. Whatever the spy tells them now, they saw that.

fail.log: You lose, and are carried back up the mountain. In the kitchen, someone is very calm.
fail.deathCause: a duel with the leader of an enemy sect, in a sect war

choices.text: Send an envoy: a war fought blind is a war already lost

effects.log: An envoy goes down the mountain. You keep your eyes on the kitchen.

events.text: You watch the kitchen for a month. Cook Bai rises an hour before everyone, ties a red thread to the third plum tree by the wall, and goes back to the dough. The thread is gone by noon. Bai has fed this sect for thirty years, and taught half your disciples to fold dumplings.

choices.text: Have the thread replaced with one of your own choosing

effects.log: The next morning a red thread tells the enemy the east gate is unguarded. That night the east gate is very well guarded.

choices.text: Confront Bai in the kitchen, alone

effects.log: Bai puts down the rolling pin and sits. "They have my grandson," the old cook says. "In their mountain. He is nine."

choices.text: Have Bai seized in front of the whole sect

effects.log: Bai is led from the kitchen with flour to the elbows. The disciples watch in silence, and nobody eats well that week.

events.text: The war is over, but the kitchen is not. Cook Bai still rises an hour early, still looks at the third plum tree, and no longer ties anything to it. The grandson is the question nobody on the mountain will ask aloud.

choices.text: Send your best scout to bring the boy home

effects.log: Nine days later a thin boy walks up the mountain holding a scout's hand. Bai drops a whole tray of buns and does not pick them up.

choices.text: Trade a captured enemy disciple for the boy

ok.log: The exchange is made on a bridge at dawn. The boy runs; the enemy disciple walks.

fail.log: Their envoy laughs at the offer. Bai hears of it and says nothing for a week.

choices.text: Retire Bai to a farm in the valley, with a pension

effects.log: Bai goes without a word. The new cook burns the rice for a month, and the whole mountain blames you for it.

events.text: {sw_foe} hold the island pavilion in the middle of Mirror Lake, and this morning the fog is so thick you cannot see the bow of your own boat. Forty disciples sit in twelve fishing boats, oars wrapped in cloth. Somewhere ahead a heron complains, and the whole fleet freezes.

choices.text: Row straight for the pavilion and trust the fog to hide you

effects.log: Twelve boats slide out of the white all at once, and the pavilion's sentries drop their tea.

choices.text: Split the boats and land behind the island, in the reeds

effects.log: You come ashore through the reeds, wet to the knees, behind a camp that is facing the wrong way.

choices.text: Call across the water for {sw_leader} to meet you on the jetty

ok.log: You win on the slick planks of the jetty. Their disciples hear it through the fog before they see it.

fail.log: You go into the lake, and are fished out by your own people with a boathook.
fail.deathCause: a duel with the leader of an enemy sect, in a sect war

choices.text: Ring the boat bell three times: the old sign for parley

effects.log: Three notes cross the fog. After a long silence, three notes come back.

events.text: When the fog lifts, two of your boats are missing. One comes home at noon with a broken oar. The other belonged to Fisherman Lao, who lent it for the battle, and it is found upturned among the lotus with nobody in it. Two disciples were aboard.

choices.text: Search the lake yourself, until dark

effects.log: You search until the stars are out. At the last light you find the two of them on a mudbank, cold and furious and alive.

choices.text: Hold a lamp-boat memorial on the water

effects.log: Two paper lamps drift out over Mirror Lake. The whole sect stands on the shore until they go out.

choices.text: Pay Lao for the boat and stop looking (60 taels)

effects.log: Lao takes the silver and keeps looking alone, every morning, for a month.

events.text: Fisherman Lao comes up the mountain in winter with a basket of dried fish and a question: does the sect still owe a boat? Lao has never asked anyone for anything, and is visibly hating every moment of this.

choices.text: Have the sect's carpenters build Lao a new boat

effects.log: The new boat is better than the old one. Lao names it after the two disciples, which embarrasses them very much.

choices.text: Give Lao a place teaching your disciples to read the water

effects.log: Lao teaches knots and currents to grinning disciples. Your next lake battle, if it ever comes, will be a different story.

choices.text: Pay for a boat, with interest (120 taels)

effects.log: Lao counts the silver twice, bows once and goes back to the lake.

events.text: Lao's new boat goes out on Mirror Lake every dawn, and the sect's disciples now race it in summer, badly. This year the two who were lost in the fog ask to row in the race themselves, in Lao's boat, against the whole sect.

choices.text: Row against them

effects.log: You lose by three lengths, splashing. Lao laughs so hard the boat nearly tips.

choices.text: Ring the boat bell to start the race

effects.log: Three notes cross the lake, the old sign of parley, now the sign of a race. Everyone cheers.

choices.text: Watch from the shore with Lao's dried fish

effects.log: You sit on the jetty eating fish. It is the best morning of the year.

events.text: Scouts report that {sw_foe} mean to cross the Yellow Reed river on the night ferry, a flat old raft hauled on a rope by Ferryman Tong. Tong has carried your disciples to market for twenty years for two coppers each. Tonight Tong is carrying the enemy, at sword point.
events.arc: The Last Ferry of the Night

choices.text: Meet them on the bank as the raft grounds

effects.log: You are waiting on the mud when the raft touches. It is a short, wet, ugly fight.

choices.text: Slacken the ferry rope from your side and let the current take them

effects.log: The raft spins off downstream with forty swordsmen clinging to it, and Tong clinging to the rope.

choices.text: Wade out and challenge {sw_leader} on the raft itself

ok.log: You win on a deck that rocks with every step. Tong poles calmly through the whole thing.

fail.log: You lose, and swim home in the dark, carrying your boots in your teeth.
fail.deathCause: a duel with the leader of an enemy sect, in a sect war

choices.text: Have Tong carry a letter across before the fighting starts

effects.log: Tong poles across with your letter tucked in a hat, grumbling that this is not the usual cargo.

events.text: Tong's raft is wrecked on a sandbar three miles down the river, and Tong is sitting on the bank beside it, wet, unhurt and extremely angry. "Twenty years," the ferryman says, "and not one of you ever asked me which side I was on."
events.arc: The Last Ferry of the Night

choices.text: Ask now

effects.log: "The side with the raft," says Tong. Then, more quietly: "Yours, you fools. I slowed the haul to give you time."

choices.text: Promise Tong a new raft

effects.log: Tong snorts. "Promise. Sects always promise." But the ferryman takes your hand.

choices.text: Leave Tong to it: the war is not over

effects.log: You ride back to the line. Behind you Tong is already counting planks.

events.text: Spring. The river runs high and there is still no ferry, so the whole valley walks two days round by the stone bridge. Market women curse the sects, the war and you specifically. Tong is living in a hut on the bank, mending nets.
events.arc: The Last Ferry of the Night

choices.text: Build Tong a new ferry with the sect's timber (150 taels)

effects.log: The new raft is broad and sound, with a little roof. Tong charges your disciples two coppers each, same as always.

choices.text: Give Tong a sect token: no fare for us, protection for you

effects.log: Tong hangs the token on the ferry post. Nobody in the valley robs that ferry again.

choices.text: Tell the valley the sect owes nobody a ferry

effects.log: The market women stop selling your kitchen eggs. It is a very long spring.

events.text: {sw_foe} are camped in the Thousand Pole bamboo grove, and one of your elders has a simple plan: the wind is from the east, the bamboo is dry, and fire does not need training. The grove belongs to the paper village of Little Ma, whose people make every sheet your sect writes on.

choices.text: No fire. Go in on foot, through the bamboo, at dawn

effects.log: You fight them pole by pole through the grove. Nothing burns but tempers.

choices.text: Light the eastern edge and wait for them on the far side

effects.log: The grove goes up with a roar like a waterfall. The enemy comes out coughing, straight into your line.

choices.text: Walk into the grove alone and call for {sw_leader}

ok.log: You win in a clearing among the green stems. The grove is spared, and you are a story.

fail.log: You lose among the bamboo and limp out, cut in a dozen small places by leaves and pride.
fail.deathCause: a duel with the leader of an enemy sect, in a sect war

choices.text: Send an envoy: no one wants to fight in a tinderbox

effects.log: Both sides agree, at least, that nobody will light anything.

events.text: Some of the Thousand Pole grove has burned, whether by your elders' torches or by an enemy cookfire kicked over in the fighting. Black stumps stand in rows like ink strokes. The paper-makers of Little Ma come up to look at it and say nothing at all, which is worse than shouting.

choices.text: Apologise to the village elders in person

effects.log: You bow in the ashes. Old Ma, the head paper-maker, looks at you for a long time and nods once.

choices.text: Send disciples to help clear the ash

effects.log: Your disciples haul burnt poles for a month. They come back black to the eyebrows and much humbler.

choices.text: Point out that the enemy was in the grove first

effects.log: Old Ma says the bamboo does not care whose fault it is.

events.text: Bamboo grows back faster than anything, if someone plants it. The village has no young people left to plant; they went to the city. Old Ma comes up the mountain with a basket of shoots and a look that says a sect with two hundred idle disciples has no excuse.

choices.text: Plant the grove with the whole sect for three days

effects.log: Two hundred disciples plant bamboo in the rain. In five years the grove is taller than before, and Little Ma sends you paper free.

choices.text: Pay the village to hire planters (100 taels)

effects.log: Hired hands plant the grove. It grows. The paper still comes, at full price.

choices.text: Use a wood-qi technique to quicken the shoots

ok.log: The shoots stand a hand taller by morning. Old Ma calls it witchcraft and is delighted.

fail.log: Nothing grows except your headache. Old Ma pats your shoulder and hands you a spade.

events.text: There is only one way up the mountain to {sect}: nine hundred stone steps, each one wide enough for two people. {sw_foe} are at the bottom of them now, in their hundreds. Your disciples have carried up baskets of stones and are arguing about which step is the best one to die on.

choices.text: Charge down the stair while they are still climbing

effects.log: You come down the steps like a landslide. The front of their column folds.

choices.text: Let them climb tired, then hit them from the pines at step six hundred

effects.log: At step six hundred the pines are full of your people. Climbers make poor fighters.

choices.text: Stand on the middle step and challenge {sw_leader} to come up alone

ok.log: You win on the four hundred and fiftieth step, and they never climb past it.

fail.log: You lose, and are carried up the rest of the stair by two disciples, which is its own kind of shame.
fail.deathCause: a duel with the leader of an enemy sect, in a sect war

choices.text: Walk down the nine hundred steps unarmed to talk

effects.log: Your knees hate every step. At the bottom, the enemy listens, if only out of surprise.

events.text: The fighting on the stair is over. Disciple Yan Xiaoshi, seventeen, held step six hundred and twelve alone for most of an hour, and did not come back up. The sect's gatekeeper asks quietly whether the step should be marked.

choices.text: Carve Yan's name on the step

effects.log: The carver takes three days. Every disciple who climbs the stair now steps around it.

choices.text: Visit Yan's family in the village below

effects.log: Yan's grandmother serves you tea and asks if Yan was brave. You tell the truth, which is yes.

choices.text: Leave the stair as it is: every step held

effects.log: The gatekeeper bows and goes. The stair keeps its silence, and so do you.

events.text: A year on, a little boy from the village climbs the nine hundred steps alone and asks to join the sect. He is Yan Xiaoshi's cousin, eight years old, and has brought his own lunch. The gate disciples do not know whether to laugh or cry.

choices.text: Take him in when he is old enough, and say so

effects.log: He goes home with a sect token and a full belly. Every new year he climbs the stair to check you remember.

choices.text: Walk him down to step six hundred and twelve first

effects.log: He reads the name aloud, very slowly, then sits on the step and eats his lunch next to it.

choices.text: Send him home: the sect is no place for a child

effects.log: He goes down the steps crying. The gatekeeper does not speak to you for a week.

events.text: The only way to {sw_foe} is a rope bridge over the Gorge of Swallows, three hundred feet of fraying hemp and old planks. Their camp is on the far side. Your disciples look at the bridge, then at each other, then very hard at you.

choices.text: Cross it fast, ten at a time

effects.log: The bridge sways like a drunk. Your first ten make it, and the rest follow faster than they ever have.

choices.text: Climb down into the gorge and up the other cliff by night

effects.log: A night climb, no lanterns. By dawn your people come over the far edge behind their pickets.

choices.text: Walk out to the middle and call {sw_leader} to meet you there

ok.log: You win on a bridge that swings with every blow. Swallows scatter, and both armies breathe again.

fail.log: You lose, and hang from a rope for a long moment before your disciples haul you in.
fail.deathCause: a duel with the leader of an enemy sect, in a sect war

choices.text: Shout terms across the gorge: neither side wants to fight on this bridge

effects.log: The wind carries your words away twice. The third time, they shout back.

events.text: After the battle, a dozen enemy disciples are trapped on the far side with the bridge damaged behind them, no food and winter coming. Your own elder suggests cutting the last ropes. "Then the gorge does the work," the elder says, "and our hands stay clean."

choices.text: Repair the bridge and let them walk home

effects.log: They cross one at a time, very carefully, staring at you. Nobody says thank you, and nobody needs to.

choices.text: Send food across on a rope basket, and wait

effects.log: Rice crosses the gorge in a basket. In three days they send the basket back with a note: we yield.

choices.text: Cut the ropes

effects.log: The bridge falls into the gorge with a long whisper. Your elder looks pleased, and you do not sleep well.

events.text: A traveling merchant brings a gift up your mountain: a coil of new hemp rope, the finest you have ever seen, and a message with no name on it. "For the next bridge. From the twelve."

choices.text: Rebuild the Gorge of Swallows bridge with it

effects.log: The new bridge is the best in the province. Merchants start using it, and your sect collects a small, cheerful toll.

choices.text: Keep the rope in the sect hall as a reminder

effects.log: The coil hangs in the hall. New disciples ask about it, and you tell them.

choices.text: Send the rope back: you want no debts with the enemy

effects.log: The merchant carries it away again, shaking their head.

events.text: {sw_foe} came over the Ox Head pass in late autumn to strike your mountain from behind. Then the snow came, four days of it, and now both armies are sealed in the same narrow valley with one woodcutter's hut, three goats and a great deal of mutual dislike.

choices.text: Attack through the drifts before they dig in

effects.log: You flounder at them waist-deep in snow. They flounder back. It is very slow and very cold.

choices.text: Drop the snow cornice on their camp from the ridge

effects.log: The cornice comes down with a soft roar, burying their tents to the ridgepoles. Nobody dies, but the war goes out of them.

choices.text: Challenge {sw_leader} to settle it on the frozen stream

ok.log: You win on the ice, slipping and steaming. Both camps cheer, mostly because it is something to watch.

fail.log: You lose, and the ice breaks under you at the end. Your own people pull you out blue.
fail.deathCause: a duel with the leader of an enemy sect, in a sect war

choices.text: Propose a truce until the thaw: nobody can fight in this

effects.log: Both camps agree. The goats, which belong to neither side, are claimed by both.

events.text: The pass stays sealed for six weeks. The enemy camp has run out of rice; your scouts can hear their coughing from the ridge. Your own stores are thin, but there is enough for your people, and a little more. The woodcutter's three goats look at you with deep suspicion.

choices.text: Send them half a sack of rice under a white flag

effects.log: The rice goes across the snow on a sledge. The next morning the sledge comes back with a jar of their pickles, frozen solid.

choices.text: Do nothing and let the winter decide

effects.log: You wait. The coughing over the ridge grows quieter, then stops being a question you let yourself ask.

choices.text: Buy the goats from the woodcutter for both camps (30 taels)

effects.log: Three goats, six weeks, two armies. The woodcutter becomes rich and the goats famous.

events.text: At the thaw, the enemy marches home through the pass instead of over your mountain. Their captain stops at your camp, bows stiffly, and leaves a sword in the snow by your tent: an old one, with a jade pommel. The woodcutter says it is worth more than the hut.

choices.text: Hang it in the sect hall: the Winter Sword

effects.log: The Winter Sword hangs over the hall door. Your disciples tell the story wrong, and better, every year.

choices.text: Give it to the woodcutter for the hut and the goats

effects.log: The woodcutter sells it in the city and builds a teahouse at the foot of the pass called The Three Goats.

choices.text: Sell it for the sect's treasury

effects.log: A collector in the city pays well. Your treasurer is happy. The story ends there.

events.text: The Three Goats teahouse at the foot of Ox Head pass has become famous. Travellers come to hear the story of two sects snowed in together. The woodcutter, now very fat and very prosperous, sends word that the enemy's old captain is staying there tonight, and asks if you would like the corner table.

choices.text: Go, and share a pot of tea with the captain

effects.log: You sit up over tea until midnight, two old enemies arguing about whose pickles were worse. The goats are honoured guests.

choices.text: Send a jar of rice wine to the captain's table

effects.log: The captain raises the jar toward your mountain. The whole teahouse drinks to it.

choices.text: Stay home: some stories are better from a distance

effects.log: You stay home. The woodcutter tells the story without you, and improves it.

events.text: Willow Market sits on the road between your mountain and {sw_foe}, and their vanguard has taken the town's inn for a headquarters. Merchants are boarding up their stalls. A noodle seller in a straw hat is still cooking, loudly, in the middle of the square, as if daring both sects to knock the pot over.

choices.text: Take the inn by storm before they fortify it

effects.log: You go through the front door, the back door and two windows at once. The inn is yours by noon.

choices.text: Wait until they come out for noodles, then close the square

effects.log: They come out for noodles. They do not get them.

choices.text: Challenge {sw_leader} to fight in the square, away from the stalls

ok.log: You win on the cobbles, under every shuttered window. The noodle seller never stops cooking.

fail.log: You lose, and are knocked flat across a cabbage stall. The cabbage seller sends your sect a bill.
fail.deathCause: a duel with the leader of an enemy sect, in a sect war

choices.text: Invite them to talk at the noodle stall, neutral ground

effects.log: Both leaders sit on low stools and eat noodles while talking terms. The noodle seller charges double.

events.text: The fighting has left Willow Market with a burnt-out inn, three smashed stalls and a town council that has drawn up a list. It is a long list. At the top it says, in careful clerk's hand: "Who pays?"

choices.text: Pay the town in full (180 taels)

effects.log: The council reads your silver twice and puts the list away. Willow Market speaks well of your sect for a generation.

choices.text: Pay half and send disciples to rebuild the rest

effects.log: Your disciples learn carpentry from angry shopkeepers. The inn's new roof leaks only slightly.

choices.text: Tell the council to bill the enemy

effects.log: The council sends the bill to both sects. Neither pays. The town remembers.

events.text: A year later the noodle seller from the square opens a proper shop in the rebuilt inn, and sends up an invitation to the opening. The sign over the door says "Between Two Sects". There is a special on the menu named after you.

choices.text: Go, and eat the special

effects.log: The special is extremely spicy, which the noodle seller swears is a compliment.

choices.text: Bring the disciples who rebuilt the inn

effects.log: Your disciples sit under the roof they patched, very proud of the leak. The noodle seller feeds them free.

choices.text: Send a gift but stay away

effects.log: A scroll of good wishes hangs by the door. The town is a little disappointed.

events.text: {sw_foe} have come to your gate with an old proposal: let each side choose three champions, and let the champions decide the war. It would spare hundreds. Your three best fighters stand in the courtyard, and the youngest, Disciple Hou Ming, is so nervous he is polishing a sword that is already clean.

choices.text: Refuse the champions and fall on their camp

effects.log: Your whole sect comes over the wall at once, and the champions' duel never happens.

choices.text: Accept, but hide archers on the slope in case of tricks

effects.log: Their tricks come, as you thought, and your archers answer them.

choices.text: Name yourself the first champion and face {sw_leader}

ok.log: You win the first bout so cleanly that the other two are never fought. Hou Ming is visibly relieved.

fail.log: You lose the first bout. Hou Ming has to fight the second after all.
fail.deathCause: a duel with the leader of an enemy sect, in a sect war

choices.text: Propose that the champions fight with wooden swords

effects.log: The enemy laughs, then thinks about it, then agrees. Nobody dies today.

events.text: In the fighting, Hou Ming took a blow to the knee that the physician says will never fully heal. He will walk, slowly. He will not fight again. He sits by the training yard every day watching the others, and smiles too much.

choices.text: Make Hou Ming the keeper of the sect's records

effects.log: Hou Ming takes to the archive like a fish to water, and finds three mistakes in your accounts on the first day.

choices.text: Teach Hou Ming a seated breathing art

effects.log: Hou Ming's qi grows quiet and deep. He says it is like learning to swim in a well.

choices.text: Send Hou Ming home with a pension (60 taels)

effects.log: Hou Ming goes home to a farm. His letters stop after the second year.

events.text: Hou Ming, keeper of the records, comes to you with a ledger open in both hands. "Somebody has been paying the enemy for word of our champions," he says. "The silver came from our own kitchen fund. For three years."

choices.text: Follow the silver to its end

effects.log: It leads to a steward who has gambled away a fortune. The steward goes, and Hou Ming walks taller.

choices.text: Let Hou Ming lead the inquiry himself

effects.log: Hou Ming questions the stewards from a chair, slowly and without mercy. He is very good at it.

choices.text: Close the ledger: the war is over

effects.log: Hou Ming closes the book. He does not open the subject again, and does not quite forgive it.

events.text: {sw_foe} are famous for one thing: hidden weapons. Plum-blossom needles, iron lotus seeds, sleeve arrows. Your scouts say their whole camp throws at once, a rain you cannot see. Your armourer has stayed up all night making shields of lacquered rattan and is very proud of them.

choices.text: Advance behind the rattan shields, in one tight block

effects.log: The needles patter on the rattan like hail. Your armourer weeps with joy.

choices.text: Attack at night: you cannot aim what you cannot see

effects.log: In the dark, their hidden weapons are just hidden. Your people close before the rain can fall.

choices.text: Challenge {sw_leader} to a duel with no hidden weapons

ok.log: You win. Afterwards they shake out their sleeves, and a whole handful of needles falls out.

fail.log: You lose, and the physician picks needles out of your sleeves for an hour.
fail.deathCause: a duel with the leader of an enemy sect, in a sect war

choices.text: Send a parley flag, with a rattan shield as a gift

effects.log: Their leader studies the shield and laughs aloud. Talks begin.

events.text: After the battle the field glitters. Thousands of needles and iron seeds lie in the grass, and the farmers who own it will be finding them in their feet for a decade. A blind disciple of yours, Sightless Wen, offers to find them all, by sound.

choices.text: Let Wen try, with a dozen helpers

effects.log: Wen walks the field ringing a small bell and listening. In a week, eleven jars of needles. The farmers bow to Wen like a god.

choices.text: Hire the farmers' children to collect them, a copper a needle (40 taels)

effects.log: The children become rich and very careful. The field is clean by autumn.

choices.text: Leave the field: it is the farmers' problem

effects.log: A plough horse goes lame in spring. The farmers stop greeting your disciples.

events.text: Sightless Wen has melted down the eleven jars of enemy needles in the sect forge and made a single bell from the iron. "It is ugly," Wen says, "but it rings true." Wen wants to hang it somewhere.

choices.text: Hang it at the sect gate

effects.log: Every visitor rings the needle bell. It sounds a little sour, and everyone loves it.

choices.text: Ask Wen to teach the disciples to fight by sound

effects.log: Your disciples train blindfolded for a season. Afterwards nobody can surprise them in the dark.

choices.text: Send it to the enemy as a peace gift

effects.log: The bell comes back a month later with a note: "We have enough needles." It is almost a joke.

events.text: Rain for nine days, and {sw_foe} are camped above the old earth dam at Stone Weir, with sappers. If the dam breaks, your lower terraces, the valley village, and the road all go under the water. Your disciples stand in the rain waiting for your word.

choices.text: Storm the dam before their sappers finish

effects.log: You take the dam in the rain, sliding in mud, and drive the sappers off it.

choices.text: Cut round through the gully and fall on their sappers' camp

effects.log: The gully is a river, but your people get through it, and the sappers' camp is very surprised.

choices.text: Climb the dam and call {sw_leader} to fight on top of it

ok.log: You win on top of the dam, with the water roaring on one side and the valley on the other.

fail.log: You lose, and fall down the dry face of the dam into the mud. You are lucky it is the dry face.
fail.deathCause: a duel with the leader of an enemy sect, in a sect war

choices.text: Offer a truce until the rain stops, to spare the valley

effects.log: Even the enemy has families downstream. The truce holds for nine days.

events.text: The dam broke anyway, on the tenth night, whether from the sappers or the rain. The valley village is under four feet of brown water. Families are on their roofs with chickens and grandmothers, and there are not enough boats.

choices.text: Turn the whole sect into boatmen for a week

effects.log: Your disciples pole doors and tubs through the flood, pulling people off roofs. Nobody in the valley drowns.

choices.text: Open the sect's storehouse to the village (100 taels)

effects.log: Two hundred villagers sleep in your training halls, and eat your rice for a month.

choices.text: Protect the sect's own terraces first

effects.log: Your terraces are saved. The village saves itself, mostly, and remembers who was busy.

events.text: When the water goes down, the valley elders come up the mountain carrying a long red banner with four characters stitched on it: "Mountain Above the Flood". They want to hang it at your gate, and they want to know who will rebuild the dam, properly this time.

choices.text: Hang the banner and pay for a stone dam (200 taels)

effects.log: The new dam is stone, not earth. Your name is cut into it, and the valley's harvests double.

choices.text: Design the new dam yourself

ok.log: Your dam holds through three floods. Engineers come from the capital to study it.

fail.log: Your dam has a small leak. The village calls it the Elder's Tear and is fond of it.

choices.text: Accept the banner and leave the dam to the magistrate

effects.log: The banner hangs at your gate. The magistrate's dam is not built for five years.

events.text: Ten years on, a great flood comes again, worse than before. The new dam holds. Below it, the valley village looks up at the wall of brown water and does not run. The village children have been taught, in their song about the dam, to say your name.

choices.text: Walk the dam in the storm with the villagers

effects.log: You stand on the dam in the rain with a hundred villagers. It does not move. Nobody leaves until dawn.

choices.text: Send the sect's disciples to watch the old breach point

effects.log: Your disciples sit on the dam all night. Nothing happens, which is the best thing that can happen.

choices.text: Stay on the mountain and trust the stone

effects.log: You sleep. In the morning the valley is dry, and someone has hung a new red banner on your gate.

events.text: {sw_foe} have dug in at the ruins of Cloud Gate Temple, a broken hall on a hill where one old monk still lives alone and rings the bell at dawn. Your scouts say the monk has refused to leave. "The bell must be rung," was the whole reply.
events.arc: The Monk Who Rang the Bell

choices.text: Take the hill at a run, before dawn

effects.log: You are on the hill before the monk rises. The bell rings anyway, in the middle of the fighting.

choices.text: Wait for the bell, when their watch changes, and strike then

effects.log: The bell rings, their watch changes, and your people come up the back of the hill.

choices.text: Challenge {sw_leader} to fight in the temple yard, under the bell

ok.log: You win under the bell. The monk sweeps around the two of you the whole time, unbothered.

fail.log: You lose, and the monk bandages you afterwards, then rings the bell as usual.
fail.deathCause: a duel with the leader of an enemy sect, in a sect war

choices.text: Ask the monk to carry your terms to them

effects.log: The old monk carries your letter in a sleeve and comes back with an answer and some radishes.

events.text: When the fighting is over, Cloud Gate Temple is more broken than before. A beam has fallen across the bell frame, and the bell lies cracked in the dust. The old monk, Abbot Kong, sits beside it and does not speak.
events.arc: The Monk Who Rang the Bell

choices.text: Have your disciples raise the beam and rehang the bell

effects.log: The cracked bell goes back up. It rings flat now, and Abbot Kong bows to you for the first time.

choices.text: Sit with Kong, and say nothing either

effects.log: You sit together all afternoon. At sunset Kong says, "Thank you," and goes to cook supper.

choices.text: Leave the abbot a purse of silver (50 taels)

effects.log: Kong does not look at the purse. In the morning it is on your saddle again.

events.text: Two years after the battle, a letter from Abbot Kong, in a hand like leaves blown by wind: the cracked bell has been heard as far as the enemy's mountain, and their disciples have started climbing the hill to listen. Kong would like both sects to come, the same morning.
events.arc: The Monk Who Rang the Bell

choices.text: Go, and stand beside them while the bell rings

effects.log: Two sects stand in the temple yard in silence. Nobody fights. Kong rings the flat bell and smiles.

choices.text: Send a gift of new temple roof tiles (80 taels)

effects.log: The temple gets a roof. Kong writes back a single line: "The rain thanks you."

choices.text: Decline: some wounds should stay closed

effects.log: Kong does not write again. The bell still rings at dawn.

events.text: {sw_foe} have closed the salt road, the only way your sect's kitchens get salt, pickles and soy. The cooks are rationing. A salt caravan is trying to get through to you anyway, led by old Merchant Fu on a mule that bites everyone, including Fu.

choices.text: Ride down the road and clear it by force

effects.log: You clear the road in a running fight from tree to tree. Fu's mule bites two of the enemy.

choices.text: Hide in the caravan's salt carts and spring out at the checkpoint

effects.log: They lift the cart covers to tax the salt and find your disciples instead.

choices.text: Meet {sw_leader} at the road checkpoint, alone

ok.log: You win at the checkpoint. The caravan rolls through with Fu waving like a magistrate.

fail.log: You lose. The caravan is turned back, and the cooks cry into unsalted soup.
fail.deathCause: a duel with the leader of an enemy sect, in a sect war

choices.text: Offer them a share of the salt in exchange for passage

effects.log: A salt tax of one cart in ten. The cooks complain, but they have salt.

events.text: Merchant Fu arrives at last with two carts out of five. The others were taken or overturned in the fighting. Fu's mule is fine. Fu is not fine, and sits in your kitchen yard counting the loss on an abacus with shaking fingers.

choices.text: Pay Fu for the lost carts (150 taels)

effects.log: Fu stops counting, stares at you, then starts counting your silver instead, smiling.

choices.text: Give Fu a sect escort on the road from now on

effects.log: Fu travels with two of your disciples ever after, and the salt road is the safest in the province.

choices.text: Thank Fu, but the loss is a merchant's risk

effects.log: Fu nods slowly, packs the abacus, and does not come back with salt again.

events.text: Merchant Fu has died in the winter, quietly, in a bed in town. Fu's heir, a sharp young woman named Fu Lan, rides up the salt road with the mule and a ledger. "My aunt said you were the only honest buyer on the mountain," she says. "Let us see."

choices.text: Honour Fu's old prices for Fu Lan

effects.log: Fu Lan narrows her eyes, then writes your sect into the ledger in red ink: preferred.

choices.text: Haggle hard with Fu Lan, for the sect's treasury

ok.log: You agree a fair price, and Fu Lan respects you for fighting. The mule bites you anyway.

fail.log: Fu Lan out-haggles you completely, and leaves laughing.

choices.text: Go with her to burn incense for old Fu

effects.log: You stand at Fu's grave with the mule. Even the mule is quiet.

events.text: The Murim Alliance has asked your righteous sect to drive {sw_foe} out of the Pear Blossom valley. It is the third month and every tree is white. Old Farmer Xu, who owns the orchard, stands at the gate with a hoe and a face that says the blossoms will be the casualties.

choices.text: Charge through the orchard in line

effects.log: Your line goes through the rows, and blossom falls like snow. Xu shouts the whole time.

choices.text: Go round the orchard by the irrigation ditches

effects.log: You come up the ditches, muddy to the waist, without breaking a branch. Xu is very nearly grateful.

choices.text: Call {sw_leader} out into the open field beyond the trees

ok.log: You win in the field, with the orchard watching. Not a single tree is touched.

fail.log: You lose, and land in the irrigation ditch. Xu laughs until coughing.
fail.deathCause: a duel with the leader of an enemy sect, in a sect war

choices.text: Ask the Alliance envoy to talk before blossom falls

effects.log: The envoy grumbles, but the talks happen under a tree in full bloom.

events.text: The Alliance envoy is pleased with you, and wants to report a great righteous victory. But in Farmer Xu's orchard, twenty trees are broken, and this year's pears will be thin. The envoy suggests that the farmer should be honoured to have helped the cause.

choices.text: Ask the Alliance to pay Farmer Xu

effects.log: The envoy coughs and pays, with a face like a sour pear. Xu bows to you, not to the envoy.

choices.text: Pay Xu yourself (70 taels)

effects.log: You pay quietly. Xu tells everyone anyway.

choices.text: Agree with the envoy: the cause is honour enough

effects.log: The Alliance praises you in its letters. Xu spits when your disciples pass.

events.text: Autumn. A cart arrives at your mountain gate loaded with pears from Xu's orchard, the good ones, the sweet golden kind. On top is a note: "From the trees that lived."

choices.text: Share them with the whole sect

effects.log: Every disciple gets one pear. It is the best thing anyone has eaten all year.

choices.text: Send half to the Alliance envoy, with no message

effects.log: The envoy receives a box of pears and no explanation. It is talked about for weeks.

choices.text: Eat one yourself and send the rest to the infirmary

effects.log: The wounded eat pears and argue about whose tree was best.

events.text: {sw_foe} come at your walls with drums of their own, deep ones, booming at night to rob your people of sleep. Your sect's only drummer is Disciple Qiu, sixteen, who has never played for anything bigger than a festival, and whose hands are shaking.

choices.text: Let Qiu drum the charge and go out to meet them

effects.log: Qiu drums like thunder. Your gate opens, and your people pour through it.

choices.text: Have Qiu keep drumming on the wall while you slip out the side gate

effects.log: They listen to the drum and watch the wall. You come at them from the side.

choices.text: Challenge {sw_leader}, with Qiu beating the time

ok.log: You win to the beat of Qiu's drum. Qiu plays the victory roll and then sits down, shaking.

fail.log: You lose, and Qiu keeps drumming anyway, to cover the retreat.
fail.deathCause: a duel with the leader of an enemy sect, in a sect war

choices.text: Have Qiu beat the three slow strokes of parley

effects.log: Three slow strokes. Their drums stop. In the silence, envoys go out.

events.text: Qiu has drummed for three nights without stopping, and both palms are blistered raw. The physician wraps them. Qiu does not want to stop. "If I stop," Qiu says, "they will think we are afraid."

choices.text: Take the drumsticks yourself for a night

effects.log: You drum until dawn, badly, and the sect laughs on the wall for the first time in weeks.

choices.text: Order Qiu to rest, and teach two others

effects.log: Three drummers now, in shifts. The enemy drums stop first.

choices.text: Let Qiu go on drumming

effects.log: Qiu drums for a fourth night, then faints over the drum. The sound of that is worse than any silence.

events.text: The war is long over. Qiu has made a new drum for the sect from an old wine barrel and an ox hide, and wants to teach the whole sect a war-drum pattern, "so we are never silent again." Qiu asks if you remember the rhythm you played that night.

choices.text: Admit you never knew any rhythm at all

effects.log: Qiu laughs until crying, and names the pattern after you anyway: the Elder's Mess.

choices.text: Make Qiu the sect's master of drums

effects.log: Qiu bows deeply. Every festival on the mountain now starts with that drum.

choices.text: Learn the drum properly, from Qiu

effects.log: You learn to drum. It does something good to your qi, oddly.

events.text: The orthodox sects call {sect} demons, and {sw_foe} believe it: they have gone home for the Mid-Autumn festival and left only a token guard. Your disciples in their black robes are waiting for the full moon. One of them is eating a mooncake, crumbs everywhere, very calmly.

choices.text: Strike while they are celebrating

effects.log: You come down on them under the full moon. Lanterns go out one by one.

choices.text: Wait at the road for those coming back from the festival

effects.log: They come back cheerful and full of mooncakes, and walk straight into your black robes.

choices.text: Walk into their festival and challenge {sw_leader} by name

ok.log: You win in front of their lanterns. Your sect's name will be whispered in their children's stories now.

fail.log: You lose in front of their festival crowd, and the orthodox will tell this story for years.
fail.deathCause: a duel with the leader of an enemy sect, in a sect war

choices.text: Send a mooncake with a letter inside: let both sides keep the festival

effects.log: They open the mooncake and find terms. Even demons, it seems, keep the moon.

events.text: In the dark, after the fighting, your disciples found a village family hiding in the enemy's barn: an old couple and a little girl, terrified, sure the demonic sect eats people. They are watching you now, clutching their festival lanterns.

choices.text: Give them your own mooncakes and walk them home

effects.log: The girl takes a mooncake. By the village gate she is holding your hand.

choices.text: Leave them, and let them tell whatever story they like

effects.log: They run. The story they tell in the village is extremely dramatic.

choices.text: Make the disciples apologise for frightening them

effects.log: Ten black-robed disciples bow to an old couple. The old man faints a little.

events.text: The next Mid-Autumn, a parcel arrives at your demonic sect's gate: a single mooncake, slightly squashed, wrapped in red paper, with a child's drawing of a person in black holding a lantern. Your disciples pass it around in absolute silence.

choices.text: Hang the drawing in your hall

effects.log: Black robes, red drawing. The disciples say it brings luck, and nobody argues.

choices.text: Eat the mooncake with the elders, one bite each

effects.log: Twelve fierce elders share one squashed mooncake. It is very quiet in the hall.

choices.text: Burn the drawing: the sect cannot be soft

effects.log: The paper burns. One of your elders sighs when it does.

events.text: {sw_foe} are trying to slip through Reed Marsh to take your sect from the south. Your scouts are lying in the reeds. The trouble is that the marsh belongs to ten thousand ducks, and the ducks are loud and loyal to no one.

choices.text: Charge them in the shallows before they reach dry land

effects.log: You meet them knee-deep in the marsh. The ducks rise in a great complaining cloud.

choices.text: Wait until the ducks give away their line, then strike

effects.log: The ducks scream at their every step. You know exactly where they are.

choices.text: Wade out and challenge {sw_leader} in the shallows

ok.log: You win, both of you soaked. A duck sits on the enemy's hat in the end.

fail.log: You lose, face-first into the marsh mud. Even the ducks are laughing.
fail.deathCause: a duel with the leader of an enemy sect, in a sect war

choices.text: Shout across the reeds: nobody can fight with these ducks

effects.log: The enemy agrees. It is the ducks' marsh, after all.

events.text: The battle is over. A local duck farmer, Granny Pei, comes stomping up to your gate with a list. Forty ducks frightened off. One duck stolen, she says, by your people, and roasted. She has smelled it on the wind.

choices.text: Find out who roasted the duck

effects.log: Three junior disciples confess at once, with feathers still on their sleeves.

choices.text: Pay Granny Pei for every duck (25 taels)

effects.log: Pei counts the silver and says the roasted one was her favourite.

choices.text: Tell Pei the war has its costs

effects.log: Pei curses your sect so thoroughly that your elders are impressed.

events.text: The three duck-roasting disciples have spent a season working on Granny Pei's farm. Granny Pei now comes to visit you, with a basket. "They are good children," Pei says, "lazy as rocks. I am keeping one."

choices.text: Let the one who wants to stay, stay

effects.log: One of the three becomes Granny Pei's apprentice and, eventually, the best duck farmer in the province.

choices.text: Buy a flock of ducks for the sect pond (40 taels)

effects.log: The sect now has ducks. They are loud at dawn and everyone blames you.

choices.text: Thank Pei for the basket, and leave it there

effects.log: The basket is full of salted duck eggs. Pei grins as she goes.

events.text: {sw_foe} have blocked the spring outside your walls, and inside the walls there is one well, the Sweet Well, dug by the founder. This morning the bucket came up half full and muddy. Four hundred people are drinking from it. Elder Shu, the oldest, says there is a second spring under the mountain, if anyone remembers where.

choices.text: Ration the water: a bowl a day for everyone, you included

effects.log: You drink your bowl in public at dawn. Nobody complains, out loud.

choices.text: Search the founder's old notes for the second spring

ok.log: In a crumbling scroll, a map. The second spring is under the old woodshed.

fail.log: The notes are mostly about the founder's bad knees.

choices.text: Send a team out at night to break the enemy's dam

effects.log: Your team breaks the dam. Two do not come back, and the spring runs again.

events.text: The disciples are digging under the old woodshed with spades and swords, looking for the second spring. After three days they hit rock. On the fourth night Elder Shu goes down alone with a lamp and comes back up crying, because the old elder can hear water.

choices.text: Break through the rock with qi

effects.log: You strike the rock until your arms ache. On the fifth blow, water pours up cold and clean.

choices.text: Hand the digging to the strongest disciples in shifts

effects.log: Shifts all night. At dawn, water. The disciples carry the first bucket up like a bride.

choices.text: Let Elder Shu choose how to dig

effects.log: Shu chooses slowly, carefully, for a whole day, and then the water comes on the first try.

events.text: The siege is over. The second spring under the woodshed still runs, cleaner than the Sweet Well ever was. Elder Shu would like to name it. The disciples would like to name it after the woodshed.

choices.text: Name it after Elder Shu

effects.log: Shu's Spring. The old elder pretends to be annoyed for a year.

choices.text: Name it for the bowl-a-day you shared

effects.log: The Spring of One Bowl. Every new disciple drinks one bowl from it on joining.

choices.text: Let the disciples have the woodshed

effects.log: Woodshed Spring. It is ridiculous and everyone loves it.

events.text: Two months into the siege, the head cook, a heavy man named Pang, reports that the granary is losing a sack of rice every three nights. Rats, says Pang, but very clever rats, that untie knots. {sw_foe} sing drinking songs outside the walls every night, very well fed.

choices.text: Sit up in the granary yourself, in the dark

effects.log: You sit in the dark among the sacks for three nights, and on the third, the rat has two legs.

choices.text: Bring in the sect's cats, all eleven of them

effects.log: The cats eat well and catch nothing. The rice keeps vanishing.

choices.text: Cut everyone's rations by a third

effects.log: Hunger quiets the mountain. Somebody, somewhere, is still eating well.

events.text: The rice thief is Steward Gui, who has been giving the rice to the enemy's camp in exchange for promises of safety when the walls fall. Gui is on the floor now, begging. Half the sect is hungry because of this, and the other half wants to hear what you do.

choices.text: Expel Gui through the front gate, to the enemy

effects.log: Gui goes out into the enemy camp. They have no use for a thief either.

choices.text: Put Gui to work on half rations, under watch

effects.log: Gui hauls water for the rest of the siege, eating less than anyone, and never steals again.

choices.text: Make Gui confess in front of the whole sect

effects.log: Gui confesses in the courtyard. Afterwards, nobody hoards a grain of rice.

events.text: After the siege, Cook Pang serves a feast with the last good sack of rice, and asks you to say a few words. Steward Gui's chair at the long table is empty. Everyone looks at it.

choices.text: Toast those who went hungry for the rest

effects.log: Four hundred cups rise. Pang cries into the soup, which the soup did not need.

choices.text: Toast Pang, who kept the kitchen going

effects.log: Pang turns red as a crab and serves you double.

choices.text: Leave a bowl of rice at the empty chair

effects.log: A bowl of rice at Gui's seat. Nobody says anything, and everybody understands.

events.text: {sw_foe} sit behind walls you cannot climb. A coal miner named {npc} walks into your camp with a pick over one shoulder and offers, for a price, to dig under them. "Forty days," says the miner. "Thirty if the clay is kind. I need twenty strong backs and nobody talking."
events.arc: The Miner from Black Coal Hill

choices.text: Hire the miner (100 taels)

effects.log: {npc} takes the silver, bites one coin, and starts digging that night.

choices.text: Offer a share of whatever is in the enemy's treasury instead

effects.log: {npc} grins. "A gambler. Good." The digging starts at dawn.

choices.text: Send the miner away: tunnels are a coward's road

effects.log: {npc} shrugs, shoulders the pick and walks off whistling.

events.text: Twenty-eight days under the earth. The tunnel is a hundred and twelve paces long, propped with pine, and {npc} has not slept properly in a week. Tonight the miner presses an ear to the clay and holds up a hand: the enemy is digging too, toward you, very close.
events.arc: The Miner from Black Coal Hill

choices.text: Break through first and fight in the dark

effects.log: You burst into their tunnel with lamps. The fight is short, filthy and yours.

choices.text: Do what the miner says, exactly

effects.log: {npc} shores up a wall, waits, and lets their tunnel fall in on itself. Nobody is under it. Very clever.

choices.text: Listen yourself, with qi, to find their line

ok.log: You hear every pick stroke. You go round them and come up under their kitchen.

fail.log: You hear your own heartbeat, very loud. {npc} sighs and takes over.

events.text: The siege is over. {npc} comes to collect, standing in your hall in a coat still grey with clay. The miner says the tunnel will collapse within the year, and that a hole in the ground is not a thing to be proud of. Then the miner asks if your sect has any use for a digger.
events.arc: The Miner from Black Coal Hill

choices.text: Pay the share, as agreed (150 taels)

effects.log: {npc} takes the share and laughs. "Honest sect. Rare."

choices.text: Offer the miner a place in the sect, building cellars

effects.log: {npc} digs the finest cold cellars on the mountain. Your wine has never been so good.

choices.text: Thank the miner and walk {him} to the gate

effects.log: {npc} goes back to Black Coal Hill. Sometimes a lump of good coal arrives, with no note.

events.text: Somebody is digging under your walls. You know it because old Auntie Mo, who has run the sect laundry for forty years, has put bowls of water all over the cellar floor, and three of them are rippling. {sw_foe} are coming up from underneath. Auntie Mo is very calm about this.
events.arc: Bowls of Water on the Floor

choices.text: Dig a counter-tunnel to meet them

effects.log: Your disciples dig toward the ripples, with Mo reading the bowls like a scholar.

choices.text: Flood the cellar to drown out their tunnel

effects.log: Water goes down, mud comes up. Their tunnel fills. Auntie Mo complains that you ruined the cellar.

choices.text: Wait at the ripples with your best fighters

effects.log: You sit in the dark cellar with ten swords and a lot of bowls. It is a very long night.

events.text: The ripples stop three feet from the cellar wall. Then a pick comes through the stone, and a lamp, and a very frightened young sapper of the enemy, who looks at your ten swords and Auntie Mo's bowls and says, "Oh."
events.arc: Bowls of Water on the Floor

choices.text: Take the sapper prisoner, unharmed

effects.log: The sapper surrenders very fast. Mo gives the youth a dry cloth and a look.

choices.text: Send the sapper back down the tunnel with a message

effects.log: The sapper scrambles home with your message: "We heard you. Come again." Nobody comes again.

choices.text: Collapse their tunnel, now, with them in it

effects.log: The tunnel comes down. Mo looks at you a long while and puts away the bowls.

events.text: After the siege, Auntie Mo asks to be allowed to retire from the laundry. Mo is seventy-three and has, apparently, been listening to the ground for invaders for forty years, just in case. "Somebody should," Mo says.
events.arc: Bowls of Water on the Floor

choices.text: Make Auntie Mo the sect's watchkeeper of the earth

effects.log: Mo gets a title, a chair and a room full of bowls. The disciples call it the Water Hall.

choices.text: Learn Mo's craft yourself

effects.log: You learn to read the ground through still water. It is the strangest martial art you know.

choices.text: Give Mo a pension and a garden (80 taels)

effects.log: Mo grows cabbages and still keeps one bowl of water on the floor, just in case.

events.text: Morale is bad. Half the sect has not laughed in a month of siege, and {sw_foe} shout insults over the walls at dawn. Then a traveling storyteller, trapped inside your walls when the siege began, offers to perform on the wall every evening, "for a bowl of rice and the pleasure of an audience who cannot leave."

choices.text: Agree, and sit in the front row

effects.log: The storyteller performs the tale of the Monkey King. You laugh so hard the disciples stare.

choices.text: Agree, but only heroic tales

effects.log: The storyteller does heroic tales, very well. Morale lifts, a little.

choices.text: Refuse: this is a siege, not a teahouse

effects.log: The storyteller sits in a corner, silent. Morale stays where it was.

events.text: Every evening the storyteller climbs onto the wall and tells tales. The enemy camp has started listening too. Tonight there is a cliffhanger, and from the enemy lines a voice shouts: "And then? What happened to the general?"

choices.text: Have the storyteller finish the story, loudly, for both sides

effects.log: Both camps hear the ending. Both camps cheer. Nobody fights that night.

choices.text: Stop at the cliffhanger every night, to torment them

effects.log: The enemy begs for the ending for a week. Their morale is worse than yours now.

choices.text: Ask the storyteller for a tale about your own sect

effects.log: The storyteller makes you the hero of an epic. It is mostly lies, and very good.

events.text: The siege is over, and the storyteller is leaving, with a sack of rice and a new tale called "The Siege of {sect}". In it, you appear in chapter nine. The storyteller asks if you would like to hear it before the teahouses do.

choices.text: Listen, and laugh at yourself

effects.log: In chapter nine you are taller and wiser and fall off a wall. You laugh until your ribs hurt.

choices.text: Pay the storyteller to make you look better (60 taels)

effects.log: The storyteller takes your silver and makes you taller. Everyone in the teahouses can tell.

choices.text: Let the tale go out as it is

effects.log: The tale spreads through the province. People come to your gate to see the wall.

events.text: A girl of eleven, the gatekeeper's granddaughter Little Lu, has climbed onto your wall with a slingshot and has been shooting pebbles at {sw_foe} all afternoon. She has hit one of them on the helmet. They are shouting threats. She is shouting back, much worse ones.

choices.text: Carry her down yourself, kicking

effects.log: She kicks you twice on the way down and once more at the bottom.

choices.text: Give her a job: watching the far tower with a gong

effects.log: Little Lu takes the gong as if it were a sword. She spots the enemy's night move before anyone.

choices.text: Let her stay, and stand next to her

effects.log: You stand beside a child with a slingshot. The enemy stops shouting, not sure what to make of it.

events.text: The enemy's scouts have started using their own child, a drummer boy no older than Little Lu, to shout insults back. The two of them have been trading insults across the ditch for a week. Today Little Lu wants permission to throw him a sweet cake.

choices.text: Allow it

effects.log: The cake goes over the ditch. A dried date comes back. The war, for a moment, looks very foolish.

choices.text: Forbid it: he could be a spy

effects.log: Lu throws the cake when you are not looking. A date comes back anyway.

choices.text: Throw it yourself, farther

effects.log: You throw it farther than needed, and it hits their captain. Both sides laugh.

events.text: Years later, Little Lu is a full disciple, still small, still loud. She comes to tell you she is going to visit the enemy sect, now at peace, to meet the drummer boy, who is grown and writes very bad poetry to her.

choices.text: Give her a sect token for safe passage

effects.log: She goes with your token. The bad poetry, she reports, is much worse in person.

choices.text: Give her the old gong to take as a gift

effects.log: She carries the gong across the mountains. The drummer, she writes, cried.

choices.text: Tell her the wounds of war are not yet healed

effects.log: She goes anyway, a month later, without asking. Some things you cannot order.

events.text: {sw_foe} are at your outer gate, and the only person who knows how the founder's old defensive array works is {npc}, the eighty-two-year-old gardener, who claims to have been the founder's servant. Nobody has ever believed it. {npc} is pointing at nine stones in the herb garden with a trowel.

choices.text: Believe the gardener and follow every instruction

effects.log: {npc} has you move the nine stones a finger's width each. Nothing happens. Then the mist rises.

choices.text: Study the stones yourself

ok.log: You see it: a buried ring of formation lines. You wake it, and the gate disappears behind mist.

fail.log: You see nine stones and some mint. {npc} sighs a gardener's sigh.

choices.text: Ignore the gardener and reinforce the gate

effects.log: You pile timber at the gate. {npc} goes back to pruning, unimpressed.

events.text: The mist array holds the enemy at the gate for nine days. They wander in circles, swearing. But each night the gardener grows more tired, and tonight {npc} sits down among the herbs and says the array is fed by whoever stands at its heart. "That has been me, for nine days."

choices.text: Take {npc}'s place at the heart of the array

effects.log: You stand among the herbs all night, and the mist draws on you like a hungry child. At dawn it still holds.

choices.text: Ask {npc} to teach three disciples to share it

effects.log: {npc} teaches in whispers. Three disciples take turns, and the gardener sleeps for two days.

choices.text: Let the array fall and fight at the gate

effects.log: The mist thins. You fight at the gate the old way, and {npc} watches from the garden.

events.text: The siege is over. {npc} has not left the garden bed for a month, and the physician says the gardener will not see another spring. One evening {npc} calls for you, and hands you the trowel. "The stones need moving a finger's width each autumn. That is all. That is the whole secret."

choices.text: Promise to move them yourself, every autumn

effects.log: Each autumn you move nine stones in the herb garden. The mist sleeps, and waits.

choices.text: Ask whether {npc} truly served the founder

effects.log: {npc} laughs a long time, coughs, and says only, "Who do you think planted the mint?"

choices.text: Carve {npc}'s name into the ninth stone

effects.log: The ninth stone carries a gardener's name now, beside the founder's.

events.text: Autumn again. You kneel in the herb garden and move nine stones a finger's width each. A young apprentice gardener watches from the path, the way you must once have watched, and asks what the stones are for.

choices.text: Teach the apprentice the secret

effects.log: You hand over the trowel. The mist will sleep and wait for another lifetime.

choices.text: Say they are for the mint

effects.log: The apprentice nods very seriously and waters the mint every day after.

choices.text: Keep the secret a little longer

effects.log: You move the stones alone, in the evening, as the old gardener did.

events.text: {sw_foe} are building siege towers, tall clever things on wheels that walk toward your walls. Your scouts have learned the engineer's name: {npc}, once a builder of bridges for the Ministry of Works, who sells skill to any sect that pays. Tonight {npc} is asleep in a tent at the edge of their camp, guarded by two bored men.
events.arc: The Engineer Who Built Their Towers

choices.text: Send a team to carry the engineer off

effects.log: Your team comes back at dawn with a very surprised engineer in a sack, still in sleeping robes.

choices.text: Burn the towers instead

effects.log: The towers burn like torches. {npc} will just build more, but it buys you a week.

choices.text: Send {npc} a letter offering better pay

effects.log: A reply comes: "Double, and I am yours after this contract." Professional, at least.

events.text: {npc} is sitting in your hall, drinking your tea, and studying your walls with real interest. "Terrible," says the engineer. "Whoever built your east wall should be ashamed. I could have it down in a week. Or I could fix it."
events.arc: The Engineer Who Built Their Towers

choices.text: Hire {npc} to fix it (120 taels)

effects.log: {npc} fixes the east wall in nine days, and complains about every stone.

choices.text: Make {npc} a prisoner who works for food

effects.log: {npc} works for food, slowly and badly, with great dignity.

choices.text: Let {npc} go home with a warning

effects.log: {npc} bows, and leaves. The towers do not come back this war.

events.text: Years later, {npc} turns up at your gate with a cart of drawings. "Every sect I ever worked for is now at war with one of the others," the engineer says. "I want to build one thing that is not for knocking down. A covered bridge, for your valley. I would need nothing but timber and time."
events.arc: The Engineer Who Built Their Towers

choices.text: Give {npc} the timber, and the time

effects.log: The covered bridge takes two years. It is beautiful. Children play under it in the rain.

choices.text: Pay for the bridge outright (150 taels)

effects.log: The bridge is built. {npc} carves your sect's crest into the keystone, slightly crooked.

choices.text: Decline: the valley has enough bridges

effects.log: {npc} packs the drawings and goes. The rain falls on an old ford.

events.text: The north wall comes down at dusk, after six days of {sw_foe} pounding it with a ram. The breach is ten paces wide and full of rubble. They will come through at dawn. You have one night, four hundred tired people, and every loose stone on the mountain.

choices.text: Rebuild the breach with every hand you have

effects.log: Everyone carries stones: elders, cooks, children, you. By dawn the breach is shoulder-high.

choices.text: Build a second wall behind the breach, a trap

effects.log: When they come through the gap, they find a second wall and arrows on three sides.

choices.text: Hold the breach yourself, alone, until dawn

ok.log: You stand in the breach all night. In the morning they look at you and decide to wait.

fail.log: You hold until the third rush, and fall. Your people carry you back.
fail.deathCause: holding a breached wall alone, in a sect war

events.text: Dawn. They came, and were thrown back. In the rubble of the breach the disciples find a battered cooking pot, a sandal, and a little wooden carving of a horse, belonging to a disciple called Tian, who carried stones all night and slipped from the wall at the last hour, and did not wake.

choices.text: Set Tian's horse in the rebuilt wall

effects.log: The little horse sits in a niche of the new wall. Disciples touch it on the way past.

choices.text: Write to Tian's family yourself

effects.log: You write all night. The letter is short, because the true things are short.

choices.text: Order everyone back to work: the war is not over

effects.log: They go back to work, in silence. The horse stays in your sleeve.

events.text: The war is over. The north wall stands again, rebuilt properly by masons, but nobody has removed the rough patch of rubble stones from the night of the breach. The masons want to replace it with dressed stone.

choices.text: Leave the rough patch as it is, forever

effects.log: The ugly patch stays. Every new disciple is told what night it was built.

choices.text: Let the masons dress the stone

effects.log: The wall is smooth again. Some disciples are sorry, and do not say so.

choices.text: Have the names of all who carried stones cut into it

effects.log: Four hundred names cut small into the rough stones. It takes the carver a year.

events.text: Every year on the night of the breach, the sect keeps a strange custom: everyone, from the eldest elder to the newest child, carries one stone up to the north wall and sets it at its foot. The pile is now taller than a person. A new disciple asks you why.

choices.text: Carry a stone with the new disciple, and tell the story on the way

effects.log: By the top of the path the disciple has stopped asking questions and is carrying the stone very carefully.

choices.text: Say: so that we remember how heavy one night is

effects.log: The disciple thinks about that for a whole year.

choices.text: Carry two stones yourself this year

effects.log: Your back aches for a week. Tian's little horse watches from its niche.

events.text: You have {sw_foe} surrounded on their mountain, and they are starving. This morning their gate opens a crack and a messenger comes out: they will surrender nothing, but they ask that their old people and young children be allowed to leave. Your elders say it is a trick to save rice.
events.arc: The Gate of the Old and Young

choices.text: Let the old and young walk out

effects.log: Sixty people walk out between your lines, very slowly. One old woman bows to every disciple she passes.

choices.text: Agree, but search every one of them

effects.log: Your people search sixty frightened people. You find one dagger and a great deal of shame.

choices.text: Refuse: they chose this war

effects.log: The gate closes. That night you hear children crying behind it.

events.text: Among the sixty is a boy of twelve who, your scouts swear, is the leader's own nephew. He is sitting in your camp now, eating your rice and staring at you with pure hatred. Your elders see a bargaining piece.
events.arc: The Gate of the Old and Young

choices.text: Treat him as you would any guest

effects.log: The boy eats, sleeps and says nothing. On the third day he asks for more pickles.

choices.text: Send a message: the boy is safe, whatever happens

effects.log: The message goes in. That night, their gate is quiet for the first time.

choices.text: Use him: terms for the boy

effects.log: You send terms. The answer comes back very cold, but it comes.

events.text: The war is over. The sixty have gone home, and their mountain stands, though its sect is weaker. A letter arrives, not from their leader but from the old woman who bowed to your disciples. She has knitted, she says, a pair of socks for whoever was kind to her grandson in your camp.
events.arc: The Gate of the Old and Young

choices.text: Wear the socks

effects.log: They are lumpy and very warm. You wear them every winter after.

choices.text: Give the socks to the disciple who fed the boy

effects.log: The disciple who fed him wears them proudly, and tells the story to every new recruit.

choices.text: Write back to the old woman

effects.log: She writes again, and again. The letters go on for years.

events.text: Your demonic sect has {sw_foe} shut up in their walls, and they have told their disciples that your people eat prisoners. Your youngest elder, a cheerful woman named Hua, has a plan: kites. Hundreds of paper kites, flown over their walls, each carrying a letter. "Truth," Hua says, "is lighter than arrows."

choices.text: Let Hua write the letters

effects.log: Hua's letters are funny, short and full of good food. Two hundred kites cross their wall.

choices.text: Write the letters yourself, coldly

effects.log: Your letters list the terms of surrender, very clearly. They frighten more than they persuade.

choices.text: Fly the kites with burning tails instead

effects.log: Burning kites over their walls. Your sect lives up to its reputation tonight.

events.text: The kites work. At night, disciples start slipping over the wall to surrender, one or two at a time, all of them hungry. One young man carries a kite letter folded in his sleeve and asks, very seriously, whether the dumplings in it are real.

choices.text: Feed him dumplings, exactly as promised

effects.log: He eats twenty. The next night, eight more come over the wall.

choices.text: Make the deserters fly kites back over the wall

effects.log: Their own disciples fly kites over the wall. It is the cruellest and kindest thing you have done.

choices.text: Hold them all as prisoners until the war ends

effects.log: The deserters wait in a tent. The kites stop working.

events.text: After the siege, the orthodox sect's own disciples tell a story about your demonic sect: that you fed your deserters dumplings, flew kites over their walls and never ate anyone. The Murim Alliance is very irritated about this story.

choices.text: Hang a kite in your sect hall

effects.log: One paper kite hangs over your demonic hall now. It is a strange sight among the black banners.

choices.text: Spread the story further

effects.log: The story spreads. Two orthodox disciples defect the next year, for the dumplings.

choices.text: Let the story die: fear is useful too

effects.log: You let the old rumours stand. The Alliance relaxes. So do you, a little.

events.text: The Murim Alliance has praised your righteous sect for besieging {sw_foe}, but praise does not keep anyone warm. It is the coldest winter in twenty years and your disciples are in tents. Behind the enemy walls there are warm halls and fires. Your quartermaster is burning the spare spears for heat.

choices.text: Buy furs from the nearest town (120 taels)

effects.log: Furs arrive by ox-cart. Your disciples look like bears and stop shivering.

choices.text: Order the disciples to cultivate warmth, in shifts

effects.log: A hundred disciples meditate in the snow, steaming gently. It works, mostly.

choices.text: Pull back to the town for the winter

effects.log: You pull back. The Alliance writes you a very stiff letter.

events.text: Midwinter. A delegation comes out of the enemy gate with a cart. Inside the cart are blankets, quite a lot of them, and a letter: "Our elders say the orthodox will die of cold before we die of hunger. We would rather beat you in spring."

choices.text: Accept the blankets, and send back rice

effects.log: Blankets out, rice in. The siege continues, oddly, as a kind of trade.

choices.text: Refuse the blankets: a righteous sect needs no charity

effects.log: The cart goes back. Your disciples watch it go, shivering.

choices.text: Accept them and propose terms

effects.log: You talk terms over a cart of blankets. They are surprisingly reasonable terms.

events.text: The war is over. Your quartermaster brings you the winter's accounts: so much for rice, so much for furs, and a column for "blankets, enemy, returned?" with a question mark. The Alliance has asked for a full report of the siege.

choices.text: Report everything, blankets included

effects.log: The Alliance does not know what to make of your report. Two elders call it shameful; one calls it wise.

choices.text: Leave the blankets out of the report

effects.log: Your report is a clean, heroic thing. You know what it leaves out.

choices.text: Send the furs on to the poor of the town

effects.log: The town wears your furs that winter. The Alliance reads about that instead.

events.text: Somebody is selling maps of your mountain to {sw_foe}: secret paths, guard posts, the old drainage tunnel. Your scouts have found a copy in an enemy camp. The hand is beautiful, and you know it at once. It belongs to {npc}, the sect's archivist, who taught you to read.

choices.text: Go to the archive and ask {npc} directly

effects.log: {npc} does not deny it. The archivist only says, "Sit. I will make tea. This will take a while."

choices.text: Watch the archive in secret for a month

effects.log: In a month you see {npc} meet a pedlar three times. The pedlar carries rolled paper away.

choices.text: Report it to the other elders at once

effects.log: The elders seize {npc} in the archive. The ink is still wet on a new map.

events.text: The truth: {npc} has a grandchild, sick with a lung fever, in a town the enemy controls. They pay for the physician. They have been paying for two years. {npc} drew every map with one small error in it, so that nobody who followed them would ever reach the inner hall.

choices.text: Check the maps for the errors

effects.log: Every map is wrong in one place: always the place that matters. The enemy never got far.

choices.text: Pay for the grandchild's physician yourself (150 taels)

effects.log: Your silver reaches the town. {npc} weeps in the archive, very quietly, among the books.

choices.text: Have {npc} keep selling maps, wrong ones you design

effects.log: {npc} draws your maps now. The enemy walks into three ambushes in a month.

events.text: The war is over, and {npc} has come to resign as archivist. "A keeper of records who sold them," the archivist says. "I cannot stay in the room." On the desk is a new map, beautifully drawn, of the mountain, with no errors at all. It is a gift.

choices.text: Refuse the resignation

effects.log: {npc} stays in the archive until the end, and is buried with an ink brush. The maps are still the best in the province.

choices.text: Accept it, and send {npc} to the grandchild

effects.log: {npc} goes to the town and the healthy grandchild. A letter comes every spring.

choices.text: Accept it, and keep the map locked away

effects.log: The map goes into your strongbox. {npc} goes down the mountain alone.

events.text: Spring. The archive's window is open and someone has put fresh plum blossom on the desk where the old archivist worked. Under it lies a rolled map you have never seen: the whole of the enemy's mountain, drawn in that same beautiful hand, with no errors at all.

choices.text: Lock it away, unused, as a promise of peace

effects.log: The map goes into the strongbox. You hope you never open it.

choices.text: Send it to the enemy, with a note

effects.log: The enemy receives a perfect map of their own mountain and a note: "We could have. We did not." The peace is very firm after that.

choices.text: Study it, quietly, just in case

effects.log: You study it for a month. Then you put the blossom back on the desk.

events.text: Your scouts have caught one of your own disciples, {npc}, at the river ford at midnight, meeting a disciple of {sw_foe}. They were not trading secrets. They were trading peaches. {npc} kneels in front of you, wet to the knees, and refuses to say the other one's name.

choices.text: Ask {npc} how long it has been going on

effects.log: "Three years," says {npc}. "Since before the war. We met at the lantern festival."

choices.text: Forbid it, while the war lasts

effects.log: {npc} bows and says yes, and you both know what that yes is worth.

choices.text: Confine {npc} to the mountain

effects.log: {npc} is confined. The peaches stop. So does the smile.

events.text: The enemy has caught the other one, the peach-trader from their side, and is about to expel that disciple for treason. {npc} comes to you white-faced. "If they throw my friend out, there is nowhere to go but the road," {npc} says. "Please. Anything."

choices.text: Offer the expelled disciple sanctuary with your sect

effects.log: The peach-trader climbs your mountain with a bundle. {npc} meets the road halfway.

choices.text: Write to their leader and plead the pair's case

ok.log: The leader, surprisingly, relents. War is war, the letter says, but peaches are peaches.

fail.log: Your letter is thrown in a fire. The expulsion goes ahead.

choices.text: Stay out of it

effects.log: {npc} says nothing more. Later you hear the peach-trader has taken to the road alone.

events.text: Peace has come. {npc} and the peach-trader want to marry, and the wedding needs a senior from each sect to stand witness. The other sect's elders have said yes, if you will. It would be the first wedding between the two mountains in fifty years.

choices.text: Stand witness at the wedding

effects.log: You stand under the red lanterns beside your old enemy's elder. The peaches at the feast are excellent.

choices.text: Send a wedding gift of silver (60 taels)

effects.log: Your gift arrives. {npc} writes that the pair have bought a peach orchard with it.

choices.text: Refuse: the war is too close

effects.log: The wedding happens without you. {npc} does not write for many years.

events.text: Spring, years later. The orchard of {npc} and the peach-trader is in bloom on the border between the two mountains, and disciples of both sects come to pick fruit there in summer. The pair have sent you a basket of peaches and an invitation to name their first tree.

choices.text: Name it the Ford at Midnight

effects.log: The tree is called the Ford at Midnight. Couples from both sects meet under it now.

choices.text: Name it after the war that nearly parted them

effects.log: A sober name. Under it, disciples of both sides remember.
