choices.text: Go and plant a second tree beside it

effects.log: You plant a peach tree with your own hands. {npc} laughs at your digging.

events.text: The enemy's spy in {sect} has been caught: a quiet copyist called {npc}, who has passed letters to {sw_foe} for a year. {npc} is sitting in a cell, calm as a clerk, and makes an offer. "I can keep writing to them," says {npc}. "Whatever you like. For my life, and a little silver."
events.arc: The Agent Who Served Two Halls

choices.text: Accept, and run {npc} as your own agent

effects.log: {npc} writes the first false letter that night, in a perfect hand, and asks for more paper.

choices.text: Accept, but have {npc} watched every hour

effects.log: Two disciples shadow {npc} day and night. {npc} finds this flattering.

choices.text: Refuse, and expel {npc} from the sect

effects.log: {npc} walks out of the gate with a bundle and a small, amused bow.

events.text: Your false letters are working. Three enemy raids have gone the wrong way. But today the enemy's reply to {npc} contains a line that only someone in your inner hall could know. {npc} shows it to you at once. "There is another one," says the copyist. "And it is not me."
events.arc: The Agent Who Served Two Halls

choices.text: Trust {npc} and hunt the second spy together

effects.log: Together you find the second spy in two weeks: a steward with gambling debts. {npc} looks very pleased.

choices.text: Test {npc} with a secret only the copyist knows

ok.log: The secret never reaches the enemy. {npc} is loyal, as far as anyone is.

fail.log: The secret reaches the enemy, but so do two others, and you cannot tell which leak was which.

choices.text: Lock {npc} up again, just in case

effects.log: {npc} goes back to the cell, unsurprised. The other spy keeps working.

events.text: Peace. {npc} comes to you with a small bag packed and asks what happens now. The copyist has served two halls for two years and belongs to neither. "I am very good at this," says {npc}. "It is a terrible thing to be good at."
events.arc: The Agent Who Served Two Halls

choices.text: Make {npc} the sect's own keeper of secrets

effects.log: {npc} runs your letters and listeners from a small room. Nobody surprises you again.

choices.text: Give {npc} silver and a new name (100 taels)

effects.log: {npc} goes to the south with silver and a new name. A postcard of a teahouse comes once a year, unsigned.

choices.text: Hand {npc} back to the enemy, as part of the peace

effects.log: {npc} goes back to the enemy. You never learn what they did, and try not to think about it.

events.text: A letter is found in the camp of {sw_foe}, after a skirmish, and brought to you. It is written in the hand of Elder Ruan, your most loyal elder, and it offers to open the west gate on the night of the new moon. Ruan has served the sect for forty years and is asleep in the next hall.
events.arc: A Letter in Elder Ruan's Hand

choices.text: Study the letter yourself, slowly

effects.log: You compare it with Ruan's reports. The hand is perfect. Too perfect: Ruan always blots the third stroke.

choices.text: Show the letter to Ruan, alone

effects.log: Ruan reads it twice and goes grey. "That is my hand," the old elder says. "I did not write it."

choices.text: Have Ruan arrested before the new moon

effects.log: Ruan is led away without a word, and the whole hall goes silent.

events.text: The new moon. If Ruan is a traitor, the west gate is the place. If the letter is a forgery, someone meant you to strike at your own best elder. Either way, someone in the enemy camp is waiting tonight to see what you do.
events.arc: A Letter in Elder Ruan's Hand

choices.text: Put Ruan in command of the west gate

effects.log: Ruan stands on the west gate all night. Nobody comes. In the morning the old elder is shaking with relief.

choices.text: Lay an ambush at the west gate

effects.log: At midnight a small enemy band comes to the gate expecting it open. They find your swords.

choices.text: Release Ruan and apologise before the whole sect

effects.log: You bow to Ruan in front of everyone. The old elder bows back, lower.

events.text: After the war, an enemy disciple turns up at your gate with a confession: their sect had a forger, a scholar who copied hands for gold, and the forger has since died. Among the forger's papers was a practice sheet: three hundred copies of a single stroke, Ruan's third stroke, blotted.
events.arc: A Letter in Elder Ruan's Hand

choices.text: Give the practice sheet to Ruan

effects.log: Ruan frames it and hangs it in the elder's study. "The price of a blot," Ruan says.

choices.text: Order every elder to seal letters with a personal mark

effects.log: Every letter on the mountain now carries a seal. Forgers will have to work much harder.

choices.text: Burn the sheet

effects.log: The sheet burns. Ruan watches without a word.

events.text: Three of your elders fell ill after the evening tea, and the physician smells something bitter in the pot. Not deadly, the physician thinks, but enough to keep them abed during a battle. {sw_foe} have someone in your kitchens. The tea boy, a nervous youth called Ah Jin, has not slept since.

choices.text: Question Ah Jin gently

effects.log: Ah Jin breaks down at once: a pedlar paid him to put a powder in the pot. He thought it was sleeping powder.

choices.text: Set a trap: let the pedlar come back

effects.log: The pedlar comes back with more powder, and walks into four of your disciples.

choices.text: Search every room in the kitchens

effects.log: You find a packet of powder hidden in the rice jar. Whose, nobody will say.

events.text: Ah Jin is seventeen, an orphan, and was paid five taels for a powder that nearly put three elders in their graves. The elders who drank it want the boy expelled. Ah Jin's only family is the sect.

choices.text: Keep Ah Jin, under watch, in the infirmary

effects.log: Ah Jin works in the infirmary, nursing the elders who drank his tea. One of them, eventually, forgives him.

choices.text: Expel Ah Jin

effects.log: Ah Jin walks out of the gate with five taels and no home. Nobody watches him go.

choices.text: Make Ah Jin lead you to the pedlar's master

effects.log: Ah Jin leads you to an inn and a man with a trunk of powders. That is the end of that.

events.text: Years after the war, Ah Jin has become the sect's best herbalist, and comes to you with a new tea blend. "It cures the bitterness," Ah Jin says, "in the stomach and elsewhere. I wanted you to taste it first."

choices.text: Drink it, without hesitation

effects.log: The tea is wonderful. Ah Jin watches you drink it and has to look away.

choices.text: Make Ah Jin drink the first cup

effects.log: Ah Jin drinks it, smiling a little sadly. You drink the second.

choices.text: Name the blend the Second Pot

effects.log: The Second Pot is sold in teahouses across the province. Nobody knows why it is called that.

events.text: On the eve of your great attack on {sw_foe}, Elder {npc} has done the unthinkable: warned them. Your scouts caught the messenger. {npc} sits in chains in front of the whole sect and does not look sorry. "Your plan sends two hundred disciples into a valley with one way out," the elder says. "I could not watch it."

choices.text: Ask {npc} to show you on the map

effects.log: {npc} traces it with a chained finger. One way in, one way out, and the hills above.

choices.text: Hold the attack for a day while you think

effects.log: The attack waits. Your elders grumble, and {npc} waits in the cell.

choices.text: Order the attack anyway

effects.log: You attack at dawn as planned. The valley does exactly what {npc} said it would.

events.text: The attack has been changed, and you came in over the hills instead of up the valley. Your scouts found the valley mouth full of enemy archers who had been waiting for two days. {npc} is still in chains, because no matter what, an elder of the sect warned the enemy.

choices.text: Free {npc} and name the reason before the whole sect

effects.log: {npc} is freed in front of everyone. Half the sect is grateful; the other half will never trust the elder again.

choices.text: Keep {npc} in chains until the war ends

effects.log: {npc} stays in the cell, and asks only for a window.

choices.text: Exile {npc}, but quietly, with silver (80 taels)

effects.log: {npc} leaves at night with silver and no title.

events.text: Peace. {npc} has come to the sect hall to resign from the council of elders, with a speech prepared. Before the elder can begin, half the young disciples stand up. Some of them were in the valley-mouth party. They are not sitting down until you speak.

choices.text: Refuse the resignation

effects.log: {npc} stays an elder, the one who said no. The young disciples tell that story more than any battle.

choices.text: Accept it, with honour

effects.log: {npc} resigns, and is given a house and a garden by the gate. The young ones visit every week.

choices.text: Make {npc} the keeper of the war council's plans

effects.log: Every plan now goes past {npc} first. Your plans get worse at sounding good and better at working.

events.text: Your sect's pigeon loft has thirty birds. This morning it has thirty-one. The new one is grey with a red band on its leg and a little tube with a letter in it, addressed to {sw_foe}, in a code nobody can read. The pigeon is eating your best millet and looking very relaxed.

choices.text: Send the pigeon on its way with a false letter

effects.log: The pigeon flies off carrying your lie. The keeper of the loft is very impressed with you.

choices.text: Keep the pigeon and try to break the code

effects.log: You sit up all night with the letter and a lamp. By dawn you have one word: "millet".

choices.text: Cook the pigeon

effects.log: The pigeon is delicious. The loft-keeper does not speak to you for a week.

events.text: The red-banded pigeon keeps coming back, every five days, with a new letter, each time to your loft. Whoever trained it trained it to the wrong loft, or the right one. The loft-keeper, Old Liu, thinks the bird likes the millet. Everyone else thinks there is a spy.

choices.text: Watch who visits the loft

effects.log: It is Old Liu's own apprentice, who has been selling the loft's routines to the enemy for a jar of honey.

choices.text: Keep sending false letters

effects.log: Five more false letters. The enemy marches to three wrong valleys. Old Liu calls the pigeon a hero.

choices.text: Give the pigeon to Old Liu to keep

effects.log: Liu clips the pigeon's wings and names it Traitor. It lives very happily.

events.text: After the war, the enemy sends you a single request through the peace envoy: could they please have their pigeon back. The envoy says it with an absolutely straight face. Old Liu is at the window, holding the bird.

choices.text: Give it back, with a sack of millet

effects.log: The pigeon goes home in a cage with a sack of millet. A week later, it is back in your loft.

choices.text: Refuse: it defected

effects.log: The envoy writes it down very carefully. It becomes a clause in the peace.

choices.text: Let Old Liu decide

effects.log: Old Liu decides the pigeon stays. The envoy goes home with an empty cage.

events.text: A beggar has sat outside your mountain gate every day since the war began, a cheerful old fellow with one sandal and a song about turnips. Your gate disciples give him leftovers. Today your scout says the beggar was seen in the camp of {sw_foe}, singing the same song.

choices.text: Invite the beggar in for a meal and a talk

effects.log: The beggar eats three bowls and says: "Beggars go everywhere, Elder. We listen to both sides. For a price."

choices.text: Have him chased off the mountain

effects.log: The beggar goes, still singing. You never know what he knew.

choices.text: Feed him false news to carry

effects.log: You complain loudly near the gate about the north road. The enemy watches the north road for a week.

events.text: The beggar, it turns out, belongs to the Beggar Sect, the oldest network of eyes and ears in the murim. The Beggars are neutral. They sell to everyone. The old fellow offers you, for a reasonable price, what the enemy is planning for the spring.

choices.text: Buy it (80 taels)

effects.log: The news is good: the date, the road, the numbers. You are waiting on that road in spring.

choices.text: Offer something better than silver: a favour to the Beggar Sect

effects.log: The beggar sucks his teeth and agrees. The Beggar Sect will collect that favour one day.

choices.text: Refuse: neutral spies sell you as well

effects.log: "True," says the beggar. "But we sell you honestly." He goes on singing.

events.text: Peace has come. One winter morning, a different beggar, a young one with a crutch, appears at your gate with a message: the Beggar Sect has come to collect its favour. A family of beggars needs shelter for the winter, and the cities have shut their doors.

choices.text: Open the sect's halls to them

effects.log: Thirty beggars spend the winter on your mountain. They eat a great deal and sing even more.

choices.text: Give them silver for an inn (60 taels)

effects.log: The beggars winter in an inn. They send back a song about you, which is quite flattering.

choices.text: Turn them away

effects.log: The young beggar nods and limps off. The Beggar Sect will remember, and so will you.

events.text: An envoy from the Murim Alliance comes to {sect} with a quiet request. A neighbouring sect, the Azure Pine school, is suspected of dealing with demonic cultivators. The Alliance would like you to place a disciple among them, to watch. "For the righteous path," the envoy says, sipping your tea.

choices.text: Agree, and send your quietest disciple

effects.log: Disciple Shen goes to the Azure Pine school as a student. You hope Shen is as quiet as you think.

choices.text: Ask the Alliance what proof they have

effects.log: The envoy has a rumour, a merchant's story and a strong feeling. You write all three down.

choices.text: Refuse: you will not spy on neighbours

effects.log: The envoy smiles a thin smile. The Alliance will remember the refusal.

events.text: Disciple Shen writes from the Azure Pine school. The school is poor, proud and honest. They have no demonic dealings. They do, however, have a rich vein of jade under their mountain, and an Alliance elder has been trying to buy it for years.

choices.text: Tell the Alliance the truth: the school is clean

effects.log: The Alliance accepts your report coldly. The jade quarrel goes on without you.

choices.text: Warn the Azure Pine school yourself

effects.log: You write to the school's master. A grateful reply comes back, and a little piece of jade.

choices.text: Recall Shen and say nothing

effects.log: Shen comes home. The Alliance does not ask again.

events.text: A year later, the Alliance elder who wanted the jade has been disgraced, and the Azure Pine school's master comes to your sect in person to thank you. The master has heard everything, it seems, from someone.

choices.text: Admit that you once agreed to spy

effects.log: The master laughs long and loud. "Then you are honest twice." The two sects become good friends.

choices.text: Accept the thanks without explaining

effects.log: The master goes away happy. You keep your part of the story to yourself.

choices.text: Propose an alliance of the two schools

effects.log: A small alliance of honest sects is born over tea. The Murim Alliance does not like this at all.

events.text: The elders of your demonic sect choose you for a task: walk down the mountain, put on plain clothes, and join the orthodox Green Willow school as a student. Watch, listen, report. "They will be kind to you," your elder says with distaste. "Try not to catch it."

choices.text: Go, and play the part well

effects.log: You become a cheerful student called Little Cai. The Green Willow school is, in fact, kind.

choices.text: Go, but report only what is useless

effects.log: You report the menu, the weather and the colour of the robes. Your elders are puzzled.

choices.text: Refuse the task

effects.log: Your elder looks at you a long time. You are given the latrines for a season.

events.text: Six months in the Green Willow school. You have a friend there now, a loud boy called Bao who shares his dumplings and believes all demonic cultivators have horns. Your sect wants a full map of the school's treasury by the new moon.

choices.text: Draw the map, as ordered

effects.log: You draw the map. Bao brings you dumplings that night and you can barely eat them.

choices.text: Draw it wrong

effects.log: The map you send leads to the school's turnip cellar. Your elders are not amused.

choices.text: Tell Bao the truth

effects.log: Bao stares at you, then at your forehead, looking for horns. "You are a terrible demon," Bao says.

events.text: Your sect recalls you. On your last night at the Green Willow school, Bao finds you packing. Bao has known for a month, or guessed, and has a present: a bag of dumplings and a wooden token of the school, in case you ever need a friend among the righteous.

choices.text: Take the token and keep it hidden

effects.log: The token goes into your sleeve. Among demons, you carry one piece of willow.

choices.text: Leave the token, but take the dumplings

effects.log: You walk home eating dumplings. They taste better than anything in your sect's kitchen.

choices.text: Report Bao to your elders as a useful contact

effects.log: Your elders are pleased. Bao never hears from you again, and you try not to think about it.

events.text: As an elder of {sect}, you are handed the year's accounts to sign. The figures for arrows do not add up: the sect has bought eight thousand arrows this year and has only ever used two thousand. Somebody is selling the rest. To whom, in a year of wars, is not a comforting question.
events.arc: The Ledger That Did Not Add Up

choices.text: Count the arrows in the armoury yourself

effects.log: Six thousand arrows are missing. The quartermaster is suddenly very ill.

choices.text: Ask the quartermaster, casually

effects.log: The quartermaster laughs too loudly and says the rats eat them.

choices.text: Sign the accounts and stay out of it

effects.log: You sign. The figures are not your problem. Yet.

events.text: The arrows went to a merchant in the river town, who sold them on to bandits in the hills, who used them on a caravan carrying your sect's own silk. The quartermaster has a wife, three children and a gambling habit, and is weeping in your study.
events.arc: The Ledger That Did Not Add Up

choices.text: Take it to the sect leader

effects.log: The quartermaster is dismissed. The leader thanks you, and looks at you differently after.

choices.text: Make the quartermaster repay it in labour

effects.log: The quartermaster carries arrows up the mountain for a year. The figures add up again.

choices.text: Go after the merchant in the river town

effects.log: You visit the merchant. The merchant decides, very suddenly, to retire to the south.

events.text: Next year, the new quartermaster hands you the accounts. Every arrow is counted, every coin. At the bottom there is a note in a careful hand: "Checked twice, because the Elder reads."
events.arc: The Ledger That Did Not Add Up

choices.text: Sign them, with a note of thanks

effects.log: The note of thanks goes up on the armoury wall. It is the first one there in a century.

choices.text: Check them anyway

effects.log: You check them all. They are perfect. The quartermaster is delighted to have been checked.

choices.text: Give the quartermaster a bonus (30 taels)

effects.log: The quartermaster blushes all the way to the armoury.

events.text: Among the prisoners taken from {sw_foe} is {npc}, nineteen, who fought well and surrendered only when the sword broke. {npc} has asked to speak to you. "I want to join your sect," says the prisoner. "Mine sent us to die on purpose. I saw the elders' faces."
events.arc: The Prisoner Who Wanted to Stay

choices.text: Listen to the whole story

effects.log: {npc} talks for an hour: an elder's feud, a sacrifice, a valley. It sounds true.

choices.text: Treat it as a trick and keep {npc} locked up

effects.log: {npc} nods, as if expecting it, and goes back to the cell.

choices.text: Say yes, on the spot

effects.log: Your elders are horrified. {npc} is given a robe of your colours and many suspicious looks.

events.text: {npc} has been training with your disciples for some months. The others have started to like the newcomer, slowly. Then a letter is found in {npc}'s bedroll, addressed to the old sect, half finished. It says: "I am safe. Tell Granny not to worry."
events.arc: The Prisoner Who Wanted to Stay

choices.text: Let {npc} send it, after reading it

effects.log: The letter goes, read and unchanged. {npc} bows to you in the yard for a long time.

choices.text: Burn the letter and say nothing

effects.log: {npc} looks for the letter for a week, then stops looking.

choices.text: Ask {npc} about Granny

effects.log: Granny is ninety, lives in the enemy's valley and makes the best pickled plums in the province.

events.text: Peace has come, and with it the exchange of prisoners. {npc} is on the list to be returned to the old sect. {npc} stands in the yard with a bundle, not looking at anyone. Your disciples are looking at you.
events.arc: The Prisoner Who Wanted to Stay

choices.text: Keep {npc}: the prisoner chose this sect

effects.log: You strike {npc}'s name from the list. The yard bursts into cheers, then into training.

choices.text: Send {npc} home, as the treaty says

effects.log: {npc} goes home. The disciples are quiet for days. A jar of pickled plums arrives in autumn.

choices.text: Send {npc} to fetch Granny, then come back

effects.log: {npc} comes back in a month with a ninety-year-old woman on a donkey and a cart of pickles.

events.text: {npc} has become one of your best disciples, and today stands before the council to be raised to inner disciple. One elder objects: a former enemy, raised so high? {npc} waits, quite still, as on the first day in the cell.
events.arc: The Prisoner Who Wanted to Stay

choices.text: Speak for {npc} before the council

effects.log: You speak briefly. The council raises {npc}, and the old objector is the first to bow.

choices.text: Let {npc} answer the elder alone

ok.log: {npc} answers so well that the elder laughs and withdraws the objection.

fail.log: {npc} answers badly and is raised anyway, by one vote.

choices.text: Delay a year, to be safe

effects.log: {npc} bows, and waits another year without a word of complaint.

events.text: {sw_foe} hold eleven of your disciples. You hold nine of theirs. Their envoy proposes an exchange at the Moon Bridge at dawn, all at once, both sides walking across the middle. Your elders are counting on their fingers and pointing out that eleven is more than nine.

choices.text: Accept, and add two sacks of rice to make up the difference

effects.log: The envoy laughs. "Rice for disciples. Agreed." Dawn is set.

choices.text: Insist on one at a time, slowly

effects.log: The envoy agrees, with a sigh. It will take all morning.

choices.text: Refuse: you want all eleven for nine

effects.log: The envoy goes away. Your eleven stay where they are.

events.text: Dawn at the Moon Bridge. Both lines stand at each end. The prisoners start walking. Halfway across, one of the enemy's prisoners, a skinny youth, stops dead and refuses to go on. On the other side, one of yours has done the same. They are looking at each other.

choices.text: Walk out onto the bridge yourself

effects.log: You walk to the middle. The enemy leader does the same. Two leaders, two stubborn prisoners, one bridge.

choices.text: Shout to your disciple to keep walking

effects.log: Your disciple walks on. The skinny youth, alone in the middle, starts crying, then goes home.

choices.text: Wait, and let them sort it out

effects.log: After a long time the two prisoners shake hands and go to their own sides. Everyone breathes.

events.text: Months later, after the peace, you learn what happened on the bridge. The two stubborn prisoners had been held in neighbouring cells for a year and become friends, and neither wanted the other to go back alone. They write to each other now, every month, and want to meet on the Moon Bridge again.

choices.text: Go with them and stand at your end

effects.log: Two sects stand at the ends of the Moon Bridge for a reason that is not war. It feels very strange.

choices.text: Give them leave and a jar of wine

effects.log: They meet on the bridge with a jar of wine and stay until moonrise.

choices.text: Pay to put a stone lantern in the middle of the bridge (60 taels)

effects.log: A stone lantern stands at the middle of the Moon Bridge now. People call it the Prisoners' Lamp.

events.text: Your raiders have come back with something you did not order: {npc}, sixteen, the only heir of {sw_leader}. {npc} sits in your guest room in torn silk, chin up, and informs you that {his} parent will burn your mountain to the ground. Your elders are delighted. You are not sure you are.

choices.text: Treat {npc} as an honoured guest

effects.log: {npc} is given a clean room, good food and books. The heir eats the food and ignores the books.

choices.text: Send a demand: the war ends, or the heir stays

effects.log: The message goes. The reply is a single word: "Wait."

choices.text: Send {npc} back at once, unharmed

effects.log: {npc} rides home on your best horse, confused and furious. The enemy does not know what to make of it.

events.text: {npc} has been on your mountain for some months. The heir has started training in your yard at dawn, alone, and correcting your disciples' stances, rudely and accurately. Today {npc} asks you a question nobody else has dared: "Why did you not ransom me?"

choices.text: Tell the truth: you do not want to win that way

effects.log: {npc} stares at you, then laughs. "My parent would have," says the heir, very quietly.

choices.text: Say that the price is not yet right

effects.log: {npc} goes cold, and stops training in your yard.

choices.text: Offer {npc} a sparring match instead of an answer

effects.log: You spar at dawn. {npc} is very good, and nearly wins.

events.text: Peace has come. {npc} goes home as part of it, riding down the mountain with your disciples lining the road. At the bottom the heir stops, turns the horse and rides back up to you. "When I lead my sect," says {npc}, "there will be no war between us. I promise it on my name."

choices.text: Accept the promise

effects.log: {npc} rides away. Years later, when the heir leads that sect, the promise holds.

choices.text: Tell {npc} not to promise what no one can keep

effects.log: {npc} smiles. "Then I will try." It is a better promise.

choices.text: Give {npc} a gift: the sword from your training yard

effects.log: {npc} takes the plain practice sword like a treasure.

events.text: News from the old enemy mountain: the sect's leader has fallen ill, and the heir now speaks for the sect at its council. The first thing the heir does is send you a letter, in a proud, careful hand, that says only: "I am trying."

choices.text: Send your best physician

effects.log: Your physician rides out in the night. The heir writes again: "Thank you. Still trying."

choices.text: Reply: so am I

effects.log: Two letters, two lines. Between the two mountains, the peace holds for a generation.

choices.text: Use the moment to demand the old tea gardens back

effects.log: Their council gives up the gardens. The heir's letters stop.

events.text: {sw_foe} have taken seven of your disciples prisoner in a skirmish and are holding them in a mountain fort called the Iron Hat. Their price is high: you call off the attack. Your elders say seven is a small price for victory. The seven are all under twenty.
events.arc: Seven of Ours in Their Cells

choices.text: Plan a rescue

effects.log: You spread a map of the Iron Hat on the table. The elders shake their heads, but they lean in.

choices.text: Pay a ransom in silver instead (200 taels)

effects.log: The silver goes. Six disciples come back. The seventh, they say, will be released "later."

choices.text: Press on with the attack anyway

effects.log: The attack goes on. Behind the walls of the Iron Hat, seven disciples hear it.

events.text: A night at the foot of the Iron Hat. The fort's back wall is a cliff, and the cells are against it. One of your scouts, a climber called Lean Wu, offers to go up it with a rope. If it works, the seven come down the cliff one by one, in the dark.
events.arc: Seven of Ours in Their Cells

choices.text: Climb with Lean Wu yourself

ok.log: You and Wu reach the cells. Seven disciples come down the rope, one by one, white as paper.

fail.log: You slip, and Wu catches you. You get four out before the alarm.

choices.text: Send Lean Wu alone, with a signal lamp

effects.log: Wu climbs alone. In the third hour a lamp flashes three times. They are coming down.

choices.text: Go to the gate and offer yourself for them

effects.log: You walk to the gate. They let the prisoners go, then lock you in instead, for nine days, until the peace.

events.text: After the war, the disciples who came back from the Iron Hat ask to see you together. They have been talking, and they want to thank you. They also want to know whether, in your place, any of them would have done the same.
events.arc: Seven of Ours in Their Cells

choices.text: Tell them honestly that you nearly did not

effects.log: There is a long silence. Then the eldest of them says, "Thank you for nearly."

choices.text: Tell them a sect is its people, not its battles

effects.log: They bow. They will say it to their own disciples one day.

choices.text: Ask about the one who was held longer

effects.log: The last of them came home in the spring, thin and silent. They all go to visit.

events.text: Among the prisoners from {sw_foe} is a plump young man in very good silk, who keeps asking for tea and explaining that his uncle owns half the silk shops in the capital. His uncle has sent a letter offering a ransom so large that your treasurer had to sit down.

choices.text: Accept the ransom

effects.log: The ransom arrives in four chests. The nephew goes home in a palanquin, complaining about the cell.

choices.text: Ask what the nephew was doing in the enemy sect

effects.log: "Learning the sword," he says. "My uncle wanted me to be tough." He is not tough.

choices.text: Release him free, as a gesture

effects.log: He goes home free. His uncle writes a very confused letter of thanks.

events.text: The silk merchant himself, Uncle Zhou, comes up your mountain in person. A short, busy man with eyes like an abacus. He wants to know what kind of sect you are, and why his nephew talks about you as if you were a hero from an opera.

choices.text: Give him the tour

effects.log: Zhou sees everything and asks the price of everything. At the end he says, "Hm. Honest."

choices.text: Offer to take the nephew as a disciple

effects.log: Zhou thinks about it for a long moment. "Make him tough," he says. "I will pay."

choices.text: Ask Zhou to supply silk for the sect at cost

effects.log: Zhou agrees at once, which surprises you. "You let the boy go," he says. "That is a deal."

events.text: Some years later, the plump nephew is no longer plump. He has become a decent swordsman, if not a good one, and is about to take over his uncle's silk empire. He comes to you to ask for one last lesson, "about mercy, which you taught me without teaching me."

choices.text: Give him the lesson

effects.log: You talk all night. He goes down the mountain to run half the silk in the capital, very fairly.

choices.text: Tell him to go and find out himself

effects.log: He laughs, and goes. A bolt of the finest silk arrives every new year after.

choices.text: Ask him for a donation to the sect

effects.log: He gives twice what you ask. It costs you a little of the lesson, he says, smiling.

events.text: Twenty prisoners of {sw_foe} are kept in your old granary. In the confusion of the last battle, you gave them your word, in front of witnesses: if they laid down their swords, they would go home at the war's end, unharmed. Now your elders say that word was given in haste.

choices.text: Confirm the vow in front of the whole sect

effects.log: You repeat it in the courtyard, loudly. The prisoners hear it through the granary wall.

choices.text: Say nothing, and keep your options open

effects.log: Your elders nod. The prisoners watch you every time you pass.

choices.text: Withdraw the vow: a war-time promise

effects.log: The prisoners hear of it. That night none of them sleep, and nor do you.

events.text: The enemy has executed none of your people, but they have taken a village of yours and burned its granary. Your elders say the twenty prisoners should pay for it. The disciples who lost family in the village agree. They are standing outside the old granary door.

choices.text: Stand in front of the granary door yourself

effects.log: You stand at the door with your sword sheathed. Slowly, one by one, the disciples go home.

choices.text: Move the prisoners to a safer place, at night

effects.log: You move them before dawn. The angry disciples find an empty granary and a lot of questions.

choices.text: Let the elders decide

effects.log: The elders decide on extra labour for the prisoners, not worse. It is not your decision, and you are glad.

events.text: The war is over. The twenty prisoners walk out of the granary and down your mountain road, every one of them, as you promised. At the bottom, one of them, an old soldier, turns back and bows to the mountain. Then all twenty do.

choices.text: Bow back

effects.log: Twenty bows, one returned. Your disciples will argue for years about whether that was right.

choices.text: Send them off with rice for the road

effects.log: Twenty sacks of rice go down the road with them. The enemy sect hears of it.

choices.text: Watch them go in silence

effects.log: They go. Your word, at least, held.

events.text: One of the prisoners from {sw_foe} is a cook, captured with their supply train, a big cheerful man with a cleaver tattoo on his arm. After a week in your cells he sends a polite note to the kitchen: their rice is badly made, and he would be happy to show them how, if released into the kitchen under guard.

choices.text: Let him into the kitchen, under guard

effects.log: The guard watches him. He watches the rice. That night, the whole sect eats the best meal of the war.

choices.text: Refuse: he could poison everyone

effects.log: He sighs. "Fair," he writes. "But your rice is still terrible."

choices.text: Send your own cook to learn from him in the cell

effects.log: Your cook comes back from the cell with a notebook full of recipes and a new respect for the enemy.

events.text: Your disciples are now eating better than the enemy sect, and the enemy knows it, because their scouts can smell your kitchen. Your elders are worried about the prisoner. "He cooks for us," one says. "Who does he cook against?"

choices.text: Ask the cook which side he is on

effects.log: "The side that eats," says the cook, stirring. "Everybody eats."

choices.text: Send a pot of his stew to the enemy camp

effects.log: The stew goes over to the enemy. A white flag comes back with the empty pot.

choices.text: Return him to the cells

effects.log: The rice is terrible again. Your disciples blame you, loudly.

events.text: Peace. The prisoner-cook is free to go. He stands in your kitchen doorway with his bundle, looking at the stove. Your own cook is standing next to him, very quiet, holding a ladle as if it were a sword.

choices.text: Offer him a job in your kitchen

effects.log: He stays. Your kitchen becomes famous. The enemy sect complains about this for years.

choices.text: Let him go home with a recipe book (20 taels)

effects.log: He goes home with a fine book and a bag of your mountain's pepper.

choices.text: Let your cook decide

effects.log: Your cook hugs him at the door, says "Never come back", and cries for a day.

events.text: The most valuable prisoner you hold is {npc}, seventy-one, a senior elder of {sw_foe}, captured in a skirmish at the river. {npc} has asked for only one thing in the cell: a weiqi board. Today the old elder invites you to play. "One game," says {npc}. "Then you may ask me anything."

choices.text: Play, and try to win

effects.log: You lose badly. {npc} smiles. "Ask anyway."

choices.text: Play, and watch how {npc} plays

effects.log: {npc} plays like a general: patient, then sudden. You learn more about the enemy than any spy could tell you.

choices.text: Refuse: you are not here to play games

effects.log: {npc} shrugs and plays against {him}self all night.

events.text: You have played forty games with {npc} now, losing thirty-nine. The fortieth you won, and you are not sure whether the old elder let you. Today {npc} says the enemy's leader is planning a reckless attack, and the old elder thinks it will be a slaughter, on both sides.

choices.text: Ask {npc} why tell you this

effects.log: "Because I have taught you weiqi," says {npc}, "and you can see the board now."

choices.text: Prepare for the attack quietly

effects.log: You prepare. When the attack comes, it breaks on your lines, and fewer die than anyone feared.

choices.text: Send {npc} home to stop it

effects.log: {npc} goes home. The attack does not come. Neither does the old elder again.

events.text: The war is over. A small parcel arrives from the enemy mountain: a weiqi board, very old, and a single black stone with a note. "For the fortieth game. You did win it." The note is signed by {npc}.

choices.text: Write back, with a move

effects.log: You send one white stone. A black one comes back in a month. The game takes eleven years.

choices.text: Visit {npc} on the enemy mountain

effects.log: You climb the enemy's mountain, unarmed. {npc} has set up the board already.

choices.text: Put the board in the sect hall

effects.log: The old board sits in your hall, where the disciples argue over it every evening.

events.text: The long game by letter has reached move two hundred and eleven when the black stones stop coming. A messenger from the enemy mountain arrives instead, bowing deeply. The old elder has died in sleep, the messenger says, and left you the next move.

choices.text: Play the move, and leave the board as it is

effects.log: You place one white stone. The board stays unfinished in your hall, forever.

choices.text: Go to the funeral on the enemy mountain

effects.log: You climb the enemy's mountain in white. They let you stand among the elders.

choices.text: Teach a young disciple to finish the game for both

effects.log: The disciple plays both sides for a year, and finishes it in a draw.

events.text: Three prisoners of {sw_foe} have escaped in the night, and the cell door was not broken: it was unlocked. The guard on duty, an earnest young disciple named Su Yue, is standing in front of you now, pale as rice paper, and has not yet said a word.
events.arc: The Night the Cell Door Was Open

choices.text: Ask Su Yue to tell the truth

effects.log: "One of them was my cousin," says Su Yue. "I did not know until the second night."

choices.text: Send the trackers out after the three

effects.log: The trackers bring back two. The third, the youngest, is gone.

choices.text: Have Su Yue locked in the empty cell

effects.log: Su Yue goes into the cell without a word. The door is locked, properly this time.

events.text: Your elders want Su Yue expelled, for letting enemy prisoners go during a war. It is the law of the sect. Su Yue is sitting in the hall with head bowed, waiting to hear, and the cousin is somewhere on the road, safe.
events.arc: The Night the Cell Door Was Open

choices.text: Speak for Su Yue in front of the elders

effects.log: You speak for an hour. The elders give Su Yue a year of hard labour instead of expulsion.

choices.text: Let the law stand: expel Su Yue

effects.log: Su Yue goes down the mountain. The disciples who watch it are quiet for days.

choices.text: Punish Su Yue lightly yourself, before the elders can

effects.log: Su Yue scrubs pots for a season, which everybody agrees is the real punishment.

events.text: Peace. A letter arrives for Su Yue from the enemy mountain, from the cousin. The cousin has been made an elder there and wants to visit, to thank Su Yue, and to bring you a gift, "for not chasing me very hard."
events.arc: The Night the Cell Door Was Open

choices.text: Welcome the cousin

effects.log: The cousin arrives with a box of sweets and many apologies. Su Yue cries for an hour.

choices.text: Tell Su Yue to meet the cousin at the border instead

effects.log: They meet at the border. You get the box of sweets anyway.

choices.text: Refuse: the war is too close yet

effects.log: Su Yue reads your answer and says nothing.

events.text: You wake to find two wounded martial artists in your barn, one in green robes, one in black, from two sects at war in the hills. They are both too hurt to fight, and are lying on opposite sides of the hay, glaring at each other. Your goat is standing between them like a judge.

choices.text: Bandage both of them

effects.log: You bandage them both. Neither says thank you. Both eat your porridge.

choices.text: Send for the village physician (30 taels)

effects.log: The physician comes, sees the robes, and charges you double for nerves.

choices.text: Leave them to it, and lock the barn

effects.log: You lock the barn and go to work. When you get back, they are both still alive and still glaring.

events.text: Three days on, the two wounded fighters are well enough to argue, and they do, all day, about whose sect started the war. Your goat has eaten the green one's sash. The black one finds this hilarious. Search parties from both sects are now riding through the village.

choices.text: Hide them both, together

effects.log: The search parties ride past. In the barn, the two fighters hold their breath side by side.

choices.text: Tell both search parties at once, at the same time

effects.log: Both search parties arrive in your yard at once. Nobody wants to fight in front of a goat.

choices.text: Hand them to their own sides quietly, one at a time

effects.log: The green one goes at noon, the black one at dusk. Neither looks back.

events.text: A year later, two riders come to your farm, one in green, one in black. The war is over. They have brought you a goat, a fine young one, to replace the sash, they say, and a pouch of silver, and they want to know if you would mind if they sat together a while in your barn.

choices.text: Open the barn and bring the wine

effects.log: The two of them drink in your barn all night, laughing, while the goats watch.

choices.text: Take the silver and the goat, and wish them well

effects.log: The goat is very handsome. The silver is generous.

choices.text: Ask them to teach you a little of each art

effects.log: They teach you a little of each, arguing about which is better, all summer.

events.text: A long column of prisoners from the great war between {war_a} and {war_b} passes along the road by your home, guarded by tired riders. The prisoners are thin and roped together. One of them, a girl of sixteen, falls in the dust right in front of your gate.

choices.text: Bring her water

effects.log: You bring water. A guard shouts, then sees the girl's face and lets it go.

choices.text: Offer the guards silver to let her rest (30 taels)

effects.log: The guards take the silver and give the whole column an hour's rest in the shade.

choices.text: Close your gate

effects.log: You close the gate. You hear the column pass for a long time.

events.text: That night someone knocks at your back door. It is the girl from the column, rope burns on her wrists, shaking. She slipped away when the guards were drinking. She asks for nothing but a place to sleep before she runs again.

choices.text: Hide her in the loft

effects.log: She sleeps for two days straight. When the riders search the village, they do not search your loft.

choices.text: Give her food and an old coat, and send her on

effects.log: She goes before dawn with your coat and half your bread.

choices.text: Turn her over to the guards

effects.log: The guards thank you and take her away. They give you a small reward, which you cannot spend.

events.text: Years after the great war, a letter arrives at your house from a sect far in the south. Its new elder writes that she was once a prisoner in a column on your road, and that she has named the sect's guesthouse after you. Inside the letter is a pressed flower from your own garden.

choices.text: Write back to her

effects.log: She writes back for twenty years. You never meet, and it never matters.

choices.text: Travel south to visit her sect

effects.log: You travel a month south. She meets you at the gate and bows lower than any elder should.

choices.text: Keep the flower and say nothing

effects.log: The pressed flower sits on your shelf. You take it down sometimes.

events.text: Neither righteous nor demonic, {sect} answers to nobody, which means nobody comes to help now that {sw_foe} are at your gates. Your banner-bearer, Old Kang, has just discovered the sect's battle banner was eaten by moths in storage. What remains looks like a red fishing net.

choices.text: Charge under the moth-eaten banner anyway

effects.log: You charge under what looks like a net. The enemy laughs, and then stops laughing.

choices.text: Fly the banner on the wall as a decoy and strike from the side

effects.log: They aim everything at the holey banner on the wall. You hit them from the other side.

choices.text: Challenge {sw_leader} under no banner at all

ok.log: You win without a banner. That night, the disciples decide you are the banner.

fail.log: You lose, and Old Kang drapes the moth-eaten banner over you as you are carried back.
fail.deathCause: a duel with the leader of an enemy sect, in a sect war

choices.text: Send the ruined banner as a white flag, since it is mostly holes anyway

effects.log: The enemy is confused by the flag, then laughs, then agrees to talk.

events.text: After the battle, Old Kang wants to make a new banner, and the sect's tailors want to make it beautiful. Kang wants to keep the old one, holes and all, and sew it into the new one. The tailors are appalled.

choices.text: Let Kang sew the old into the new

effects.log: The new banner has a ragged red heart. The tailors refuse to take credit.

choices.text: Let the tailors make it beautiful (60 taels)

effects.log: The new banner is magnificent, silk and gold. Kang folds the old one away.

choices.text: Fly no banner at all from now on

effects.log: Your sect fights under no flag. Some sects find this alarming, which is useful.

events.text: Old Kang has died in the winter, at ninety, with the banner folded at the foot of the bed. The disciples want to bury the old banner-bearer with it. Others say it belongs to the sect.

choices.text: Bury Kang with a piece of the old banner

effects.log: A strip of moth-eaten red goes into the ground with Kang. The rest flies on.

choices.text: Fly the banner at half mast for a month

effects.log: The banner flies low for a month. Even the merchants on the road take off their hats.

choices.text: Make the youngest disciple the new banner-bearer

effects.log: The youngest disciple carries the banner proudly, and trips over it twice.

events.text: The war is lost. {sect} has given up a valley and the old tea gardens as the price of peace. Your disciples come home with their heads down, and in the hall there are empty places at the long table. The kitchen has set out bowls for everyone anyway, out of habit, and no one has the heart to clear them.

choices.text: Leave the bowls, and eat beside them

effects.log: You eat in silence beside the empty bowls. One by one the others sit down too.

choices.text: Hold a lantern night for the fallen

effects.log: Paper lanterns rise over the mountain, one for each. The whole valley watches them go.

choices.text: Order the hall cleared, and training resumed

effects.log: The bowls are cleared. Training starts at dawn. Nobody speaks of it.

events.text: A month after the defeat, a young disciple named Chen Gao comes to you. Chen's elder brother fell in the war, and Chen wants to leave the sect. "Not because of the defeat," Chen says. "Because I cannot see the empty bowl every night."

choices.text: Ask Chen to stay one more season, and set the table with you

effects.log: Chen stays. Every evening the two of you set the empty bowls together. In spring, Chen can bear it.

choices.text: Give Chen leave, with silver for the road (50 taels)

effects.log: Chen goes home to the family farm with your silver and a letter. It is the right road.

choices.text: Tell Chen to become strong enough that it never happens again

effects.log: Chen trains like fury. It does not help the grief, but it helps the sect.

events.text: A year after the defeat, the empty places at the table are filled by new disciples, who do not know who sat there. One evening a new girl asks who used to sit in her seat.

choices.text: Tell her the name, and the story

effects.log: You tell her about the disciple who sat there. She sits a little straighter after.

choices.text: Have the names carved on the long table

effects.log: Every seat carries a small carved name now. New disciples learn them by the end of their first year.

choices.text: Tell her it does not matter: it is her seat now

effects.log: She nods and eats. Life moves on, as it must.

events.text: The Plum Rain Alliance meets on your mountain for its tenth-year banquet: three sect masters, forty guests, and one round table that is round only in theory, since whoever faces the gate is senior. Your steward has redrawn the seating chart eleven times and is now sitting on the kitchen step holding the twelfth.

choices.text: Sit facing the gate yourself: it is your mountain

effects.log: You take the gate seat. Two sect masters smile the way cats smile at a closed door.

choices.text: Give the gate seat to old Sect Master Lu of the Azure Pine

effects.log: Lu accepts it with a long, slow look at you, as if reading a letter twice.

choices.text: Replace the round table with three square ones, side by side

effects.log: Nobody is senior and everybody is offended equally. The steward weeps with relief.

events.text: Halfway through the duck, Sect Master Lu raises a cup and toasts "the youngest sect at this table, which has grown so fast one wonders what it fed on." The hall goes quiet. Lu's disciples watch your hands, and Iron Gourd Han, the third master, eats a duck leg very slowly.

choices.text: Toast back: "On rice, and on other people's insults."

effects.log: The hall laughs, Han loudest of all. Lu laughs last, but does laugh.

choices.text: Answer with an impromptu poem that turns the barb into praise

ok.log: Four lines about a young pine in an old forest. Lu sets down the cup and bows from the seat.

fail.log: The poem loses its way in the third line. Han kindly coughs over the fourth.

choices.text: Remind Lu, quietly, who is sitting facing the gate

effects.log: Lu goes pale and drinks the toast alone. Nobody at the table forgets it.

choices.text: Set down your cup and walk out of your own banquet

effects.log: You leave forty guests with the duck. The story is told in three provinces by spring.

events.text: A year later the Azure Pine is raided by a cult band and writes to the alliance for help. Lu's letter is polite and very short. Iron Gourd Han has already answered that his disciples are busy with the harvest, which is true, and also convenient.

choices.text: Send thirty disciples at once, under your best elder

effects.log: Your disciples hold the Azure Pine gate for nine days. Lu writes a much longer letter afterwards.

choices.text: Go yourself: Lu once accepted your seat with grace

effects.log: Lu meets you at the gate in person. At every banquet after, the gate seat is yours, by Lu's own order.

choices.text: Send rice and medicine but no swords (100 taels)

effects.log: The carts arrive safely. Lu's thanks are correct, and cool.

choices.text: Answer as Lu toasted: the young sect is still growing

effects.log: You do not go. The Azure Pine survives without you, and remembers how.

events.text: The next tenth-year banquet comes round. Your steward, older and calmer, brings the seating chart to you on one sheet, already drawn. At its centre, where the gate seat used to be, there is a small square table for one, with a question mark on it in very neat ink.

choices.text: Put old Lu in the question-mark seat, as a guest of honour

effects.log: Lu sits there laughing, and toasts the youngest sect at the table, this time without a barb.

choices.text: Sit there yourself, alone, as host

effects.log: You eat your duck at the centre of the hall. It is splendid, and slightly lonely.

choices.text: Put the steward there

effects.log: The steward refuses, then accepts, then eats more duck than anyone. The whole alliance drinks to the seating chart.

events.text: Sect Master Qiao of the River Bell Sect proposes a sworn pact: incense on the peak, three bows, the old words. "We were not born on the same day," Qiao says, "but we may as well fall on the same one." The River Bell is small, poor, and has the best healers in the province.

choices.text: Swear the full oath on the peak, words and all

effects.log: Incense, three bows, the old words. Qiao's eyes are wet, and so, a little, are yours.

choices.text: Offer a trade pact instead: healers for swords, in writing

effects.log: Qiao signs it with a sigh. "Paper," Qiao says, "does not catch cold."

choices.text: Decline, politely

effects.log: Qiao bows, unoffended. "A careful sect lives long," Qiao says, and leaves you a jar of fever pills anyway.

events.text: A River Bell messenger arrives at midnight: Qiao has quarrelled with the Iron Jaw Hall over a ford and means to fight. Qiao's letter quotes the oath and underlines the part about falling together. The ford, your scouts report, was always Iron Jaw's.

choices.text: Keep the oath: march with Qiao, even in the wrong

effects.log: Your disciples stand at the ford beside the River Bell. Iron Jaw withdraws, and hates you both.

choices.text: Ride to Qiao and argue through the night

ok.log: Qiao listens until dawn, then sends the swords home and buys the ford fishing rights instead.

fail.log: Qiao listens, thanks you warmly, and marches anyway.

choices.text: Send what the paper promises: swords for defence, none for attack

effects.log: Your letter is exact. Qiao reads it twice and does not attack.

choices.text: Send nothing

effects.log: Silence goes down the mountain. The River Bell hears it clearly.

events.text: Winter brings a fever to your disciples' halls: eleven down in a week, and your physician is out of ideas. Down in the valley the River Bell keeps the best healers in the province, and they remember the business at the ford, one way or another.

choices.text: Send for Qiao's healers

effects.log: They come through a snowstorm and refuse payment. Qiao sits by the sickbeds all night, humming.

choices.text: Write to the River Bell and offer to pay (80 taels)

effects.log: Two healers arrive with a bill and good medicine. Every disciple recovers.

choices.text: Nurse them yourself, from the old medical manuals

ok.log: You boil roots for nine nights and every disciple wakes. You learn more than any manual says.

fail.log: Nine of the eleven recover. You write the other two names on the hall's tablet yourself.

events.text: Qiao dies in old age, peacefully, in the spring. The River Bell sends you the oath incense burner from the peak, with a note in Qiao's own shaky hand, written weeks before: "Same year, same month, same day was too much to ask. Come to the funeral on time instead."

choices.text: Go to the funeral and stand with the River Bell disciples

effects.log: You stand at the graveside among healers in white. Afterwards they treat you as one of their own elders.

choices.text: Light the incense on the peak alone, at the hour of the funeral

effects.log: The smoke goes straight up. You say the old words once more, to nobody, to Qiao.

choices.text: Send your best disciples to carry the coffin

effects.log: Your disciples carry Qiao down the valley road. The River Bell never forgets it.

events.text: {sw_foe} are camped at the foot of your mountain and the signal fires have burned three nights. The Cloud Ridge Sect swore to come at the third fire. The ridge road stays empty, except for one rider on a grey mule: Cloud Ridge's envoy {npc}, with a letter and a very apologetic face.

choices.text: Read the letter aloud before your elders

effects.log: Cloud Ridge regrets. Cloud Ridge has its own troubles. Cloud Ridge sends a jar of pickles.

choices.text: Hold {npc} at the gate until the war is decided

effects.log: {npc} is given a room, a guard and the pickles. The envoy does not complain once.

choices.text: Send {npc} back with a single word: remembered

effects.log: {npc} bows very low and rides away. The mule, at least, seems relieved.

events.text: The war is over and the letter has been read until it is soft. Cloud Ridge claims its own gate was threatened that month. {npc}, at the end of a long evening, says quietly that the Cloud Ridge master was at a birthday banquet, and that the road was clear the whole time.

choices.text: Break the alliance publicly, at the next sect gathering

effects.log: You read the letter aloud again, this time to nine sects. Cloud Ridge's seat at gatherings stays empty a long while.

choices.text: Demand compensation for every disciple you lost (gain)

effects.log: Cloud Ridge pays quickly and quietly, which is its own confession.

choices.text: Ask {npc} to leave Cloud Ridge and join your mountain

effects.log: {npc} looks at the floor a long time, then nods. "I carried that letter," the envoy says. "I would rather carry something else."

events.text: Three years on, Cloud Ridge itself is besieged, and writes to you for help in a letter that quotes old friendships at great length. Nobody on your mountain needs it read aloud. Everyone looks, for some reason, at the jar of pickles on the shelf.

choices.text: Ask {npc} to choose what to answer

effects.log: {npc} writes the answer: twenty disciples, sent at the second fire, not the third. Cloud Ridge understands perfectly.

choices.text: Send help at once: someone has to be better than this

effects.log: Your disciples arrive before the siege closes. The Cloud Ridge master cannot look at you for a year.

choices.text: Send them a jar of pickles

effects.log: The pickles are delivered at the third fire. It is the most quoted joke in the province for a decade.

events.text: The Jade Spring Sect, your oldest ally, writes after the autumn flood: their granary is under the river and they have sixty disciples to feed through winter. They ask for three hundred taels of grain. Your own granary, your steward reports, has exactly enough for your own mountain, plus one optimistic sack.

choices.text: Send it all (300 taels)

effects.log: Thirty carts roll down to the Jade Spring. Your steward counts the sacks left and stops talking to you.

choices.text: Send half, with a letter explaining why (150 taels)

effects.log: Half the grain and a long, honest letter. The Jade Spring thanks you for both.

choices.text: Send forty disciples to rebuild their dykes instead

effects.log: Your disciples haul stones all autumn. Jade Spring will be dry next year, if hungry this one.

choices.text: Refuse, with every apology you can write

effects.log: The apology is beautifully brushed. The Jade Spring keeps it, and does not answer.

events.text: Winter comes early and hard. Your own rice jars are scraped by the twelfth month, and a junior steward suggests, very carefully, selling the old bronze bell that has called your disciples to practice since the founding.

choices.text: Sell the bell

effects.log: A merchant takes it down the mountain on an ox cart. Mornings are very quiet now.

choices.text: Cut every ration by a third, your own first

effects.log: Everyone is hungry, and nobody can say you were not. The disciples grumble less than you feared.

choices.text: Write to the Jade Spring for whatever they can spare

effects.log: Ten carts of firewood come up the road, with a note: "It is not rice, but it is warm."

choices.text: Hunt the forest with your disciples

effects.log: Your disciples learn to track deer in the snow. It is not a technique, but they eat.

events.text: Two springs later the Jade Spring Sect has new granaries and a new master, young Shen, who rides up your mountain with a cart and a long face. The cart holds a bronze bell, or a box of silver, or nothing at all, depending, it seems, on what you did in the flood year.

choices.text: Receive the bell: Shen bought it back from the merchant

effects.log: The bell is hung again, and rings at dawn. Shen stays a week and drills with your disciples.

choices.text: Receive the silver, and Shen's renewed pact

effects.log: Shen repays the grain with interest and signs the old alliance afresh.

choices.text: Receive Shen's thanks for the dykes

effects.log: "The river came again this year," Shen says, "and stopped at your stones."

choices.text: Receive Shen, who has come only to say goodbye to the alliance

effects.log: Shen is courteous and brief. The Jade Spring finds other friends, and you find out who yours are.

events.text: The Golden Bell Sect arrives to share your defence against {sw_foe}: sixty disciples, two war drums and a strong opinion about whose drum is louder. By evening they have built their own wall twenty paces in front of yours, so that they will be first to fall. They seem very pleased about it.

choices.text: Merge the two walls into one, and the drums into one rhythm

effects.log: It takes a night of shouting. By dawn there is one wall and one drumbeat, and nobody can say whose.

choices.text: Let them hold the front wall: guests have their pride

effects.log: The Golden Bell stands first. They are proud, and brave, and too far forward.

choices.text: Give them the east gate, the hardest post on the mountain

effects.log: The Golden Bell master bows deeply. It is the greatest honour you could offer, and both of you know the price.

events.text: The war is over. Between the two walls, where the worst of it fell, someone has planted white chrysanthemums. The Golden Bell's eldest drummer, Old Wen, did not come home, and the great drum has been left on your mountain with a note: it should stay where its drummer stayed.

choices.text: Hang the drum in your hall and beat it every year on that day

effects.log: Once a year the mountain hears Old Wen's drum. The Golden Bell sends a drummer for it, every year.

choices.text: Carry the drum home to the Golden Bell yourself

effects.log: You walk four days with it on your back. The Golden Bell disciples meet you on the road in silence.

choices.text: Build a small shrine at the east gate

effects.log: A shrine of grey stone, with Old Wen's name first. The gate is never called the east gate again, only Wen's Gate.

events.text: Old Wen's granddaughter, now master of the Golden Bell, climbs your mountain on the anniversary. She has founded a new hall, she says, and wants it opened properly: someone who stood on the walls must beat its first drum.

choices.text: Beat her new drum, and play Old Wen's rhythm

effects.log: Your arms remember it. Half the Golden Bell weeps, and the other half pretends to have dust in their eyes.

choices.text: Go and beat it, badly, with all your heart

effects.log: The rhythm is wrong and the drum forgives it. The new master laughs for the first time that day.

choices.text: Send your best young drummer in your place

effects.log: Your disciple comes home a week later engaged to a Golden Bell drummer. The alliance is now, apparently, family.

events.text: As a pledge of the new alliance, Sect Master Pei of the Ninefold Cloud sends the heir, {npc}, to live on your mountain for three years. {npc} arrives with two trunks, a zither, and an opinion about your food that is shared, at length, with the cook.

choices.text: Train {npc} exactly like any other disciple

effects.log: {npc} carries water at dawn with everyone else and complains in a whisper. By winter the whisper stops.

choices.text: Treat {npc} as an honoured guest

effects.log: {npc} has the best room and the best tea, and is bored within a month.

choices.text: Set {npc} to copy manuals in the library

effects.log: {npc} has a beautiful hand and no patience. Your library gains three manuals and many ink blots.

events.text: At midnight a watchman finds {npc} halfway down the north wall on a rope of knotted bedsheets. {He} is not running away, the heir insists: letters from home stopped in spring, and nobody will say why.

choices.text: Ride out together at first light to find out

effects.log: You ride three days with {npc} at your side, saying little. The Ninefold Cloud gate is draped in white.

choices.text: Lock the gate, and send your own rider to ask

effects.log: Your rider returns in a week with the news, and {npc} hears it from you, not from a stranger.

choices.text: Send {npc} home alone with an escort

effects.log: {npc} goes before dawn. The pledge is broken, but nobody on your mountain blames the heir for it.

events.text: Sect Master Pei died of a winter fever, quietly, and the Ninefold Cloud elders have kept it hidden while they quarrelled. Now {npc} must go home and lead them, at an age when most disciples are still learning to stand in a horse stance.

choices.text: Give {npc} your own sword for the road

effects.log: {npc} holds the sword the way you taught. "I will send it back," {he} says, "when I have earned my own."

choices.text: Send ten of your disciples to stand behind {npc} the first year

effects.log: Ten of your disciples stand at the back of every Ninefold Cloud council. The elders stop quarrelling remarkably fast.

choices.text: Ask {npc} to swear the alliance anew, as master now

effects.log: {npc} swears it on your mountain, with the zither in one hand. It is the shortest oath and the most sincere you have heard.

choices.text: Simply walk {npc} to the gate

effects.log: At the gate {npc} bows, then turns back to complain about the food one last time. You will miss it.

events.text: The sect master sends you, as an elder, to the Tiger Brook Sect to renew a forty-year alliance. Tiger Brook's new master reads the treaty, smiles, and crosses out one word with a fat brush: "equal". In its place is written "elder and younger". Tiger Brook, of course, is the elder.

choices.text: Sign: words are cheap and swords are not

effects.log: You sign. The Tiger Brook master pours you tea with great warmth.

choices.text: Refuse, and carry the treaty home unsigned

effects.log: You bow and leave. The Tiger Brook gate shuts behind you a little loudly.

choices.text: Find the founding clause in their own archive that names your sect the elder

ok.log: There it is, in the founder's hand: your sect lent them their first sword manual. The new master signs "equal" with a sour face.

fail.log: Their archive is chaos and their archivist is deaf. You sign the original treaty unchanged, by luck rather than skill.

events.text: Back home, the sect master hears the story in silence, then asks the question elders dread: what would you have done, if the choice had been yours alone? The other elders lean forward to listen, and somebody's tea goes cold.

choices.text: Say you signed for peace, and would again

effects.log: The sect master nods slowly. "Peace is a word," the master says, "that Tiger Brook will now spell for us."

choices.text: Say you would have refused, and did

effects.log: Two elders frown, one smiles. The sect master writes something in a small book.

choices.text: Say a younger sect that knows it is younger lives longer

effects.log: The hall goes quiet. The sect master laughs, once. "Write that down," the master says to a disciple.

choices.text: Say nothing, and bow

effects.log: Your silence is noted. Elders who say nothing rarely get sent anywhere again.

events.text: Two years on, Tiger Brook is drawn into a feud and sends for its "younger" ally's disciples, citing the very word on the treaty, twice, in large characters. The sect master hands you the letter without comment and waits.

choices.text: Go: a younger sect obeys its elder, as signed

effects.log: Your disciples fight Tiger Brook's feud and come home tired and thanked. The word costs you every year now.

choices.text: Answer that equals choose their own wars

effects.log: Tiger Brook rages for a season, then sends an envoy about a new treaty, with the word "equal" already in it.

choices.text: Go as a mediator, not a soldier

effects.log: You sit down with both feuding masters over tea. It ends with a fishing contract and one broken teapot.

choices.text: Advise the sect master to let the alliance quietly lapse

effects.log: The alliance ends with no letter at all. Tiger Brook finds a younger sect elsewhere.

events.text: Years later the sect master retires and the elders gather to name a successor. Somebody unrolls the old Tiger Brook treaty and points at the single crossed-out word, which has become a kind of joke on the mountain. It is a test, of course, and they are all looking at you.

choices.text: Say the word still matters

effects.log: The elders nod slowly. You are not chosen, but you are asked to write the next treaty.

choices.text: Say no word matters as much as the sword behind it

effects.log: Half the elders approve, half are alarmed. It is discussed for a month.

choices.text: Laugh, and cross the word out again

effects.log: The hall laughs with you. The new sect master keeps the treaty on the wall, with both crossings.

events.text: You asked the Five Peaks Sect for fifty swords against {sw_foe}. Two hundred come, with tents, cooks, and a sect master who calls your lower valley "lovely farmland" twice before dinner. They fight superbly, which makes it harder to say anything.
events.arc: The Ally Who Came Too Well

choices.text: Welcome every one of them and say nothing yet

effects.log: The Five Peaks win you a battle that same week. Their cooks begin planting turnips.

choices.text: Thank them, and politely assign them the far ridge

effects.log: The Five Peaks camp on the far ridge, a long way from your farmland, and notice why.

choices.text: Ask for a written promise to leave when the war ends

effects.log: The Five Peaks master signs with a flourish and a small, private smile.

events.text: The war has been over a full season. The Five Peaks camp is now a village, with a well, a shrine and a market on the fifth day. Their master writes to propose "a shared valley, for our shared victory".
events.arc: The Ally Who Came Too Well

choices.text: Produce the written promise

effects.log: The Five Peaks master reads it, sighs, and orders the tents struck. The turnips are left to you as a gift.

choices.text: Out-argue the Five Peaks master before both sects

ok.log: By the end even their disciples are nodding. They leave in a month, singing.

fail.log: Their master quotes every battle they won for you. Your own disciples start to agree with them.

choices.text: Offer them the far ridge for good, as allies

effects.log: The Five Peaks keep the ridge and build a branch hall. You now have two hundred neighbours with swords.

choices.text: Pay them to leave (200 taels)

effects.log: They take the silver and go, saying fair is fair. It does not feel fair to anybody.

events.text: Years later, the valley is quiet. Some of the Five Peaks disciples who married local farmers stayed behind anyway, and their market day is now the busiest in the county. Your steward reports the market tax with a puzzled expression: it is good money.
events.arc: The Ally Who Came Too Well

choices.text: Tax the market and use it to feed your disciples

effects.log: Your granary fills from turnips you did not plant. The steward stops being puzzled.

choices.text: Invite the Five Peaks to the market's first anniversary

effects.log: Their master comes, eats your turnips and laughs. "We did conquer your valley," the master says, "only slowly."

choices.text: Make the far-ridge branch hall your formal ally

effects.log: The two halls sign a pact on market day, over turnip cakes.

events.text: The war is won. The banners come down, the drums are put away, and in the quiet that follows you notice how many sandals by the dormitory doors have nobody to wear them. Old Mason Hou climbs up from the valley with a cart of grey stone and asks one question: how many names?

choices.text: Every name, disciple and servant alike

effects.log: Hou counts on knotted fingers and nods. "Cooks die in wars too," the mason says.

choices.text: The fallen disciples, by rank, as tradition says

effects.log: Hou writes the list carefully. The kitchen staff read it and say nothing.

choices.text: Victory is the memorial: no stele

effects.log: Hou takes the cart back down. Every spring, someone leaves flowers by the gate anyway.

events.text: Hou has carved for a month when a grey-haired farmer arrives at the gate. Her son ran off to fight on the enemy side and fell on your slope. Nobody else will carve his name, she says, so she has come to the only mason who is carving.

choices.text: Let Hou add her son's name, on the back of the stone

effects.log: The farmer touches the new name for a long time. Some of your disciples are angry; some go quiet.

choices.text: Give her silver for a stone of her own (60 taels)

effects.log: She takes the silver with both hands and does not thank you. You understand.

choices.text: Refuse: the stone belongs to your dead

effects.log: She walks down the mountain alone. Hou watches her go and carves very slowly the rest of the day.

events.text: The stele is finished on a cold morning. The whole mountain stands before it while the incense burns, and the eldest surviving disciple asks you to speak. Hundreds of faces wait. Somewhere at the back, someone is already crying.

choices.text: Read every name aloud, slowly, one by one

effects.log: It takes most of the morning. Nobody leaves. When you finish, the incense is ash and the sun is up.

choices.text: Walk around and read the name on the back as well

effects.log: The disciples follow you round the stone. A long silence, and then a low bow, to both sides of it.

choices.text: Say only: "We remember."

effects.log: Two words, and then the bell. It is enough.

choices.text: Speak of each fallen disciple you knew well

ok.log: Laughter and tears together: a story about stolen dumplings, then one about a broken sword. The mountain grieves properly.

fail.log: Your voice breaks in the second story. An elder takes your arm, and the disciples love you more for it.

events.text: Every year on the anniversary, the stele draws more people: old disciples, widows, children grown up, villagers who sold rice to the sect in the war. This year Mason Hou does not climb the steps. The mason died in winter, and asked to be buried at the foot of the stone.

choices.text: Carve Hou's name on the stele, at the very bottom

effects.log: The newest name is the smallest. It is the only one carved by an apprentice, crooked and loving.

choices.text: Plant a pine at the foot of the stele for Hou

effects.log: The pine grows slowly, leaning a little towards the stone, as if reading it.

choices.text: Take Hou's chisels and finish the last line yourself

effects.log: Your letters are clumsy. The disciples say Hou would have laughed, and they are right.

events.text: The war is won, and the disciples have discovered swagger. Three of them were seen in the county town wearing their banners as capes, telling the noodle seller he should be honoured to feed the victors. The noodle seller, a very large man, did not agree.

choices.text: Send the three down to apologise, capes and all

effects.log: The three bow to the noodle seller in front of the whole street. He gives them free noodles out of pity.

choices.text: Laugh it off: let them have their glory a while

effects.log: The disciples swagger all autumn. The county begins to talk about "those people up the mountain".

choices.text: Make all three wash bowls at the noodle stall for a month

effects.log: The noodle seller is delighted. Two of the three learn to make noodles rather well.

events.text: A visiting swordsman, shabby and polite, asks to cross swords with your senior disciples. They line up laughing: they are victors, after all. The swordsman bows and puts four of them on the ground before the tea is even poured.

choices.text: Ask the swordsman to stay and teach for a season

effects.log: The swordsman stays, eats a great deal, and drills the swagger out of everyone.

choices.text: Draw your own sword and test the stranger

ok.log: A long, even bout. You win by a hair, and the stranger laughs and bows. The disciples are very quiet.

fail.log: You lose cleanly, and the disciples see it. Strangely, they swagger less after that.

choices.text: Remind the disciples of the noodle seller's bowls

effects.log: They quote the noodle seller back to each other all winter: "Victors still pay for noodles."

events.text: The next spring a rival sect sends spies to see how strong the victors truly are. Your informant in their hall brings back a copy of the spies' report. It is one line long, and it delights some of your elders and worries the rest.

choices.text: Read the report: "Proud, loud, and badly trained."

effects.log: Your elders begin a hard winter of drills. Pride can be repaired; tired muscles mend.

choices.text: Read the report: "Quiet, polite, dangerous."

effects.log: It is the best review your mountain has ever had. The rival sect stays home.

choices.text: Burn the report unread

effects.log: Whatever they think, they will find out the hard way. Your disciples train regardless.

events.text: The three disciples from the noodle-stall affair are senior disciples now. They come to you together with a request: they want to open a noodle stall of their own in the county town, under the sect's banner, staffed by the junior disciples on market days.

choices.text: Allow it: humility, with broth

effects.log: The stall is a great success. Juniors who serve noodles learn patience faster than any sword drill could teach.

choices.text: Refuse: a sect is not a kitchen

effects.log: The three bow and go back to their duties. The old noodle seller is privately relieved.

choices.text: Ask the old noodle seller to teach them first

effects.log: The noodle seller agrees, for a fee in compliments. The broth, when it comes, is excellent.

events.text: The enemy sect is gone, its gate burned and its disciples scattered. Only the library stands, a long hall of scroll shelves, and inside it one frail librarian who refuses to leave. "Take what you like," the old librarian says, "but you will not find it without me."

choices.text: Have every scroll carried to your own mountain

effects.log: Forty carts of scrolls go up the road. The librarian walks beside the last cart, uninvited.

choices.text: Leave the library standing, untouched, under guard

effects.log: You post two disciples at the door. The librarian bows to you for the first time.

choices.text: Burn it: their techniques die with their sect
