effects.log: The smoke rises for two days. The librarian sits on a stone and watches it the whole time.

events.text: Among the scrolls is a manual nobody can read, written in an old cipher. The librarian offers to teach the cipher, for a price: the names of every disciple of the fallen sect who survived must be written down and kept, so the sect is not forgotten.

choices.text: Agree, and keep the list in your own archive

effects.log: The librarian writes two hundred names in a careful hand, then teaches the cipher in a week.

choices.text: Break the cipher yourself

ok.log: After a month of lamplight you crack it, alone. The librarian looks at you as one looks at a rival.

fail.log: The cipher defeats you. The librarian, kindly, does not mention it.

choices.text: Leave the manual unread

effects.log: Some doors are better shut. The librarian nods, as if you had passed a test.

events.text: Years later a young wanderer arrives asking for the old librarian, long since buried among the scrolls. The wanderer's mother was a disciple of the fallen sect, the young one says, and always swore its library survived somewhere.

choices.text: Show the young wanderer the list of names

effects.log: A finger stops on one name, halfway down. The wanderer sits a long time in your archive.

choices.text: Give the young wanderer the key to the old library

effects.log: The young wanderer walks into the hall you guarded, and stays. A small new sect grows there, slowly.

choices.text: Offer a copy of one manual from the old sect

effects.log: The young wanderer takes it with shaking hands. It is not much, and it is everything.

choices.text: Say the library is gone

effects.log: The wanderer leaves. You lie awake that night, counting shelves.

events.text: The enemy sect is destroyed. Among the prisoners led past your gate is a thin disciple of seventeen, {npc}, who looks at you once, very steadily, and says: "I will learn your face." The guards laugh. You do not.

choices.text: Set {npc} free with a pouch of silver

effects.log: {npc} takes the silver and walks away without a word.

choices.text: Take {npc} into your mountain as a servant

effects.log: {npc} carries water, serves tea, and watches everything.

choices.text: Let {npc} go with the other prisoners

effects.log: {npc} disappears into the crowd of the defeated. You remember the face anyway.

events.text: Five winters later, a masked swordsman begins challenging your disciples on the roads and beating them, carefully, without killing. Each one comes home with the same message: "Tell your sect master I am nearly ready."

choices.text: Ride out alone to meet the swordsman

effects.log: You find {npc} on a bridge at dusk, mask off, waiting. The young face has grown hard.

choices.text: Double the guard and wait

effects.log: The roads go quiet. That is somehow worse.

choices.text: Send a letter: "I remember your face too."

effects.log: The letter comes back with one word under yours: "Good."

events.text: The duel comes at last, at the old burned gate of the fallen sect. {npc} draws first, then lowers the blade a little. "You could have ended me five years ago," {npc} says. "Why did you not?" The wind moves the ashes between you.

choices.text: "Because I hoped you would ask that."

effects.log: {npc} stands a long while, then sheathes the sword and walks off into the ruins. Nobody challenges your disciples again.

choices.text: Fight, and end it honourably

ok.log: You win, and leave {npc} alive on the stones. Later you hear {npc} has opened a small school far to the south.

fail.log: {npc} wins, and does not finish it. "Now we are even," the young swordsman says, and leaves you on the gate.

choices.text: Tell {npc} how the war began, and why

effects.log: You talk until dark. Neither of you is right; both of you are tired. {npc} leaves with the truth, which is heavier than a sword.

choices.text: Offer {npc} the burned gate and its land to rebuild on

effects.log: {npc} stares at you, then at the ruins. "I will rebuild," {he} says, "and I will not thank you."

events.text: The war is lost. The terms are signed, the tribute agreed, and the gate still stands. But nineteen disciples did not come home, and four of them leave children in the village below, who wait at the foot of the mountain steps every evening as if someone might yet come down them.

choices.text: Bring the children up the mountain to live with the sect

effects.log: Seven small children in borrowed robes, much too long. The cook starts making smaller buns.

choices.text: Pay the village families to raise them (120 taels)

effects.log: The children stay with grandparents and aunts, fed and warm. You send silver every new year.

choices.text: Leave them to their families

effects.log: The children stop coming to the steps after a while. You do not know if that is better.

events.text: The youngest orphan, a girl of six called Little Plum, will not eat, will not speak, and sleeps every night in front of the hall where her father's sword hangs. The elders want to move the sword. The cook wants to move the elders.

choices.text: Leave the sword where it is, and a blanket beside it

effects.log: Little Plum sleeps there all winter. In spring she asks, for the first time, how to hold it.

choices.text: Sit with her in the hall each evening

effects.log: You say nothing; she says nothing. After a month she falls asleep against your sleeve.

choices.text: Give her a wooden sword of her own

effects.log: She carries it everywhere, including to dinner, and finally eats.

events.text: Years pass. The orphans have grown into the steadiest disciples on the mountain, a little too serious and very good at guard duty. On the anniversary of the lost war, the eldest of them asks to speak at the memorial.

choices.text: Let Little Plum speak, holding her father's sword

effects.log: She speaks for one breath only: "He came home. He is here." Nobody on the mountain is dry-eyed.

choices.text: Let the eldest speak, however it goes

effects.log: The speech is short and fierce and about never losing again. The young disciples cheer; the old ones look away.

choices.text: Speak for them, so they need not

effects.log: You keep it gentle. Afterwards the orphans bring you tea, all at once, seven cups.

events.text: The war is lost and the price is set: every autumn a cart of silver and medicine goes down the mountain to the victors. On the day the first cart leaves, a senior disciple called Gao Feng stands at the gate and swears aloud that one day a cart will come back the other way.

choices.text: Let Gao Feng swear it: grief needs somewhere to go

effects.log: Gao Feng's oath is repeated in every dormitory that night.

choices.text: Stop the oath: the treaty is signed

effects.log: Gao Feng goes silent and drives the cart down personally, jaw tight.

choices.text: Drive the first cart down yourself, so no disciple has to

effects.log: You deliver the silver with your own hands. The victors' master seems almost embarrassed.

events.text: The fourth tribute cart. The victors' collector, a fat steward with a ledger, counts the silver slowly in front of your disciples and declares it forty taels short. It is not. Gao Feng's hand is already resting on a sword hilt.

choices.text: Pay the forty taels and stare at the steward (40 taels)

effects.log: You pay. The steward stops smiling and writes it down very slowly.

choices.text: Recount it in front of everyone, coin by coin

ok.log: It is exact, and the whole road heard it. He never shorts you again.

fail.log: You lose count at the second chest. The steward smiles wider.

choices.text: Let Gao Feng count, with a hand on the hilt

effects.log: The steward finds the count correct very quickly. The victors complain about it for a year.

events.text: The treaty has ten years to run when the victors' own sect is struck by a rival, and its master writes: they are short of medicine. Would your mountain, perhaps, be late with this year's cart? Or early?

choices.text: Send the cart early, with twice the medicine

effects.log: The victors survive their winter on your medicine. The next year their master tears up the treaty, in public.

choices.text: Let Gao Feng drive the cart back up the mountain, full

effects.log: No tribute this year, or ever again. Gao Feng's oath is kept, and nobody fights over it.

choices.text: Send it exactly on time, as signed

effects.log: The cart arrives on the day. The treaty is the treaty, and your honour is your own.

events.text: The tribute years are over. The old cart sits behind the granary, its wheels cracked and its sides still stained with the victors' brand. Gao Feng, grey now, asks what to do with it. Some of the juniors want to burn it; some want to paint it red and drive it round the valley.

choices.text: Keep it, as it is, by the gate

effects.log: Every new disciple is shown the cart on the first day. Nobody needs it explained twice.

choices.text: Burn it on the anniversary of the defeat

effects.log: The cart burns well. Gao Feng watches without a word and then goes to bed early.

choices.text: Give it to the village as a hay cart

effects.log: The cart carries hay for twenty years. It is the happiest it has ever been.

events.text: The war ends in a peace. Its terms fit on one sheet, and one line of them is a stone: a boundary marker to be set in the middle of the Willow Stream, which both sects fish. Each side wants the stone a little nearer the other bank.

choices.text: Set it exactly in the middle, measured with string

effects.log: Two elders, one string, a whole morning. The stone goes in and nobody is happy, which is fair.

choices.text: Let them have the deeper half: the fish are better there

effects.log: Your disciples grumble. The other side is so surprised it sends a basket of carp.

choices.text: Shift it a hand's width toward their bank, at night

effects.log: Nobody notices. You notice every time you fish.

events.text: Spring. A young disciple of yours and a young disciple of the other sect have been seen sitting on the boundary stone together, one on each half, fishing and talking for hours. The other sect's elders are scandalised. So are yours.

choices.text: Leave them be: this is what peace looks like

effects.log: The two keep fishing. By summer, half the young disciples of both sides fish there too.

choices.text: Forbid it, gently

effects.log: The two stop. They still wave from opposite banks, every morning.

choices.text: Go and fish on the stone yourself

effects.log: The other sect's elder joins you within the week. You catch nothing and talk about everything.

events.text: An autumn flood carries the boundary stone a hundred paces downstream, into a deep pool where nobody can reach it. Both sects send elders to the bank, and for a moment it is not clear whether the peace has gone with it.

choices.text: Propose the stream itself as the boundary from now on

effects.log: The other elder laughs and agrees. "Water moves," the elder says, "and so should we."

choices.text: Re-measure with the old string

effects.log: You find the string, the middle, and a new stone. Everyone grumbles again, which is comforting.

choices.text: Dive for the old stone and drag it back

ok.log: You come up blue with cold and holding the stone. Both sects cheer, together, for the first time ever.

fail.log: The pool is deeper than any story. You come up gasping and empty-handed.

choices.text: Let the river decide, and fish wherever you like

effects.log: There is no stone now and, oddly, no quarrel either.

events.text: The two young disciples who used to fish on the stone are elders now, one on each side of the stream, and they are getting married. Both sects are invited to the wedding on the bank, and both are waiting to see who will sit on which side of the water.

choices.text: Have the wedding table built across the stream on stilts

effects.log: Your carpenters build a table over the water. The guests sit with their feet in the stream and nobody can say whose side they are on.

choices.text: Give the couple fishing rights for life, from both banks

effects.log: The couple weeps, the elders of both sides grumble, and the carp have never been safer.

choices.text: Sit on the other sect's side, on purpose

effects.log: The other elders are thrown completely. By the third cup they are arguing over who gets to refill yours.

events.text: Peace is signed and the wounded come home. Twelve of them can no longer fight: a shattered knee, a hand that will not close, ears that ring at every loud noise. One of them, old Ru, asks you directly whether there is still a place for a sword that cannot be swung.

choices.text: Promise every wounded disciple a place, and mean it

effects.log: Ru nods once. That night the twelve eat together and argue about which of them is most useless.

choices.text: Find each of them a trade: archives, herbs, accounts

effects.log: Ru becomes your bookkeeper, and is terrible at it, and then very good.

choices.text: Pension them off to the village (100 taels)

effects.log: They take the silver and go. The mountain is quieter, and smaller.

events.text: Ru and the others have started something odd. They sit by the practice yard every morning and call out the young disciples' mistakes, mercilessly and correctly. The instructors are offended. The young disciples are improving very fast.

choices.text: Make the twelve official instructors

effects.log: The Bench of Twelve, everybody calls it. Your disciples fear it more than any elder.

choices.text: Ask the instructors and the twelve to share the yard

effects.log: There are arguments. There is also, by winter, the best class of disciples in years.

choices.text: Tell the twelve to leave the yard to the instructors

effects.log: They go back to the archives. The practice yard is quiet, and a little worse.

events.text: At the next provincial tournament, your disciples sweep the junior bouts. A judge, puzzled, asks your elders what secret training they use. Behind you, on a bench, twelve battered veterans pretend very hard not to be listening.

choices.text: Point at the bench

effects.log: The judge walks over and bows to the twelve. Ru goes red to the ears.

choices.text: Say: "Our wounded taught them what wounds are for."

effects.log: The line is copied onto a scroll and hung in three sects' halls by spring.

choices.text: Say: "Rice, and early mornings."

effects.log: The judge writes it down, unconvinced. The twelve laugh all the way home.

events.text: The sect is gone. The gate burned behind you and the mountain belongs to the enemy now. Eleven survivors follow you down the road in the snow: three wounded, two old cooks, five frightened disciples, and a goat nobody remembers bringing. They are waiting to hear where you will lead them.

choices.text: To the Pine Gate Sect, which once owed the old sect a favour

effects.log: You turn east. The goat leads the way, which is not reassuring.

choices.text: To the nearest town, to hide among ordinary people

effects.log: You take rooms above a dyer's shop. Your hands smell of indigo for months.

choices.text: Tell them to scatter: a hunted sect that stays together falls together

effects.log: They cry and argue and finally go, in ones and twos. The goat stays with you.

events.text: At the first friendly sect gate you reach, the guards will not open. Behind the walls their master sends down rice, blankets and a letter: the victors have spies everywhere, and sheltering you would bring the war here. One of your wounded has a fever that will not wait.

choices.text: Plead before the gate, in the snow, until the master comes

ok.log: At midnight the small door opens. Your fevered disciple is carried in, and you are all told you may stay until spring.

fail.log: The gate stays shut. You carry the fevered disciple to a farmhouse, where the farmer's wife nurses him through.

choices.text: Accept the rice and blankets, and go on

effects.log: You thank the guards. You do not blame them, which surprises them.

choices.text: Climb the wall by night with the sick disciple on your back

effects.log: You are caught at the top. The sect master, half asleep, sighs and sends for a healer.

events.text: Spring. Of the eleven, nine are still with you, and the goat. They have learned to cut firewood, haggle for rice and sleep anywhere. One evening the youngest asks the question they all carry: is there still a sect, or only people who used to be one?

choices.text: "As long as we train at dawn, there is a sect."

effects.log: The next morning nine people and one goat train in a farmer's field at dawn. It looks absurd. It feels like home.

choices.text: "There are people. That is enough for now."

effects.log: The youngest nods slowly. Some of the nine will marry, farm and scatter, and some will stay.

choices.text: "Ask me again in ten years."

effects.log: The youngest writes the date on the wall in charcoal, to be sure you remember.

events.text: The sect has fallen. In the cold dawn after, you find {npc}, a disciple of sixteen, sitting by the burned gate with a sword across both knees. "Teach me the rest," {npc} says. "Everything. I will finish every one of them."

choices.text: Take {npc} with you, and teach, slowly

effects.log: {npc} follows you down the mountain. You decide to teach the sword first, and the rest later.

choices.text: Take the sword gently out of {npc}'s hands

effects.log: {npc} lets go, then cries for the first time since the fire.

choices.text: Send {npc} to relatives in the south

effects.log: {npc} goes, furious. You hope the south is kind.

events.text: Two years on the road. {npc} trains like a fire, fast and hungry, and asks twice a month which of the victors' elders are still alive. One night the answer comes: the elder who burned your gate is drinking in an inn three streets away.

choices.text: Go together to the inn, and only watch

effects.log: You watch the old enemy drink. A grandchild climbs onto the enemy's lap. {npc} leaves the inn very quietly.

choices.text: Leave town that same night, before {npc} hears more

effects.log: You are on the road before midnight. {npc} knows exactly why, and walks a long way behind you.

choices.text: Go alone and challenge the elder

ok.log: You win, and walk away without finishing it. The old enemy kneels in the road, unhurt and suddenly very old.

fail.log: The old enemy is still strong. {npc} carries you out of the inn.
fail.deathCause: a duel with the elder who burned the gate

events.text: At twenty, {npc} is the best swordsman you have ever trained. One morning {npc} hands you back the sword, then the old sect's training manual. "I do not want them dead anymore," {npc} says. "I want the sect back. Is that the same thing?"

choices.text: "No. It is harder."

effects.log: You start that afternoon: a farmhouse, a borrowed field, one teacher and one student. The sect, small as a seed.

choices.text: Give the manual back to {npc}, to keep

effects.log: {npc} holds it carefully. "Then I will be the one who remembers," {npc} says.

choices.text: Say you do not know

effects.log: {npc} laughs for the first time in years. "Good. Neither do I."

events.text: You take a room at the Halfway Inn, which stands, as its name warns, exactly halfway between the Black Pine Sect and the Silver Creek Sect, now at war. The innkeeper, {npc}, keeps two sets of teacups, blue for Black Pine and white for Silver Creek, and never once mixes them up.

choices.text: Ask {npc} how the inn survives

effects.log: "Both sides need a place to drink," {npc} says, "and neither wants to burn the only good kitchen."

choices.text: Drink from a blue cup, to see what happens

effects.log: Three Silver Creek disciples stop talking. {npc} replaces the cup with a plain clay one, very quickly.

choices.text: Work in the inn for room and board

effects.log: {npc} hands you an apron and a cleaver, and tells you which cup is which.

events.text: One night a wounded Black Pine disciple stumbles in through the back door, and an hour later four Silver Creek disciples come in through the front, asking politely after a guest. {npc} looks at you across the kitchen, very calmly, and goes on wiping a blue cup.

choices.text: Hide the wounded disciple in the rice loft

effects.log: The Silver Creek four drink a white pot of tea and leave. The rice loft breathes again.

choices.text: Serve the Silver Creek four and talk them out of searching

ok.log: You tell them a long story about a ghost in the loft. They leave very early, and tip well.

fail.log: They search anyway, and find nobody: {npc} has moved the wounded one into a wine jar.

choices.text: Tell the Silver Creek four the truth

effects.log: They take the wounded disciple away. {npc} breaks a blue cup, by accident, and does not pick it up.

events.text: The war ends with a treaty signed, of all places, at the Halfway Inn, on its largest table. Both sect masters drink from plain clay cups. Afterwards {npc} takes down every blue and white cup and puts them in a box under the counter.

choices.text: Ask {npc} what the box is for

effects.log: "For the next war," {npc} says. "There is always a next war. But there is also, always, a next harvest."

choices.text: Toast the peace with {npc} in two clay cups

effects.log: You drink until the lanterns gutter. {npc} tells you every secret the inn has heard, and most are about noodles.

choices.text: Accept the Black Pine's thanks for the rice loft

effects.log: A Black Pine elder leaves a purse on the counter and a bow on the floor.

choices.text: Stay on at the inn as {npc}'s partner

effects.log: Your name goes up on the inn sign beside {npc}'s, in smaller letters.

events.text: The only ferry across the Yellow Reed River belongs to {npc}, a ferryman of sixty who has poled it for forty years. On the east bank camps the Red Cliff Sect; on the west, the Hollow Bamboo. Both are at war, and both want the ferry. {npc} has decided that it belongs to the fish.

choices.text: Pay for a crossing like anyone (20 taels)

effects.log: {npc} takes you over and talks about carp the whole way.

choices.text: Offer to help pole the ferry

effects.log: {npc} looks at your hands and laughs, then gives you the second pole.

choices.text: Ask {npc} which side will win

effects.log: "The river," {npc} says. "It always does."

events.text: Red Cliff disciples come down to the east bank with an order: the ferry is theirs now, and no Hollow Bamboo crosses again. They have brought a large axe and a small speech. {npc} listens to both, then sits down on the ferry and lights a pipe.

choices.text: Stand beside {npc} and talk the Red Cliff down

ok.log: You argue that a sunk ferry helps nobody. They leave the axe and take the speech home.

fail.log: They push you into the reeds. The ferry is seized for a season.

choices.text: Pole the ferry out into the middle of the river, with {npc}

effects.log: You anchor midstream. Nobody can reach you, and nobody can cross. It is very peaceful.

choices.text: Advise {npc} to give in, and stay alive

effects.log: {npc} hands over the pole, slowly. "Forty years," {npc} says, to nobody.

events.text: Midwinter. Wounded from both sides lie on both banks, and their healers are on the wrong ones. {npc} knocks out the pipe, says nothing, and starts poling across with a lantern hung on the prow, which in river custom means a ferry of the dead and must not be touched.

choices.text: Go with {npc}, holding the lantern

effects.log: All night you ferry wounded both ways. No arrow flies at the lantern.

choices.text: Keep watch from the bank

effects.log: You watch the lantern cross and recross until dawn, and count every crossing.

choices.text: Bring blankets and hot soup to both banks

effects.log: You ladle soup for both sides from the same pot. Nobody objects until the pot is empty.

events.text: Spring. Both sects have signed a truce, and both masters crossed on the ferry to do it, side by side, in silence. {npc} charged them each the usual twenty taels. Afterwards the ferryman sits with you in the reeds, unusually talkative.

choices.text: Ask {npc} to teach you the river

effects.log: {npc} teaches you the currents, the fish and the moods of the water. It is a technique, of sorts.

choices.text: Help {npc} paint a new name on the ferry

effects.log: You paint "The Fish's Ferry" on the prow. {npc} approves of the brushwork.

choices.text: Say goodbye and walk on

effects.log: {npc} raises the pole as you go. For years, you hear, the ferryman asks travellers about you.

events.text: Mulberry Hollow sits between the Thunder Gate and the Green Lotus sects, now at war, and both have begun collecting "protection" from it. The village headwoman, Granny Tan, shows you two receipts for the same pig and asks, in a loud and reasonable voice, which sect owns the pig's back half.

choices.text: Offer to speak for the village to both sects

effects.log: Granny Tan looks you up and down. "You are skinny," she says, "but loud enough."

choices.text: Help the villagers hide half the harvest in the hills

effects.log: You carry rice sacks up goat paths by moonlight. The goats are not helpful.

choices.text: Pay one side's tax for the village (100 taels)

effects.log: Granny Tan takes the silver and bites a coin. "One pig's half is saved," she says.

events.text: Both tax collectors arrive on the same morning: a stiff Thunder Gate elder and a cheerful Green Lotus disciple. They meet in the square. Neither will leave first. The village holds its breath, and the donkey eats the Thunder Gate elder's ledger.

choices.text: Propose a treaty in the square: one tax, split in half

ok.log: The two sides agree, mostly because they are embarrassed in front of the donkey. The village pays once.

fail.log: Both refuse, loudly. The donkey is the only one who profits.

choices.text: Challenge the cheerful Green Lotus disciple to a bout for the tax

effects.log: You win narrowly. The disciple laughs, shakes your hand, and leaves without the silver.

choices.text: Tell both the harvest failed

effects.log: The collectors look at the empty barns and leave with half a pig each.

choices.text: Stay out of it and watch

effects.log: The two collectors argue until dark, then both take everything. The village eats thin soup all winter.

events.text: The war ends with both sects exhausted. Granny Tan calls the village together, nails both receipts to the shrine door, and announces that Mulberry Hollow will now pay nobody, and keep a spear for every house. She asks whether you will stay a year and teach them to hold one.

choices.text: Stay a year and teach the village

effects.log: A year of mornings in the square. By winter, sixty farmers can stand in a spear line, and the donkey can stand behind it.

choices.text: Teach them for a month and move on

effects.log: A month is enough to teach a stance and a shout. Granny Tan says the shout is the important part.

choices.text: Advise them to pay, to stay safe

effects.log: Granny Tan looks at you with great disappointment and pays nobody anyway.

events.text: A year after the war, Granny Tan dies in her sleep, and Mulberry Hollow sends for you to carry one end of her coffin. At the graveside the villagers present you with the two tax receipts for the same pig, framed, and the donkey, who has apparently been left to you in her will.

choices.text: Accept the donkey with honour

effects.log: The donkey looks at you with deep suspicion and follows you out of the village anyway.

choices.text: Hang the receipts in the village shrine instead

effects.log: Granny Tan's receipts hang in the shrine. Tax collectors visiting the village are shown them first.

choices.text: Stay another season to train the new headman

effects.log: The new headman is Granny Tan's grandson, and twice as loud. You train him in shouting.

events.text: On the road through the Ashwood, where two sects have been skirmishing all summer, you find a young disciple in a grey robe lying in a ditch, a sword wound in her side and a broken sword in her hand. Over the hill you hear a patrol, coming this way, in the other colours.

choices.text: Drag her into the bushes and keep still

effects.log: The patrol passes three paces away. The girl in the ditch bites her sleeve to keep from crying out.

choices.text: Flag down the patrol and ask for a healer

effects.log: The patrol looks at the grey robe and then at you. They take her prisoner, alive at least.

choices.text: Walk on: this is not your war

effects.log: You walk on. The patrol's voices fade behind you, and you do not look back.

events.text: Her name is Hua and she is seventeen. You bind the wound with your own sash and carry her to a charcoal burner's hut. In the night her fever rises, and she asks you, between shivers, to carry a letter to her sect master if she does not see morning.

choices.text: Stay up all night and keep the fever down

ok.log: By dawn her fever breaks. She sleeps like a stone until noon.

fail.log: The fever climbs and falls and climbs. She lives, but it is three weeks before she can stand.

choices.text: Take the letter, and promise

effects.log: You put the letter in your shirt. She falls asleep holding your sleeve.

choices.text: Run to the nearest village for a healer (40 taels)

effects.log: The healer comes, complains about the road, and saves her.

events.text: Hua mends. When she can walk, the two of you reach her sect's outpost, where the guards are astonished to see her alive. Her sect master, a tired woman with grey braids, wants to know what an outsider wants for bringing back a disciple they had already mourned.

choices.text: Ask for nothing

effects.log: The sect master bows to you, which sect masters do not do to wanderers. Word of it spreads.

choices.text: Ask her to make peace with the other sect

effects.log: She laughs, then stops laughing. "You carried my disciple through their patrols," she says. "I will think about it."

choices.text: Hand over the unopened letter

effects.log: The sect master reads it and turns away for a moment. Then she gives you a manual from her own shelf.

choices.text: Accept the reward she offers

effects.log: A purse of silver and a pass through her sect's lands for life.

events.text: A letter finds you on the road two years later, carried by a disciple in grey. Hua is a senior disciple now, and her sect and its old enemy have signed a peace, not least, the letter says, because their master kept remembering an outsider who carried a wounded enemy through patrols.

choices.text: Go to visit Hua

effects.log: Hua meets you at the gate and walks you round the new peace stone. Her limp is almost gone.

choices.text: Write back, and keep walking

effects.log: You write by a roadside fire. Some friendships live best in letters.

choices.text: Ask Hua for a place to stay through the winter

effects.log: You winter with Hua's sect and leave in spring with a new technique and a full purse.

events.text: Disciples of the Crimson Peak, at war with their neighbours, stop you on the road and requisition your mule, Old Tofu, for their supply train. Old Tofu has opinions about this. So, it turns out, does the Crimson Peak quartermaster, who signs a receipt promising to return the mule after the war.

choices.text: Let them take Old Tofu, and keep the receipt

effects.log: You fold the receipt carefully. Old Tofu looks back at you with deep reproach.

choices.text: Follow the supply train to keep an eye on Old Tofu

effects.log: You walk behind the carts for three days. The quartermaster gives up and hires you as a mule handler.

choices.text: Pay them to leave the mule (50 taels)

effects.log: The quartermaster takes the silver and a different mule. Old Tofu is unmoved.

events.text: The supply train stalls on a mountain path. Old Tofu has lain down across it and will not move, and twenty carts of rice for the siege are stuck behind one grey mule. The Crimson Peak elders are shouting. Old Tofu is chewing.

choices.text: Whisper to Old Tofu the one word that works

effects.log: "Turnips." Old Tofu rises. The siege is fed, and the elders look at you with something like respect.

choices.text: Lift the back of the mule yourself

ok.log: You heave. Old Tofu rises, outraged. Twenty carts cheer.

fail.log: Old Tofu kicks. You spend a week limping and the carts are a day late.

choices.text: Advise the elders to wait

effects.log: They wait. Old Tofu gets up at sunset, entirely by choice, and the carts move on.

events.text: The war is over. You present yourself at the Crimson Peak gate to collect Old Tofu. The quartermaster, who has risen to elder in the war, pretends not to know you, until Old Tofu, in the stable yard behind, hears your voice and kicks down a door.

choices.text: Show the receipt, signed and sealed

effects.log: The elder reads it, sighs and returns the mule, with a sack of oats as interest.

choices.text: Call Old Tofu by name

effects.log: Old Tofu walks out of the gate on his own. Nobody tries to stop him.

choices.text: Let the Crimson Peak keep him: he is a war hero now

effects.log: You hear later that Old Tofu has his own stall, with a plaque. He bites everyone who reads it.

events.text: Old Tofu is very old now, grey at the muzzle and slow on the hills. He still carries your pack, refuses all bridges, and kicks every member of the Crimson Peak sect on sight, which is a kind of loyalty. One morning he lies down in the sun and does not want to get up.

choices.text: Sit with Old Tofu in the sun all day

effects.log: You sit together until evening. Old Tofu goes to sleep and does not wake. You bury him under a turnip field.

choices.text: Carry the pack yourself and let him walk free

effects.log: He follows you without a load for one more summer, very pleased with himself.

choices.text: Leave Old Tofu with a farmer who loves turnips

effects.log: The farmer sends word a year later: Old Tofu is fine, fat and still kicking.

events.text: Your sect is at peace, but over the ridge the Plum Valley and the Iron Cauldron sects have been at war since spring, and every evening there is smoke. Now Plum Valley refugees are climbing to your gate, mostly old people and children, and the elders have ordered the gate shut: the Alliance does not take sides.

choices.text: Open the side door at night for the oldest and youngest

effects.log: Six old people and four children come in through the woodshed. The elders do not ask, yet.

choices.text: Carry food down to the refugees outside the wall

effects.log: You make the trip every evening. A small camp grows by your gate.

choices.text: Obey the elders

effects.log: The gate stays shut. The smoke over the ridge does not care either way.

events.text: The Iron Cauldron sends an envoy to your sect master. They have heard that Plum Valley people are on your mountain, they say, and an orthodox sect that shelters one side is no longer neutral. The elders summon every disciple to the hall to ask who opened the door.

choices.text: Step forward

effects.log: The hall goes silent. The sect master looks at you for a long time, then sends the envoy away with no answer.

choices.text: Say that a camp outside the wall shelters nobody

effects.log: The envoy cannot argue with that. The elders, interestingly, do not try to.

choices.text: Stay silent with everyone else

effects.log: No one steps forward. The sect master closes the matter, and the hall breathes out.

events.text: The war ends. Plum Valley is half burned but still standing, and its new master climbs your mountain in a plain robe to thank the sect that did not take sides, and the disciple who did. The sect master looks at you over the tea, unreadable.

choices.text: Accept the thanks and the Plum Valley's friendship

effects.log: The Plum Valley master names you a friend of the sect, in writing. The elders say nothing, and that is approval.

choices.text: Say the sect master allowed it all along

effects.log: The sect master's mouth twitches. You are given an elder's errand the next month.

choices.text: Bow and leave the hall

effects.log: Some thanks are better left on the table. The Plum Valley master understands.

events.text: The four children who came in through the woodshed that first night are grown now and wear your sect's colours. On the anniversary of the Plum Valley fire they ask to climb the ridge together, and they ask you to come with them.

choices.text: Climb the ridge with them

effects.log: On the ridge you all look down at Plum Valley, green again. Nobody says anything for a long time.

choices.text: Let them go alone

effects.log: They come back at dusk with plums from the valley and a message of thanks from its new master.

choices.text: Ask the sect master to come too

effects.log: The sect master climbs slowly, and says at the top: "I knew about the woodshed."

events.text: Your sect is not at war; it is in business. Two orthodox sects are fighting down the valley, and the elders send you with a cart of wound salve to sell to both. "Same price," Elder Kang says, "same smile, and never tell either who else is buying."

choices.text: Sell to both, same price, same smile

effects.log: Both camps pay well and ask no questions. By autumn the cart has gone back and forth four times.

choices.text: Sell cheaper to the side that is losing

effects.log: The losing side remembers. Elder Kang counts the silver and frowns.

choices.text: Water down the salve and pocket the difference

effects.log: You make extra silver. Somewhere, a wound stays open longer.

events.text: A quartermaster in the White Crane camp has noticed that the Black Rock camp's salve smells exactly like his. He invites you into his tent for tea, and closes the flap. Three disciples with spears stand outside.

choices.text: Lie smoothly: every salve in the province smells of camphor

ok.log: He believes you, or decides to. You leave with your silver and your knees shaking.

fail.log: He does not believe you. You leave without the cart, which is better than without your head.

choices.text: Tell the truth: you sell to anyone who bleeds

effects.log: The quartermaster laughs, which you did not expect. "At least you are honest," he says, and orders twice as much.

choices.text: Give him the next cart free, to forget the smell

effects.log: He forgets the smell. He also remembers that you can be bargained with.

events.text: The war is over and both orthodox sects are declaring your sect "a nest of war profiteers" at the Alliance meeting. Elder Kang wants to know who talked. The elders of your sect are not pleased with the noise, though they were very pleased with the silver.

choices.text: Say the losing side's gratitude is louder than the winner's spite

effects.log: It is true. The losing sect's master stands up at the meeting and defends you. Elder Kang is amazed.

choices.text: Take the blame and go quiet for a year

effects.log: You are given ledgers to copy all winter. Elder Kang brings you a hot bun now and then.

choices.text: Point out that both sects bought willingly

effects.log: The Alliance can do nothing with that. Your sect is admired in a certain kind of teahouse.

events.text: Elder Kang is dying, slowly and grumpily, of old age, and summons you to the sickroom at midnight. The elder wants the account books burned, every one, and has a last word of advice for the sect's best salesman.

choices.text: Burn the books as asked

effects.log: The books go into the brazier one by one. Elder Kang watches every page curl, satisfied.

choices.text: Keep one book, the one with the salve accounts

effects.log: You hide it in your sleeve. It is the closest thing to a confession the old elder ever wrote.

choices.text: Ask for the advice

effects.log: "Same price, same smile," Elder Kang whispers. "But never sell to a war you would not walk away from."

events.text: The Cult is at peace, and wishes everyone else were not. Two orthodox sects to the south, the Morning Sun and the Jade Gate, are already quarrelling over a waterfall. The Cult's Whisper Hall gives you a purse and a single order: make it a war, without anyone ever seeing a black robe.

choices.text: Spread rumours in the teahouses of both towns

effects.log: In a month each sect is sure the other plans to divert the waterfall. Neither plans anything of the kind.

choices.text: Forge a letter from one sect master to the other

effects.log: Your forged insult is magnificent. The Jade Gate master reads it aloud at dinner, purple.

choices.text: Spend the purse on noodles and report that it failed

effects.log: The Whisper Hall writes you down as useless, which is safer than many other things to be.

events.text: It works. The two orthodox sects go to war over a waterfall neither of them needed. A Morning Sun disciple you drank tea with, a cheerful boy called Little Yang, is carried home from the first battle on a door. The Whisper Hall sends you a jar of good wine.

choices.text: Pour the wine away, and keep working

effects.log: It is very good wine. You pour it out alone.

choices.text: Pour the wine out at Little Yang's grave

effects.log: You stand at a grave with your own name nowhere on it. That is the whole point, and it is unbearable.

choices.text: Leave a true letter for both sect masters, unsigned

effects.log: The letter says the waterfall war was made, by whom you do not say. Both masters read it twice.

events.text: The orthodox war ends, both sects bled pale, and the Cult rejoices quietly. The Whisper Hall master summons you in person and offers a higher seat. Behind the master, in the shadows, a scribe is writing down your face.

choices.text: Take the seat

effects.log: You rise in the Cult. Somewhere south, two sects rebuild, and do not know your name.

choices.text: Ask for a quiet post far from the Whisper Hall

effects.log: The master studies you, then grants it, with a smile that worries you for years.

choices.text: Talk your way out of the summons before the letter is traced to you

ok.log: You leave the hall with your seat, your secret and your skin. The two orthodox sects have made peace.

fail.log: The scribe stops writing. You are sent to guard a remote shrine for three years, which is lenient.

events.text: The great war between {war_a} and {war_b} has swallowed the province. In the market of Lin County, two recruiters stand ten paces apart, one under each banner, each promising rice, a sword and glory. The rice is real on both sides. Nobody has seen the glory.

choices.text: Sign up with {war_a} for the rice

effects.log: You sign your name and get a bowl of rice and a bamboo shield.

choices.text: Sign up with {war_b} for the rice

effects.log: You sign your name and get a bowl of rice and a spear without a point.

choices.text: Help the market folk hide their sons from both

effects.log: You carry three boys out of town in a cabbage cart. Their mothers will not stop feeding you.

choices.text: Leave Lin County before anyone writes your name

effects.log: You walk south all night. Both banners shrink behind you.

events.text: Six months later the war has caught you one way or another, and you are crouching behind a broken wall, and on the other side of it, close enough to touch, a young fighter from the other banner is also crouching. You recognise the face: the noodle seller's boy from Lin County market. You both stare at each other's rice bowls.

choices.text: Share your rice and wait for the noise to pass

effects.log: You eat in silence on either side of the wall. When the fighting moves on, you both go back to your lines.

choices.text: Talk the boy into deserting together

ok.log: You both slip away at night and walk to the boy's mother, who weeps and hits you both with a ladle.

fail.log: The boy is too frightened. You part with a nod, and you never learn what became of him.

choices.text: Pretend you never saw the boy

effects.log: You look away, and so does the boy. The wall keeps both secrets.

events.text: Years on, the great war is a story told in teahouses, mostly wrongly. In Lin County market the noodle stall is still there. The old seller, much greyer, looks up from the steam, ladle in hand, and knows you at once.

choices.text: Sit and eat a bowl, as if nothing ever happened

effects.log: The noodles are exactly as good as you remember. Nobody talks about banners.

choices.text: Ask after the three boys from the cabbage cart

effects.log: Two are farmers now, one a carpenter. All three send the noodle seller a basket at New Year.

choices.text: Ask after the noodle seller's boy

effects.log: The seller points at the kitchen. A man about your age comes out wiping his hands, and stops still.

events.text: A district clerk asks you to help write the county's record of the great war: who went, who came back, which banner, which village. Two columns, he says, one for each side. He has already drawn the line down the middle of the page.

choices.text: Suggest one column, for everyone

effects.log: The clerk thinks about it, then tears up the page and starts again. The new record is very long.

choices.text: Write your own name, under the banner you served

effects.log: Your name goes in. It looks small on the page, and very permanent.

choices.text: Decline: some things should be forgotten

effects.log: The clerk shrugs and writes the record alone. Half the names are misspelt.

events.text: Shi Town has one bridge, and in the great war both {war_a} and {war_b} want it: one to cross, one to burn. The town elder has gathered everyone in the temple to decide what Shi Town wants, which is mostly to be left alone and to keep the bridge it built with its own hands.

choices.text: Propose the town guard the bridge for neither side

effects.log: Forty townsfolk with hoes stand on the bridge. Both armies are puzzled enough to stop and send envoys.

choices.text: Advise them to let it burn, and live

effects.log: The town elder listens gravely. "Bridges can be rebuilt," the elder says, "and so can we."

choices.text: Slip away before the armies arrive

effects.log: You leave by the river path. Behind you, the temple bell rings and rings.

events.text: Both envoys arrive on the same afternoon and stand at opposite ends of the bridge, shouting terms. The town elder looks at you. Somebody has to walk out to the middle of the bridge and speak for Shi Town.

choices.text: Walk to the middle and bargain

ok.log: By sunset both sides agree: Shi Town keeps its bridge, and charges each army the same toll.

fail.log: The envoys shout you down. That night, someone sets a fire under the third pillar.

choices.text: Walk out with a bucket of water and stand there

effects.log: You stand in the middle all night with your bucket. Nobody fires the bridge with you on it.

choices.text: Help the townsfolk move their goods across before dark

effects.log: Carts, chickens and grandmothers, all night. By dawn the old bank is empty.

choices.text: Let the town elder speak, and stand behind

effects.log: The town elder speaks well. You hold the lantern.

events.text: The great war moves on. Whether it was burned or saved, the bridge at Shi Town is in your name now in the town's memory, and the town elder sends a child to fetch you for the spring festival, when the whole town walks across the river together.

choices.text: Walk across first, with the town elder

effects.log: Shi Town cheers you over the water. A carved plank near the middle has your name on it.

choices.text: Help rebuild the third pillar, stone by stone

effects.log: A season of stone and mud. The pillar you set is the straightest one.

choices.text: Send the child back with thanks and stay away

effects.log: Some things are best remembered from a distance. The child brings you a festival cake anyway.

events.text: The front of the great war between {war_a} and {war_b} cuts a valley in two, and with it a hundred families. A blind scribe in the market writes letters for both halves and needs someone fast and quiet to carry them across the line at night. The pay is poor. The letters are mostly about grandmothers.

choices.text: Carry the letters

effects.log: Your first night you cross the line with forty letters in a bamboo tube. Nobody stops you.

choices.text: Carry them, but read each one first, in case of spies

effects.log: You read forty letters about grandmothers, goats and a missing teapot. No spies.

choices.text: Refuse: if caught, you would be called a spy

effects.log: The scribe nods. Somebody else will do it, and somebody else will be caught.

events.text: One night, a {war_b} patrol stops you on the riverbank and empties the bamboo tube. The young officer reads a letter at random by lantern light: a mother on the other side asking whether her son eats properly.

choices.text: Tell the officer what the letters are

effects.log: The officer reads three more, then rolls them up and hands back the tube. "Go," the officer says.

choices.text: Run for the river

ok.log: You swim the river with the tube in your teeth. Every letter arrives, wet but readable.

fail.log: You make it across, but the tube floats away downstream.

choices.text: Show the officer the letters you read: no secrets

effects.log: You recite the missing teapot letter word for word. The officer laughs and lets you go.

events.text: Winter. The blind scribe asks you to carry one last letter, which has no name on it. It is from a dying fighter in a field hospital to a family across the line, and the scribe wrote it down that afternoon, word by word. The address is an hour behind the enemy's camp.

choices.text: Carry it, whatever the risk

ok.log: You knock on a farmhouse door at dawn. An old couple reads it together on the step, and they hold your hand a long time.

fail.log: You are caught and held a week, then released by a sergeant who reads the letter and delivers it personally.

choices.text: Ask the scribe to keep it until the war ends

effects.log: The scribe keeps it in a drawer. A year later, at peace, you deliver it, and the family thanks you anyway.

choices.text: Carry it with the rest, as usual

effects.log: One more letter in the tube. It weighs more than all the others.

events.text: The great war ends. The blind scribe closes the stall and gives you a bundle tied with string: every letter that could never be delivered, because the sender or the receiver did not survive. Forty-one letters. "You knew the roads," the scribe says. "I knew the words."

choices.text: Deliver every one to whoever is left

effects.log: It takes a whole year. Most doors open to tears; a few to laughter, at old jokes from dead hands.

choices.text: Burn them at a temple, with incense

effects.log: The monks chant for the letters all night. The smoke goes up in forty-one threads.

choices.text: Keep them in a box, unopened, for the families to claim

effects.log: Over the years, nineteen families come and ask. You give each a letter and a cup of tea.

events.text: It is the Lantern Festival, and on the river between the camps of {war_a} and {war_b}, nobody has lit a lantern in three years. You are sitting on the bank with a paper lantern you made from habit, and a candle, and absolutely no plan.

choices.text: Light it and let it float out onto the river

effects.log: One small lantern drifts towards the middle. On both banks, the sentries stop and stare.

choices.text: Row out to the middle of the river and light it there

effects.log: You sit alone in a boat in the middle of a war, holding a lantern. It is the bravest and stupidest thing you have done.

choices.text: Keep it unlit for a better year

effects.log: You put the lantern away. The river stays dark.

events.text: A year later, at the next festival, you light another. This time, on the far bank, someone lights a second lantern and pushes it into the water. Then a third, on the near bank. Within an hour the river is full of them, and nobody on either side has fired an arrow.

choices.text: Start singing the old festival song

effects.log: Your voice is bad. By the second verse, both banks are singing it, badly, together.

choices.text: Row the boat from bank to bank, carrying sweet rice balls

effects.log: Sweet rice balls go across the river both ways all night. Nobody asks whose they are.

choices.text: Sit on the bank and watch the lanterns

effects.log: You watch until the last candle gutters. Something in your chest unknots.

events.text: The next morning the war resumes as if nothing happened. But the lantern night is told and retold in both camps, and the next year, and the year after, the Lantern Festival is kept on the river by both sides, and nobody fights that night.

choices.text: Make another lantern for next year

effects.log: You make ten. Strangers on both banks ask you how to fold the corners.

choices.text: Go and tell the story to the two commanders

effects.log: Both commanders know it already. One of them, gruffly, asks you to stay for tea.

choices.text: Keep the story to yourself

effects.log: You never tell anyone it was you. The story grows without you, and that is fine.

events.text: Your disciple {npc} wins the provincial tournament at nineteen, beating three sect heirs in one afternoon. Overnight {sect} is famous, or rather {npc} is: travellers now climb your mountain asking which hall the champion sleeps in, and what the champion eats for breakfast.
events.arc: The Disciple Who Outshone the Sect

choices.text: Hold a feast in {npc}'s honour

effects.log: The whole mountain feasts. {npc} sits at the top table, red to the ears, and eats breakfast food at dinner to please the visitors.

choices.text: Send {npc} straight back to morning drills

effects.log: {npc} is at drills before dawn the next day. The visitors watch, disappointed, and then impressed.

choices.text: Charge visitors to watch the champion train (gain)

effects.log: The gate fees fill a chest. {npc} trains in front of a crowd, and hates it quietly.

events.text: A letter arrives for {npc} from the Heavenly Sword Sect, the greatest in the land: a place among their inner disciples, a private teacher, and a room with a view of the sea. {npc} brings the letter to you unopened, which says something, and stands waiting.
events.arc: The Disciple Who Outshone the Sect

choices.text: Tell {npc} to go: a tree that size needs a bigger field

effects.log: {npc} cries, and bows, and goes. Your disciples are proud and heartbroken in equal measure.

choices.text: Ask {npc} to stay, honestly, and say why

effects.log: "Because this mountain made you, and the mountain needs you," you say. {npc} burns the letter in the lamp.

choices.text: Open the letter and answer it yourself, refusing

effects.log: {npc} hears of it a week later, from a visitor. Something closes quietly between you.

choices.text: Ask {npc} what {he} wants

effects.log: {npc} thinks a long while. "To be asked that," {he} says, "more often."

events.text: Years pass. {npc}, now known across the province, comes back up your mountain on a spring morning with a dozen young disciples behind, all wearing a new sect's colours, and asks to see you in the old practice yard.
events.arc: The Disciple Who Outshone the Sect

choices.text: Embrace {npc}: the field was big enough

effects.log: {npc} founded a branch sect by the sea, and named its first hall after yours. Your mountain is famous on two coasts.

choices.text: Hear {npc}'s plan: a second hall of your own sect

effects.log: {npc} wants to open a branch of your sect in the south. The elders gasp; you say yes before they can object.

choices.text: Hear {npc} out about the letter

effects.log: {npc} is calm and very polite. The young disciples behind are not yours, and never will be.

choices.text: Spar with {npc} in the yard, for old times

effects.log: You lose, of course, and laugh, and so does {npc}. It is the best morning in years.

events.text: Your sect is growing, and your new chief builder, a man of grand vision named Master Lou, proposes a new mountain gate: forty feet of red lacquer and gilded dragons, to tell the whole martial world that {sect} has arrived. The estimate is in a scroll so long it is carried by two disciples.

choices.text: Build the great gate (400 taels)

effects.log: A summer of scaffolding. The gate rises, enormous and glorious. Behind it, your six halls look like sheds.

choices.text: Build a sensible gate, half the size (150 taels)

effects.log: Master Lou sulks for a month, then builds the most elegant small gate in the province.

choices.text: Keep the old wooden gate

effects.log: Master Lou leaves in a huff, taking his scroll. The old gate creaks contentedly.

events.text: Problems. The great gate catches the mountain wind like a sail and howls all night. Visiting sect masters walk through it, look at the six small halls behind, and smile. Your disciples have started calling it the Gate of Promises.

choices.text: Build halls worthy of the gate, slowly (200 taels)

effects.log: Year by year, the halls grow up to meet the gate. The joke fades.

choices.text: Hang wind chimes in it, and call the howling music

effects.log: Visitors are told the gate sings for worthy guests. Several sect masters stand in it for a long time, hoping.

choices.text: Laugh with your disciples about the Gate of Promises

effects.log: The name sticks, kindly. Your disciples are fiercely proud of their ridiculous gate.

choices.text: Invite the visiting masters back in ten years

effects.log: The visiting masters accept. You have ten years to make them stop smiling.

events.text: A summer storm drives lightning into the mountain. In the morning half the province climbs to see whether your gate is still standing. It is, scorched along one dragon, and the scorch mark looks, if you squint, very like a second dragon.

choices.text: Leave the scorch: Heaven has signed the gate

effects.log: "The gate Heaven signed," pilgrims call it. Fifty new applicants come to the gate that autumn.

choices.text: Repaint it at once (60 taels)

effects.log: Fresh lacquer, gleaming red. A little magic leaves with the soot.

choices.text: Write to Master Lou with the news

effects.log: Master Lou writes back four pages, mostly about lightning rods, and one line that says he is proud.

events.text: Master Lou, very old, comes back up the mountain to see the gate before dying. He stands under it a long time, looking at the scorch-dragon and the halls that have finally grown up to meet it. "Too big," he says at last. "It was always too big. Good."

choices.text: Ask Master Lou to carve his name on the gate

effects.log: Lou carves it small, on the inside of the left pillar, where only people leaving can see it.

choices.text: Give him a room on the mountain for his last years

effects.log: Lou spends two years criticising every building on the mountain. He is loved for it.

choices.text: Walk him through it, both ways, slowly

effects.log: You go through the gate together, then back. Lou laughs like a boy.

events.text: You are invited to the great gathering of the Heavenly Sword Sect, the most famous sect under Heaven, for the first time. Your seat is at the small table by the door, with the sects that have fewer than a hundred disciples, and right next to the soup.

choices.text: Sit gracefully and enjoy the soup

effects.log: The soup is excellent. The masters at your little table are funnier than the great ones.

choices.text: Seek out the Heavenly Sword master during the toasts

effects.log: You get one sentence in, between a bow and a cup. The master nods kindly and forgets you by the next cup.

choices.text: Ask, publicly, for a demonstration bout to show your sect's worth

ok.log: You beat their fourth disciple before the whole hall. Next year your seat is two tables nearer the front.

fail.log: Their fourth disciple beats you, gently. The hall applauds your courage, which is worse.

events.text: Back home, you find yourself copying the Heavenly Sword: their robes, their bows, their way of pouring tea. Your elders notice. One of them, old Elder Fu, leaves a note on your desk with a single line: "A good plum tree does not try to grow pears."

choices.text: Order new robes in the Heavenly Sword style (100 taels)

effects.log: Your disciples look magnificent and feel ridiculous. Visitors ask whether you are a branch of the Heavenly Sword.

choices.text: Pin Elder Fu's note above your desk

effects.log: You read it every morning. Your sect goes on growing plums.

choices.text: Invite the masters from the small table to your own gathering

effects.log: Eleven small sects meet on your mountain. Nobody sits by the soup, because you put the soup in the middle.

events.text: Ten years on, the Heavenly Sword Sect falls into a bitter succession quarrel and splits in three. The gathering is cancelled. A letter comes from one of the small-table masters: would you host this year instead?

choices.text: Host it, with no small table at all

effects.log: One long table, no door end. It becomes the custom. Your sect is now the one others envy.

choices.text: Host it in your Heavenly Sword robes

effects.log: Your guests are too polite to laugh, mostly. You put the robes away afterwards for good.

choices.text: Host it as yourselves, plums and all

effects.log: Elder Fu's note is read aloud at the opening toast. The guests drink to plum trees.

choices.text: Decline: you have your own sect to run

effects.log: Another sect hosts it. Your own disciples, privately, are relieved.

events.text: A small, new sect master writes to you: they have been seated at a small table at someone else's gathering, by the door, next to the soup, and they want to know how you got from there to where you are now. They are clearly furious and trying very hard not to be.

choices.text: Write back about the soup

effects.log: You write that the soup is better by the door. The new master writes back, a year later, that it was.

choices.text: Invite them to sit at your one long table

effects.log: The new master comes, sits in the middle, and is unbearably proud all evening.

choices.text: Send them Elder Fu's note

effects.log: You copy the line about plum trees in your own hand. The new master hangs it above a desk.

events.text: Your sect's fame has spread, and the spring entrance trial brings three hundred applicants to a mountain with room for forty. They camp on the steps, in the bamboo, in the latrines. One enterprising family has opened a dumpling stall at the gate and is doing very good business.

choices.text: Take forty by trial, strictly, and send the rest home

effects.log: Forty pass. Two hundred and sixty go down the mountain. Some of them will be back.

choices.text: Take a hundred and build more dormitories (200 taels)

effects.log: The mountain is crowded, noisy and alive. The elders lose their voices by summer.

choices.text: Take every one, for a season, and see who stays

effects.log: Three hundred in the yard at dawn. By winter, seventy remain, and they are tough.

events.text: The new intake has a problem: a handful of rich families' heirs who believe they paid for their places, a poor shepherd from the west who trains in the dark because the others mock his accent, and someone who keeps stealing the instructors' sandals.

choices.text: Pair each heir with the shepherd for drills

effects.log: The heirs complain for a month. Then the shepherd throws one into the pond and they all begin to listen.

choices.text: Set a trap for the sandal thief

effects.log: The thief is a monkey from the bamboo grove. You let it stay; the instructors buy new sandals.

choices.text: Expel the worst of the heirs

effects.log: The heir's family complains in three letters and a petition to the magistrate. The other heirs behave beautifully thereafter.

events.text: Five years after the great intake. The shepherd from the west is your best young disciple; two of the heirs are elders; the monkey is the sect's unofficial mascot. And the dumpling family at the gate has built a small inn, which pays your sect rent.

choices.text: Promote the shepherd to instructor

effects.log: The shepherd teaches with the accent everyone once mocked. Now the young disciples copy it.

choices.text: Collect the rent from the dumpling inn

effects.log: The dumpling family pays in silver and steamed buns. Mostly buns.

choices.text: Hold the next trial strictly, with only twenty places

effects.log: Six hundred applicants come for twenty places. Your gate is the hardest in the province now.

choices.text: Open a second hall in the valley for the overflow

effects.log: A valley hall under your banner, run by the two heirs. They run it well, to everyone's surprise.

events.text: Years after your old sect fell, a weathered traveller stops you in a market and says your old title quietly, as if it might break. It is {npc}, once the sect's gatekeeper, who has spent all this time searching every market in the province for you.

choices.text: Take {npc} to a teahouse and listen

effects.log: {npc} talks until the teahouse closes: who lived, who did not, who married, who went to the cult.

choices.text: Pretend not to recognise {npc}

effects.log: {npc} bows and turns away, then turns back. "You still walk the same," {npc} says, and leaves an address.

choices.text: Embrace {npc} in the middle of the market

effects.log: Two old people weeping by a fish stall. The fishmonger pretends to be busy with a carp.

events.text: {npc} has kept a list: fourteen survivors still alive, scattered over five provinces, and one wooden box rescued from the fire, which {npc} has carried all these years without once opening, because it was not the gatekeeper's place.

choices.text: Open the box together

effects.log: Inside: the sect's register of disciples, the founder's sword tassel, and a bag of the old cook's dried plums, quite hard now.

choices.text: Write to all fourteen survivors

effects.log: Fourteen letters, each one hard to write. Eleven answers come back by winter.

choices.text: Tell {npc} the old sect is finished

effects.log: {npc} goes very quiet, then nods. "Then I will stop searching," {npc} says, "now that I have found you."

events.text: On the anniversary of the fall, {npc} brings you to a farmhouse in the hills. Inside, nine of the fourteen survivors are waiting, grey-haired or grown up, in their old robes, which no longer fit any of them.

choices.text: Read the names from the register

effects.log: Every name, the living and the dead. The nine say "here" for themselves, and for the others too.

choices.text: Ask them whether they want to start again

effects.log: Silence, then a hand goes up, then four, then nine. {npc} is the last, and the first to cry.

choices.text: Share the old cook's plums and remember

effects.log: The plums are terrible, and everyone eats one. You tell stories until dawn.

choices.text: Make {npc} the keeper of whatever comes next

effects.log: {npc} bows, deeper than a gatekeeper's bow. "The gate is open," {npc} says, "whatever gate it is."

events.text: In a pawnshop in a county town, between a rusted halberd and a bird cage, hangs a scorched wooden plaque with gold characters. It is the plaque that once hung over the gate of your fallen sect. The pawnbroker, an elderly woman with an abacus, notices your face and doubles the price.

choices.text: Buy it at her price (200 taels)

effects.log: She wraps it in old cloth and counts the silver twice. You carry it out like a sleeping child.

choices.text: Haggle hard

ok.log: You bargain her down to forty taels and a story. She gives you tea, too.

fail.log: She will not move a single tael, and now she knows you will be back.

choices.text: Ask where the plaque came from

effects.log: "A soldier brought it after some sect war," she says. "He said it was too heavy to burn."

choices.text: Walk out: the past belongs on the pawnbroker's wall

effects.log: You leave it hanging. That night you dream of the old gate.

events.text: Bought or not, the plaque is on your mind every day. The soldier who brought it to the pawnshop, you learn, lives in a village two days south. He kept it from the bonfire after the fall of the sect, his neighbours say, and has never said why.

choices.text: Go and find the soldier

effects.log: The old soldier opens the door, sees your face, and sits down on the step without a word.

choices.text: Leave it: some questions have no good answer

effects.log: You do not go. The question stays with you, smaller each year.

choices.text: Send the soldier a letter of thanks, unsigned

effects.log: A reply comes, unsigned too: "It had a good name. I could not burn a good name."

events.text: The plaque, scorched along one edge, wants a gate to hang on. You could hang it on a farmhouse door, or on a new gate if there will ever be one, or lay it in the ground where the old gate stood, with incense, and let it rest.

choices.text: Hang it over the door of wherever you live now

effects.log: A farmhouse with a sect's name over the door. The neighbours find it pretentious, then rather fine.

choices.text: Bury it at the old gate, with incense

effects.log: You dig at dawn in the ruins. The incense burns straight up, without wind.

choices.text: Ask the old soldier to help you hang it again

effects.log: The old soldier lifts one end, you the other. Neither of you says a word, and both of you weep.

choices.text: Keep it wrapped, waiting for a gate worthy of it

effects.log: You keep it under your bed. Some nights you can feel it there, like a promise.

events.text: Years after the fall, you have a small house, three students who pay in rice, and a patch of bare ground behind the house where you teach at dawn. One of the students asks, innocently, what the sect is called. You realise it has no name.

choices.text: Give it the old sect's name

effects.log: The old name, said aloud again, sounds strange and right. The students repeat it proudly.

choices.text: Give it a new name, something lighter

effects.log: "The Second Dawn," you say. The students like it, and the neighbour's rooster agrees.

choices.text: Tell them a sect needs no name

effects.log: "Then what do we put on the gate?" the youngest asks. "We have no gate," you say. Everyone laughs.

events.text: Word spreads. Seven students now, and a family from the next valley asking to send their twins. You need a proper hall, which costs money, or the old sect's ruins, which cost nothing, and stand on land the enemy still claims.

choices.text: Rent a hall in the village (100 taels)

effects.log: A drafty hall that once stored rice. It smells of rice, still, and it is yours.

choices.text: Rebuild on the old ruins, and dare anyone to object

ok.log: Nobody objects. The old foundation stones are still level. You build on them.

fail.log: The enemy's local elder objects, loudly and with disciples. You withdraw, embarrassed.

choices.text: Teach in the open field until you can afford better

effects.log: Students practise in snow and rain. The ones who stay are worth ten.

events.text: On the tenth anniversary of the new sect, your students, now nineteen, give you a gift wrapped in red paper. Inside is a gate plaque, carved by the oldest student, rough and uneven, with the sect's name.

choices.text: Hang it at once, rough and uneven

effects.log: The plaque goes up crooked, on a gate too small for it. You have never been prouder of anything.

choices.text: Weep, which surprises everyone

effects.log: The students are horrified, then delighted. The oldest is unbearable about it for a month.

choices.text: Notice the old name, written true

effects.log: The carving copies the founder's brushwork exactly. The oldest student studied old rubbings for a year.

choices.text: Notice the new name, and a rooster carved beside it

effects.log: The rooster is anatomically doubtful. It becomes the sect's emblem anyway.

events.text: A rich merchant offers to fund a real mountain gate, carved and lacquered, if the sect will teach his heir. The heir is lazy, charming and hopeless with a sword. Your oldest student, the one who carved the rough plaque, is watching your face very closely.

choices.text: Refuse: the rough plaque stays

effects.log: The merchant is offended, the heir disappointed, the oldest student radiant.

choices.text: Accept, and hang the rough plaque on the new gate

effects.log: A lacquered gate with a crooked wooden plaque. Everyone who passes asks about it.

choices.text: Accept the heir, refuse the gate

effects.log: The heir trains for a year, improves a little, and pays in rice like everyone else.

events.text: You go back, at last, to the mountain where your old sect fell. You expected weeds and ashes. Instead there is a teahouse, very popular, built on the old practice yard by an enterprising family who sells "Battle Tea" and charges extra for the seats by the scorched wall.

choices.text: Sit by the scorched wall and order the Battle Tea

effects.log: It is mediocre tea at an outrageous price. You drink every drop.

choices.text: Tell the owner who you are

effects.log: The owner turns white, then bows, then offers you free tea for life, and a seat with a view.

choices.text: Walk the old paths instead

effects.log: The paths remember your feet. The plum tree by the kitchen is still alive.

events.text: The next time you climb up, you stay for the evening. The teahouse's storyteller tells the tale of the sect's fall every evening, at length, for tips. It is wildly wrong: in this version the old sect master fought nine demons and flew away on a crane. The audience loves it.

choices.text: Stand up and tell the true story

ok.log: The room listens in silence. When you finish, nobody tips the storyteller, and several people tip you.

fail.log: Nobody believes you. The storyteller adds you to the next version, as a ghost.

choices.text: Tip the storyteller, and say nothing

effects.log: The crane gets bigger every night. You find you do not mind.

choices.text: Correct one small detail, privately, with the storyteller

effects.log: "The cook was named Auntie Mei," you say. The next night the storyteller names her, and the audience cheers for Auntie Mei.

events.text: On your next visit the teahouse owner asks if you would let them put up a memorial: a small stone by the scorched wall, with the names, for the travellers who come. The owner's grandfather, it turns out, was a porter who carried rice to the old sect every autumn.

choices.text: Give the owner the names, every one

effects.log: A stone goes up by the wall, with tea cups left in front of it by strangers every morning.

choices.text: Pay for the stone yourself (80 taels)

effects.log: The finest grey stone in the county. The owner refuses the silver twice and then takes it, weeping.

choices.text: Ask them to leave it as it is: a teahouse is a kind of memorial

effects.log: The owner thinks about this, then names the best tea on the menu after the sect instead.

events.text: The Orthodox Alliance council calls on every member sect to send disciples against the "Poison Hollow Cult", a demonic nest in the southern hills. The summons is sealed in gold. Your scouts report that Poison Hollow is a village of herbalists who refused to sell their medicine to the Alliance at half price.

choices.text: Send your disciples as ordered

effects.log: Thirty of your disciples march south under the Alliance banner, uneasy.

choices.text: Go yourself, ahead of the expedition, to see

effects.log: You ride south alone and walk into Poison Hollow at dusk. It smells of mint and drying roots.

choices.text: Refuse, citing a sudden illness among your disciples

effects.log: The Alliance accepts the excuse in writing and remembers it in a separate ledger.

events.text: A year later the expedition finally reaches Poison Hollow. The herbalists have no walls, only drying racks and an old headman, Grandfather Xu, who stands in the road with a basket of ginseng and asks the Alliance's commander what the price of righteousness is this year.

choices.text: Stand between the commander and the village

effects.log: The commander stares at you for a long breath, then calls a halt "to negotiate". Nobody is hurt.

choices.text: Persuade the commander to buy the medicine at a fair price

ok.log: The commander, embarrassed in front of witnesses, signs a fair contract. The expedition goes home with ginseng.

fail.log: The commander laughs. The village is fined and its racks are burned. Nobody is killed, but nobody forgets.

choices.text: Order your own disciples to stand down and watch

effects.log: Your thirty disciples sit on their packs while the Alliance shouts. Grandfather Xu notes their colours.

choices.text: Stay away from the hollow altogether

effects.log: You hear later what happened there, from three different people, in three different ways.

events.text: At the next council, the Alliance celebrates the "cleansing of Poison Hollow" with a banquet and a commemorative poem. The poem is long. Under the table, someone presses a small package into your hand: dried ginseng, and a note from Grandfather Xu.

choices.text: Stand and tell the council what Poison Hollow really is

effects.log: The hall goes cold. Two sects walk out with you. The Alliance never quite trusts you again, and some sects trust you more.

choices.text: Buy your sect's medicine from Poison Hollow from now on

effects.log: Grandfather Xu's ginseng comes up your mountain every autumn. Your disciples heal fast.

choices.text: Applaud the poem with everyone else

effects.log: You applaud. The ginseng is bitter, and you keep it anyway.

events.text: Years later the Alliance summons its sects again, this time against a real demonic band raiding the trade roads. At the council, the commander of the old Poison Hollow expedition rises to speak, sees you, and quietly sits down again.

choices.text: Join the new expedition, with your eyes open

effects.log: You march with the Alliance. This time the enemy is real, and the scouts are yours.

choices.text: Ask that Poison Hollow's herbalists heal the wounded

effects.log: The council is silent. Then the commander, red-faced, seconds the motion.

choices.text: Decline again, without an excuse

effects.log: The Alliance notes it. So do several other sects, with respect.

events.text: The Orthodox Alliance sends an inspector, {npc}, a dry old scholar of the righteous path with ink-stained fingers, to examine whether {sect} is truly orthodox. {npc} has heard that one of your techniques uses "cold qi", which in certain old manuals is a demonic sign.

choices.text: Welcome {npc} and open every hall

effects.log: {npc} reads every manual in your library, slowly, and makes tiny notes in a tiny book.

choices.text: Show {npc} only what you choose

effects.log: {npc} notices the locked doors, and writes down the number of locks.

choices.text: Demonstrate the cold qi technique in person

effects.log: You perform it in the yard. Frost forms on the plum tree. {npc} writes for a very long time.

events.text: The inspection drags into a second year. At last {npc} asks to speak alone. "Your cold qi is in the founding manuals of the Alliance itself," {npc} says, "in an older copy than the one they keep. The Alliance does not know. Should it?"

choices.text: Ask {npc} to tell the Alliance the truth

effects.log: {npc} smiles for the first time. "I was hoping you would say that."

choices.text: Ask {npc} to say nothing, and pass your sect

effects.log: {npc} closes the tiny book. "Then I passed you," {npc} says, "and I will remember that I did."

choices.text: Offer {npc} a place in your library as archivist

ok.log: {npc} thinks a long time, then accepts. "I am too old to inspect," {npc} says, "and you have the better books."
