fail.log: {npc} declines, gently. Inspectors do not change sides; it is the only rule {he} has never broken.

events.text: At the Alliance council, {npc} presents the report. The older manual is read aloud. A dozen orthodox sects discover that their own founders practised "demonic" cold qi, and the council erupts like a kicked hornets' nest.

choices.text: Stand beside {npc} as the storm breaks

effects.log: You stand beside {npc} while the masters shout. By evening, the old manual is officially "orthodox after all".

choices.text: Defend {npc} when a great sect demands a retraction

effects.log: You speak for an inspector who spoke for you. The great sect withdraws, grumbling.

choices.text: Stay silent, safe in the passed report

effects.log: The storm passes over your sect. {npc} glances at you once, across the hall.

choices.text: Laugh out loud at the absurdity

effects.log: The whole hall turns. Then, slowly, old Master Bo of the White Cloud laughs too, and the council ends in laughter.

events.text: Your sect will send you to next year's Alliance youth tournament. Months before it, an Alliance steward visits your room with a jar of good tea and a sentence: the heir of the Heavenly Sword Sect will be champion this year. Everyone knows it, the steward says, except perhaps you.

choices.text: Thank the steward for the tea

effects.log: The steward leaves smiling. You train twice as hard, and sleep badly.

choices.text: Tell the steward you fight to win

effects.log: The steward's smile tightens. "Of course," the steward says. "Everyone does."

choices.text: Report the steward to your sect elder

effects.log: Your elder listens and goes grey. "Fight as you like," the elder says, "and be ready for what comes."

events.text: The tournament final. The Heavenly Sword heir is good, very good, but not better than you, and both of you know it by the tenth exchange. Out of the corner of your eye you see the judges, the steward, and your own elder, all watching your hands.

choices.text: Win, cleanly, in front of everyone

ok.log: Your sword stops at the heir's throat. The hall is silent, then the heir bows to you first.

fail.log: The heir is better than you thought. You lose fairly, which is not what anyone expected either.

choices.text: Lose, convincingly

effects.log: You fall well. The heir knows, and looks at you afterwards with something close to shame.

choices.text: Lower your sword and declare a draw

effects.log: The judges have no rule for this. The whole hall argues for an hour.

events.text: A year later the Heavenly Sword heir comes to your mountain alone and asks for a private bout, with no judges. "I need to know," the heir says, "whether I am the champion or only the heir." The yard is empty, and the gate is shut.

choices.text: Fight properly, and let the bout decide

effects.log: You fight in the empty yard. Whoever wins, both of you walk away friends.

choices.text: Tell the heir about the steward's tea

effects.log: The heir sits on the steps for a long time. The next Alliance tournament has new stewards.

choices.text: Decline: champion is a word, not a person

effects.log: The heir laughs bitterly, and then, slowly, honestly.

events.text: The Heavenly Sword heir becomes master of that great sect, and sends you an invitation: judge the next Alliance youth tournament. In the envelope is a jar of tea, the same brand the steward brought you all those years ago, and a note: "Your turn to choose."

choices.text: Judge, and judge honestly

effects.log: Two heirs lose that year, and a farmer's child wins. The Alliance is furious and the crowd is delighted.

choices.text: Decline: you are not fit to judge

effects.log: The new master writes back that this is exactly why you were asked.

choices.text: Accept, and send the tea back unopened

effects.log: The new master laughs aloud in the council hall, and nobody else understands why.

events.text: The Alliance has put a bounty on a "demonic monster" who haunts the Black Willow Marsh. Your sect is part of the hunt. At the briefing you see the bounty portrait, and know the face: Wen Shu, who left your sect five years ago under a cloud nobody would describe.
events.arc: The Demon Who Was a Disciple

choices.text: Join the hunt, and get there first

effects.log: You push your horse through the marsh paths ahead of the hunters, to find Wen Shu before they do.

choices.text: Ask the elders what really happened five years ago

effects.log: Three elders refuse to say. The fourth, drinking, says: "Wen Shu saw the treasurer's books."

choices.text: Refuse to hunt someone you shared a dormitory with

effects.log: You are excused, coldly. You sit the night out in the dormitory you shared.

events.text: The hunt drags through a year of reeds and false trails. At last you find Wen Shu in a fisherman's hut in the marsh, thin and fierce, practising a technique from no orthodox manual. "I learned it to survive the hunters," Wen Shu says. "The sect taught me everything except how to be thrown away."
events.arc: The Demon Who Was a Disciple

choices.text: Warn Wen Shu that the hunters are a day behind

effects.log: Wen Shu is gone before dawn. You leave the hut exactly as you found it.

choices.text: Persuade Wen Shu to come back and face a hearing

ok.log: Wen Shu agrees, on one condition: the treasurer's books are read aloud too.

fail.log: Wen Shu laughs and walks out into the marsh. You do not follow.

choices.text: Ask about the treasurer's books

effects.log: Wen Shu stares. "So someone finally asked," Wen Shu says, and tells you everything.

events.text: The hunt ends with no monster found. Back at the sect, the treasurer is nervous, the elders are silent, and the Alliance has quietly moved the bounty to a different marsh. You know more than you should.
events.arc: The Demon Who Was a Disciple

choices.text: Bring the treasurer's books to the sect master

effects.log: The sect master reads all night. In the morning the treasurer is gone, and Wen Shu's name is taken off the bounty.

choices.text: Write to Wen Shu, wherever the marsh leads

effects.log: A reply comes in autumn, unsigned, with a dried lotus pressed inside.

choices.text: Keep quiet, and keep your place

effects.log: Your place is safe. The marsh, in your dreams, is not.

events.text: The Heavenly Demon Cult, to which your sect swore loyalty, sends its levy master at the Black Moon. The levy is the same every year: a tenth of your silver, your three best young disciples for a season of service at the Cult's peak, and a proof of loyalty to be named at the time.

choices.text: Pay the silver and send the three best (200 taels)

effects.log: The levy master counts the silver and inspects the three disciples like horses.

choices.text: Send three volunteers instead of the best

effects.log: The levy master notices, and says nothing, which is more frightening than anything.

choices.text: Bargain the levy down

ok.log: The levy master is amused by your nerve. The silver is halved; the disciples are not.

fail.log: The levy master is not amused. The levy is doubled next year, in writing.

events.text: The levy master names this year's proof of loyalty: burn the Green Hall, an orthodox teahouse in the county town where Alliance spies drink. The owner, a cheerful old man called Grandpa Liu, also feeds half the beggars of the town every evening.

choices.text: Burn the teahouse at night, after it closes and empties

effects.log: The Green Hall burns empty. Grandpa Liu stands in the street at dawn with a pot of congee and nowhere to serve it.

choices.text: Warn Grandpa Liu first, then burn it

effects.log: Grandpa Liu carries out the pots, the stools and the beggars' blankets, and watches it burn without a word.

choices.text: Report that the teahouse had burned already, and pay to rebuild it quietly (150 taels)

effects.log: A risky lie, told well. The Green Hall reopens under a new name, with your silver in its rafters.

events.text: The three disciples come back from the Cult's peak changed: stronger, quieter, and with a new tattoo of a black moon on each wrist. One of them brings you a message from the Cult master, delivered in a whisper: "The Cult sees everything, and forgives what it chooses."

choices.text: Ask the three what they saw at the peak

effects.log: They talk in short, careful sentences. You learn the Cult's halls, its rules, and its fears.

choices.text: Ask whether the Cult knows about the teahouse

effects.log: The disciple smiles faintly. "The Cult knows," the disciple says, "and it was amused."

choices.text: Promise the three the next levy will be different

effects.log: The three look at each other. You hope you can keep it.

choices.text: Welcome them back with a feast and no questions

effects.log: The feast is loud. The three eat in silence and sleep for two days.

events.text: The next Black Moon comes round. The levy master arrives again, older, and this time without guards. Over tea, the levy master asks something no levy master asks: how your disciples feel about the Cult. The question sounds like a trap, and also like a real question.

choices.text: Answer honestly: afraid

effects.log: The levy master nods. "Good," the levy master says, and then, after a while, "So am I."

choices.text: Answer like a loyal sect: devoted

effects.log: The levy master writes it down exactly. The levy is not raised this year.

choices.text: Ask the levy master the same question

effects.log: A long silence. The levy master finishes the tea and leaves the silver behind, by accident or not.

events.text: The Cult's Elder of Trials, {npc}, summons you at midnight to a hall lit by one candle. On the table is a black cup. "Your friend in the Western Hall has been speaking with orthodox spies," {npc} says. "Carry this cup to that friend tonight. It is only sleep, of course."

choices.text: Take the cup and bow

effects.log: You carry the cup out with both hands. "Not yet," {npc} calls after you. "When I say."

choices.text: Ask {npc} for proof

effects.log: {npc} raises an eyebrow. "Proof," {npc} says, as if tasting a strange food. "Interesting."

choices.text: Refuse outright

effects.log: {npc} smiles, and lets you go. The smile follows you for weeks.

events.text: The Elder of Trials lets a whole year pass, watching. Then, at the Black Moon, you carry the cup to the Western Hall. Your friend is mending a sandal. The friend sees what you carry, looks at your face, and puts the sandal down very carefully.

choices.text: Pour the cup out on the floor in front of your friend

effects.log: The black liquid soaks into the floorboards. Your friend breathes out for a long time.

choices.text: Warn your friend to run

effects.log: Your friend is over the wall by midnight. You never learn whether the spies were real.

choices.text: Tell your friend everything, and ask the truth

effects.log: "No spies," your friend says. "A test. They tested me with you last spring."

choices.text: Do as {npc} ordered

effects.log: Your friend drinks it without a word, and sleeps. Only sleep, it turns out. You are not sure that matters.

events.text: {npc} summons you again, the same candle, the same table, no cup. "Well," the Elder of Trials says, "you have shown us what you are. The Cult has a use for every kind of disciple. Shall I tell you which kind you are?"

choices.text: "Tell me."

effects.log: "The kind who pours the cup out," {npc} says. "We need those as well. They make good judges." You are promoted.

choices.text: "I am the kind who knows it was a test."

effects.log: {npc} laughs aloud, the only time you ever hear it. "Then you will run the tests now," {npc} says.

choices.text: Say nothing, and wait

effects.log: {npc} studies you, then nods once. You are sent back to your hall, neither raised nor lowered.

choices.text: Ask {npc} whether the Elder of Trials was ever tested

effects.log: {npc} goes very still. "Every year," {npc} says at last. "By the cup you did not pour."

events.text: The Cult has a hundred and eight rules, carved on a black wall, and new members must learn them all. Most are about obedience. Rule forty-seven, however, says: "Do not smile at the Elder of the Iron Hall." Nobody will tell you why, and the Elder of the Iron Hall is walking towards you.

choices.text: Keep a stone face

effects.log: You keep a face like a winter wall. The Elder of the Iron Hall walks past, satisfied.

choices.text: Smile, by accident

effects.log: The Elder stops. Everyone in the corridor freezes. Then the Elder smiles back, horribly, and walks on.

choices.text: Ask the Elder about rule forty-seven directly

effects.log: The Elder looks at you for a long time. "Come to the Iron Hall tonight," the Elder says.

events.text: You learn the story of rule forty-seven at last. Forty years ago the Elder of the Iron Hall, then a young disciple, told a joke at the Cult master's birthday. The Cult master laughed so hard that a rival seized the moment to strike. The joke is now forbidden. So is smiling at its teller.

choices.text: Ask to hear the joke

effects.log: The Elder tells it. It is, genuinely, the funniest thing you have ever heard. You keep a stone face, barely.

choices.text: Keep the story to yourself

effects.log: The rule seems less silly now. Every rule on the wall, you begin to think, has a body buried under it.

choices.text: Spread the story among the new members

effects.log: The new members stop smiling at the Elder, and start pitying the Elder instead. That is worse.

events.text: At the Cult master's next birthday, the hall is tense and silent, as every year. The Elder of the Iron Hall sits alone at the end of the table, old and stiff. The Cult master, unexpectedly, turns and asks whether anyone present can tell a good joke.

choices.text: Tell the forbidden joke

effects.log: The hall goes white. Then the Cult master laughs, alone, long and sad. The Elder of the Iron Hall weeps openly. Rule forty-seven is chiselled off the wall.

choices.text: Tell a harmless joke about a goat

effects.log: Polite laughter. The Cult master nods, disappointed, and the feast goes on.

choices.text: Keep your eyes on your bowl

effects.log: Rule ninety-one: when in doubt, eat. You eat.

choices.text: Smile at the Elder of the Iron Hall, deliberately

effects.log: The Elder sees, and, after forty years, smiles back. Nobody reports either of you.

events.text: You are given the task of re-carving the Cult's black wall, which has weathered badly. Forty-seven is gone now. The Cult master has told you that you may carve one new rule, of your own choosing, in the empty space.

choices.text: "Laugh when the master laughs."

effects.log: The rule is carved. Feasts at the Cult become noticeably less terrifying.

choices.text: "Every rule must say why."

effects.log: The elders are scandalised. The Cult master, after a long look, allows it.

choices.text: Leave the space empty

effects.log: An empty space on a wall of rules. Disciples stand in front of it and think.

events.text: A young disciple of the orthodox White Crane Sect arrives at your gate in the rain and asks to join your demonic sect. The reason given is short: the White Crane elders burned a village to hide a mistake, and the young one carried the torch. The Crane will want their disciple back, or silent.

choices.text: Take the defector in

effects.log: The defector kneels in the rain and is given a dry robe in your colours.

choices.text: Test the defector first: it could be a spy

effects.log: You set three small traps of trust. The defector walks through all three, honestly.

choices.text: Send the defector away

effects.log: The young one walks back down into the rain. You hear later of an unmarked grave by the river road.

events.text: The White Crane sends an envoy: return their disciple and they will forget the matter. Keep the disciple, and the Alliance will hear that your sect is harbouring a criminal. The defector stands behind your chair, very pale.

choices.text: Refuse the envoy: your gate, your rules

effects.log: The envoy leaves furious. Your disciples cheer. Demonic sects are good at refusing.

choices.text: Make the defector tell the village story to the envoy

ok.log: The envoy listens, then leaves without a word. The White Crane stops demanding anything.

fail.log: The envoy calls it lies, and goes to tell the Alliance their own version.

choices.text: Offer to trade: the disciple stays, and you keep the village quiet

effects.log: The envoy agrees, with a face like sour plums. It is blackmail. It works.

events.text: Years later, the defector is one of your best disciples and has never once smiled at the White Crane's name. Then the White Crane is attacked by a cult band, and its new master, a young one, writes to you, of all sects, for help.

choices.text: Send the defector at the head of your disciples

effects.log: The defector saves the White Crane gate, and then walks into the burned village's shrine and kneels for an hour.

choices.text: Send help, but keep the defector home

effects.log: Your disciples go. The defector watches them leave with an unreadable face.

choices.text: Let the White Crane burn

effects.log: You send nothing. The defector says nothing either, and leaves your sect in spring.

events.text: On the same morning, two embassies climb your mountain. The Orthodox Alliance sends a white jade sword and an invitation to join the righteous path. The Heavenly Demon Cult sends a black lacquer box of pills and an invitation to join the true path. Both envoys arrive at the gate at the same moment, and refuse to go in second.

choices.text: Open a second gate, so both can enter first

effects.log: Your disciples break a hole in the side wall in an hour. Both envoys enter first, and both are offended.

choices.text: Receive the Alliance envoy first

effects.log: The Cult envoy waits at the gate with a smile you do not like.

choices.text: Receive the Cult envoy first

effects.log: The Alliance envoy waits at the gate, writing something down.

events.text: A year later both envoys return with written terms. The Alliance's: join, and receive protection, fame and seats at their councils, in exchange for fighting their wars. The Cult's terms: join, and receive techniques, silver and a free hand, in exchange for fighting their wars. Your elders are split down the middle.

choices.text: Keep both gifts and join neither

effects.log: Both envoys go home with nothing. Your sect keeps a jade sword and a box of pills, and two new enemies.

choices.text: Play them against each other for a better deal

ok.log: Each envoy raises the offer twice. You sign nothing and keep the gifts, the silver, and a ten-year promise of peace from both.

fail.log: Both envoys realise what you are doing at the same moment, and leave together.

choices.text: Send both gifts back, with a letter: we are our own side

effects.log: The letters are copied in teahouses across the province. Unaligned sects begin to write to you.

events.text: Years later, an orthodox and a demonic sect go to war across your valley, and both send word: they expect you to remember the gifts. Your disciples look to you. The jade sword hangs on one wall of your hall; the lacquer box sits on the opposite shelf.

choices.text: Hang both on the same wall, and stay out

effects.log: Both sides send angry letters. Neither dares march through your valley.

choices.text: Call the unaligned sects together as a third bloc

effects.log: Seven small sects meet on your mountain. Neither side can afford to offend all seven.

choices.text: Offer your mountain as the place to talk

effects.log: Both sides send envoys. It is the longest dinner you have ever hosted, and the war ends in a month.

events.text: The white jade sword and the black lacquer box still hang in your hall, opposite each other. A young disciple asks you, very seriously, which of them you would have chosen if you had been forced to choose.

choices.text: "The sword. It does not pretend to be medicine."

effects.log: The disciple thinks about this for a week and comes back with three more questions.

choices.text: "The pills. At least they admit they want something."

effects.log: The disciple laughs, then stops, and writes it down.

choices.text: "Neither. That was the whole point."

effects.log: The disciple nods. A generation later, that disciple leads the unaligned bloc.

events.text: An orthodox sect and a demonic cult have bled each other for three years, and both are tired. They agree to talk, but only on neutral ground, and you are the only unaligned sect within a hundred li. The demonic side sends {npc}, a sharp-tongued envoy who arrives early to inspect your table for traps.

choices.text: Let {npc} inspect everything, smiling

effects.log: {npc} taps every bowl and turns over every cushion. You serve tea to the envoy anyway.

choices.text: Give {npc} the same seat as the orthodox envoy, exactly

effects.log: {npc} measures the two chairs with a string. They are the same. {npc} seems almost disappointed.

choices.text: Ask {npc} what peace would be worth to the cult

effects.log: {npc} thinks about it seriously, which is the first good sign.

events.text: The talks drag on for a year. The orthodox envoy is pompous; {npc} is rude. One night, {npc} visits you alone and admits the cult is close to collapse. "If they knew," {npc} says, "they would never sign."

choices.text: Keep {npc}'s secret: you are the neutral ground

effects.log: {npc} watches you a long time, then nods. The next day, the talks move a little faster.

choices.text: Use the secret to press both sides toward a fair deal

ok.log: You never reveal it, but your proposals fit it exactly. Both sides accept a border on the old river.

fail.log: Your proposal is too clever. The orthodox envoy suspects something and walks out for three days.

choices.text: Tell the orthodox envoy, for the greater peace

effects.log: The orthodox side demands surrender. {npc} leaves your mountain that night, without a word.

events.text: The treaty is signed in your hall. The orthodox envoy makes a long speech. {npc} makes a short one, and then, in front of everyone, bows to you, which demonic envoys never do to anyone. The orthodox envoy drops a brush.

choices.text: Invite {npc} to stay on, as your sect's guest

effects.log: {npc} stays a season, insults your tea every day, and teaches your disciples three useful tricks.

choices.text: Make your hall the permanent ground for all talks

effects.log: Your mountain becomes the place where wars come to end. Both sides pay a fee. Both sides pay it promptly.

choices.text: Walk {npc} to the gate

effects.log: At the gate, {npc} turns back. "If my side ever breaks it," {npc} says, "I will tell you first."

choices.text: Bow back, and say nothing

effects.log: It is noticed. In both camps, they say the unaligned host was humble.

events.text: The Black Market Sect has one sacred rule: deliver, never ask. Your first big job is a crate to be carried from the river docks to a mansion in the provincial capital, three days away. Halfway along the road, the crate begins, very quietly, to cry.

choices.text: Keep going: deliver, never ask

effects.log: You deliver the crate to the mansion and are paid. It cried most of the last day.

choices.text: Open the crate

effects.log: Inside is a boy of about eight, in silk, gagged and furious. You leave him with the monks of the nearest temple.

choices.text: Knock on the crate and ask who is inside

effects.log: A small, furious voice gives a magistrate's family name. You turn the cart towards that magistrate's town.

events.text: A year on, the truth is out: the crate held a magistrate's grandson, stolen for ransom by a rival gang that hired your sect as couriers. Now the gang is looking for the courier, and so is the magistrate, for reasons that may be gratitude or may be a cangue.

choices.text: Present yourself at the magistrate's hall

effects.log: The magistrate's grandson points at you and shouts. The magistrate, it turns out, wants to shake your hand.

choices.text: Go to the magistrate and confess what you carried

effects.log: The magistrate listens in cold silence, then uses your testimony to close the gang down. You are spared, barely.

choices.text: Face the rival gang's enforcers when they come for you

ok.log: Three enforcers come; three go home limping. The gang decides the courier is not worth it.

fail.log: They leave you bruised in an alley, with a message for your elders.

choices.text: Lie low in the sect's safehouse for a season

effects.log: You spend a season playing dice with an old fence. The gang gives up looking.

events.text: Your sect's elders summon you. The rule was kept, or broken; the job was finished, or not. Either way the story has spread, and the elders are divided between those who want you thrown out and those who want to know why the magistrate's family is now paying the sect a monthly fee.

choices.text: Explain that the magistrate is now a client, not an enemy

effects.log: The elders look at each other. Elder Zhang, oldest of them, adds a new line under the rule: "unless it cries."

choices.text: Accept a year of copying ledgers as penance

effects.log: You copy ledgers for a year. The other couriers bring you tea.

choices.text: Argue that every rule has a price, and this one was too high

effects.log: Half the elders agree. The sect splits its rule in two: deliver, never ask, but listen.

events.text: Your unorthodox sect lives by a code the orthodox sects mock: never rob the poor, never break a promise, always pay your debts. Now an orthodox sect's treasurer has borrowed a large sum from your sect's elders, under a false name, and refuses to repay it, sure that no court will side with "thieves".

choices.text: Volunteer to collect the debt

effects.log: The elders hand you the contract and a warning: collect it, but do it by the code.

choices.text: Advise the elders to write the debt off

effects.log: The elders look at you as if you had suggested robbing an orphanage.

choices.text: Find out who the treasurer really is first

effects.log: Two days in the archives. The treasurer's real name appears on three other unpaid debts.

events.text: The treasurer receives you in a fine house with a painted gate, flanked by disciples of the righteous path. "A thief," the treasurer says loudly, "demanding silver from an orthodox elder. Who will believe it?"

choices.text: Recite every unpaid debt, with names and dates, in front of the disciples

ok.log: The orthodox disciples stare at their treasurer. The silver is in your hands within the hour.

fail.log: You mix up two dates. The treasurer laughs you out of the house.

choices.text: Offer to take the debt to the orthodox sect master in person

effects.log: The treasurer goes pale. A purse is pressed into your hands at the gate.

choices.text: Leave quietly and tell every money-lender in the province

effects.log: No lender in the province will touch the treasurer's name again.

events.text: A few months later, the orthodox sect master arrives at your sect's gate in person, which nobody has ever seen. The old master has heard the story and come, astonishingly, to apologise, and asks your elders a question: how does a sect of thieves keep its people so honest?

choices.text: Give the answer your elders always gave: "Hunger and shame."

effects.log: The orthodox sect master laughs, and then stops, and writes it down.

choices.text: Say: "We cannot afford not to."

effects.log: The sect master nods slowly. The two sects sign a small trade agreement, the first of its kind.

choices.text: Say nothing and pour the tea

effects.log: Your elders approve of the silence. The orthodox master drinks three cups and goes home thoughtful.

events.text: The orthodox treasurer, ruined and alone, comes to your sect's gate in a patched robe and asks to borrow money. There is nowhere else, the old treasurer says. Every orthodox lender in the province remembers the story, and so does every unorthodox one.

choices.text: Lend it, by the code (100 taels)

effects.log: The old treasurer weeps, signs under a true name, and repays every tael within two years.

choices.text: Refuse, politely

effects.log: The treasurer bows and goes. You watch the patched robe down the road.

choices.text: Give the treasurer work in your sect's counting house

effects.log: The treasurer is the most honest bookkeeper the sect has ever had. Nobody quite knows what to do about that.
